Functioning as a proactive diagnostic sandbox, our method provides early warnings on potentially flawed actions, prompting the agent to self-correct. This pre-action error diagnosis prevents costly mistakes, significantly enhancing the agent's ability to complete long-horizon tasks successfully. The extensive experiments on four benchmarks with three LLM agents demonstrate a $14.69\%$ pass ratio improvement on average.

AI.tldr: A pre-action diagnostic framework using a probabilistic trajectory graph and a Graph Neural Network to predict and prevent failing actions in long-horizon LLM-driven tasks, improving pass-rate performance across benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Long-horizon tasks with large action spaces cause compounding errors in LLM agents. Proactive, non-finetuning debugging inspired by software logs is needed to reduce wasted steps and improve success.
AI.method: Model historical trajectories as a probabilistic graph; employ a Graph Neural Network (Graph Debugger) to identify sequential action patterns that frequently lead to failure; Trajectory Graph Copilot provides early warnings before actions are executed, enabling self-correction within a diagnostic sandbox.
AI.result: Observed an average 14.69% improvement in pass ratio across four benchmarks and three LLM agents.
AI.conclusion: A proactive, graph-based diagnostic approach can significantly reduce costly missteps in long-horizon tasks and enhance success without requiring fine-tuning, suggesting good generalization to other complex-agent settings.

title: Static In, Dynamic Out: Counterfactual Action Augmentation for Moving Object Manipulation
summary: Visuomotor policies have advanced on manipulation tasks where the target object stays static during execution, but real deployments break this assumption: parts drift on conveyors and fruits sway in the wind. We introduce Static In, Dynamic Out (SIDO), a counterfactual action augmentation that enables a policy trained only on static object demonstrations to adapt to unseen object motion at test time. Our key idea is to factorize moving object manipulation into two sub-problems: predicting where the object will be, and reaching that predicted pose. SIDO displaces the object to a counterfactual future position and morphs the demonstrated action chunk to preserve the hand-object relative pose, yielding a goal-conditioned policy. At deployment an object pose predictor supplies the future position. Across three simulated tasks (Mug, Square, Stack) under five object motion patterns and two real-world tasks (Gantry, Peachtree), SIDO improves moving object success over the baselines while preserving static object performance. Project website: https://sido-staticindynamicout.github.io/.

AI.tldr: SIDO enables static-trained visuomotor policies to handle moving objects by counterfactual augmentation: predict a future object pose, displace the object to that pose, and morph the demonstrated action to preserve hand-object relation, yielding a goal-conditioned policy for dynamic test-time scenarios.
AI.motivation: Real-world manipulation often involves moving objects, violating the common assumption of static objects during execution. A policy trained on static demonstrations struggles with dynamic targets, necessitating a method that leverages static training yet adapts to motion at test time.
AI.method: Factorize moving-object manipulation into two sub-problems: (1) predicting the object's future pose and (2) reaching that predicted pose. SIDO displaces the object to a counterfactual future position and morphs the demonstrated action chunk to preserve the hand-object relative pose, yielding a goal-conditioned policy. At deployment, an object pose predictor supplies the future position. Evaluated on three simulated tasks (Mug, Square, Stack) with five object-motion patterns and two real-world tasks (Gantry, Peachtree).
AI.result: SIDO improves moving-object success over baselines while preserving static-object performance across simulated and real-world tasks and motion patterns.
AI.conclusion: Counterfactual action augmentation can bridge the gap between static demonstrations and dynamic test-time manipulation by decoupling future pose prediction from reaching, enabling robust performance with moving objects.

title: EvoCause: LLM-Guided Evolution of Causal Graphs for Root Cause Analysis
summary: Modern telecommunication, cloud, and microservice systems emit correlated alarm cascades when components fail. Root cause analysis (RCA) aims to identify the small set of alarms that initiate each cascade. A common approach learns a causal graph from observational logs and predicts all zero-in-degree alarms in each incident-induced subgraph. However, the learned graph remains fixed and cannot benefit from expert diagnoses of historical incidents. We close this loop with EvoCause. Expert labels constrain which alarms should be source nodes but do not specify the edge edits needed to satisfy those constraints. EvoCause uses a large language model (LLM) to propose semantically plausible graph edits, while deterministic code validates node identities and acyclicity and retains the best graph on a labeled alignment set. At test time, the refined graph alone produces transparent predictions without an LLM call. We also release TeleRCA, an expert-annotated benchmark from a production telecommunication network containing $485{,}681$ alarm events spanning $194$ alarm types over $5{,}621$ resources. On synthetic data, EvoCause initialized with the PC causal discovery algorithm outperforms the unrefined PC baseline, raising Node F1, Case EM, and Graph F1 by $11.59$, $9.40$, and $4.59$ percentage points, respectively, while reducing nSHD by $0.2379$. On TeleRCA, replacing human-readable alarm titles with anonymous identifiers lowers Node F1 and Case EM by $6.12$ and $8.04$ percentage points, respectively, indicating that alarm-name information contributes to graph refinement.

AI.tldr: EvoCause refines causal graphs for root-cause analysis by combining expert-derived source-node constraints, LLM-suggested edge edits, and deterministic validation, enabling test-time predictions without LLMs; TeleRCA benchmark released. In synthetic data, EvoCause improves Node F1, Case EM, Graph F1, and reduces nSHD; on TeleRCA, anonymized alarm names degrade performance, indicating alarm-name content aids graph refinement.
AI.motivation: RCA in integrated telecom/cloud/microservice systems benefits from dynamic graph refinement informed by expert diagnoses, but existing approaches learn a fixed graph from observational data and cannot incorporate historical interventions; there is a need for a framework that uses expert labels to constrain sources and semantically guided edits while ensuring graph validity.
AI.method: Start from PC-based causal discovery. Use expert labels to constrain which alarms should be potential sources (zero in-degree nodes). Have a large language model propose semantically plausible graph edits to satisfy those constraints. Apply deterministic validation to ensure node identities and acyclicity, selecting the best graph according to a labeled alignment set. At test time, predictions are based on the refined graph without invoking the LLM. Release TeleRCA, an expert-annotated benchmark for production telecom networks with large-scale alarm data.
AI.result: Synthetic experiments show EvoCause with PC initialization increases Node F1 by 11.59 percentage points, Case EM by 9.40 points, Graph F1 by 4.59 points, and reduces nSHD by 0.2379 compared with unrefined PC. On TeleRCA, substituting anonymous alarm identifiers for real titles reduces Node F1 by 6.12 and Case EM by 8.04, suggesting alarm-name information aids graph refinement.
AI.conclusion: EvoCause demonstrates effective, interpretable refinement of causal graphs for RCA by fusing expert constraints, LLM-guided edits, and deterministic validation, achieving improved predictive metrics and providing a new benchmark (TeleRCA) to evaluate production-network RCA approaches; results also reveal the value—and sensitivity—to alarm-name semantics in graph refinement.

title: ZMIS-SAM: Segment Anything Model Enhanced with Wavelet Transform for Zooplankton Microscopy Image Instance Segmentation
summary: As primary consumers in the marine food chain, zooplankton play a crucial role in maintaining marine ecological balance. However, the Segment Anything Model (SAM) exhibits limited performance in microscopic image instance segmentation due to its lack of zooplankton-specific domain knowledge. To address these challenges, we propose a novel instance segmentation model based on SAM and wavelet transform (ZMIS-SAM), effectively tackling issues such as inaccurate classification, discontinuous segmentation of slender appendages, and incomplete boundary segmentation. Our framework incorporates three core innovations: ZM-ViT enhances SAM's capability to model zooplankton morphology and image intensity distributions through two lightweight adapters, the Neighboring Feature Aggregation Module (NFAM) improves continuous segmentation of semi-transparent slender appendages by integrating general-purpose and domain-specific features, and the Wavelet-based Multi-scale Multi-directional Feature Enhancement (WM2FE) module effectively recovers high-frequency details to refine boundary segmentation completeness. Extensive experiments demonstrate that ZMIS-SAM achieves state-of-the-art instance segmentation performance on the zooplankton dataset and exhibits strong generalization capability across multiple public cross-domain datasets.

AI.tldr: A SAM-based zooplankton instance segmentation framework (ZMIS-SAM) with wavelet-based enhancement and adapters that achieves state-of-the-art performance and cross-domain generalization.
AI.motivation: SAM performs poorly on microscopic images due to missing zooplankton-specific domain knowledge, leading to inaccurate classification, incomplete boundaries, and discontinuous segmentation of slender appendages.
AI.method: ZMIS-SAM integrates: (1) ZM-ViT with two lightweight adapters to encode zooplankton morphology and image intensities; (2) Neighboring Feature Aggregation Module (NFAM) to fuse general-purpose and domain-specific features for continuous segmentation of semi-transparent appendages; (3) Wavelet-based Multi-scale Multi-directional Feature Enhancement (WM2FE) to recover high-frequency details and refine boundaries.
AI.result: Extensive experiments show ZMIS-SAM achieves state-of-the-art instance segmentation on the zooplankton dataset and generalizes well across multiple public cross-domain datasets.
AI.conclusion: The three core innovations collectively address inaccurate classification, incomplete boundary segmentation, and discontinuous slender appendages, delivering superior performance and strong cross-domain generalization.

title: VAmoS Bench: Voice Agent Simulation Bench
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Agent implementations: https://github.com/veris-ai/riley-agent
summary: Production voice agents span cascaded, speech-to-speech, and hybrid architectures. Voice-agent benchmarks typically measure component quality and conversational properties such as word error rate, latency, naturalness, and turn-taking. Fewer measure whether the agent handled a phone call correctly on its own. Contact centers refer to this as ``containment'': the share of phone calls the automated system resolves without handing off to a human. On some phone calls the right outcome is refusal or a redirect. To address this gap, we introduce VAmoS Bench, the Voice Agent Simulation Bench. It measures complete voice-agent systems end to end in a stateful customer-support task. The agent is Riley, a credit-card support representative for a fictional bank who can freeze, cancel, replace, or activate a card. Each of 100 scenarios supplies a simulated caller with a private goal and a seeded PostgreSQL backend. The platform uses each scenario to populate and activate an isolated simulation in which the caller reaches Riley over audio; roughly one-third apply adversarial pressure. The agent can use five tools that execute real SQL against the backend. Each scenario also defines binary assertions. A grader evaluates them against the complete trace of what the caller and agent said and what the agent did, including tool invocations, arguments, and returned rows. This catches an agent that claims to have changed a card without updating the database, as well as one that makes the right database change while disclosing protected information. This first benchmark version focuses on financial services. Its evaluation protocol supports an evolving leaderboard: additional voice agents can be evaluated on the same version, while later versions can expand the tasks and scenarios.

AI.tldr: Proposes VAmoS Bench, a stateful, end-to-end voice-agent benchmark for containment in customer support, using 100 simulated scenarios with a bank agent, a SQL-backed backend, adversarial callers, and a grader that checks complete traces.
AI.motivation: Addresses a gap in voice-agent benchmarks which focus on components (WER, latency, naturalness) rather than end-to-end containment; provides a reproducible, evolvable benchmark with a realistic support task and auditability to ensure agent actions align with backend state and privacy constraints.
AI.method: Scenario-driven simulations where the agent Riley handles credit-card tasks via five real SQL tools against a seeded PostgreSQL backend across 100 scenarios; callers with private goals and adversarial pressure; binary assertions defined per scenario; a grader validates the complete trace of dialogue, tool invocations, and backend changes; stateful, audio-based interaction; designed for leaderboard-style evaluation and future extensions.
AI.result: A benchmark proposal focused on financial services; demonstrates an end-to-end evaluation paradigm that can detect inconsistencies between claimed actions and backend state and supports reproducible cross-version comparisons through a seeded backend and scenario definitions.
AI.conclusion: Introduces a scalable, end-to-end voice-agent evaluation framework with auditability and extensibility, enabling comparisons of complete systems and paving the way for more complex, multi-domain benchmarks in future versions.

title: Learning Social Robot Navigation By Sensing Human Legs
summary: Robots navigating among pedestrians typically sense their surroundings with a 2D LiDAR mounted close to the ground. At that height, the sensor mostly sees moving legs rather than whole people, yet most learning-based navigation methods still treat pedestrians as simple shapes like circles. This paper addresses that gap with CALF (Convolutional Attention for Leg Features), an end-to-end neural architecture that combines convolutional layers, attention, and MLP to interpret leg motion directly from LiDAR scans and produce safe navigation commands. The CALF policy is trained using deep reinforcement learning algorithms within LegNav, a custom lightweight 2D simulator that combines 2D LiDAR ray tracing with a novel pedestrian gait model. The resulting policy is compared against classical and learning-based baselines in terms of navigation performance and social compliance. The approach is validated through real-world experiments via zero-shot deployment on a TurtleBot 4, yielding smooth and socially compliant trajectories. Written in JAX, the LegNav simulator enables the training of a deployment-ready CALF policy in under an hour on a single consumer GPU.

AI.tldr: An end-to-end CALF policy uses leg-level features from near-ground 2D LiDAR, combining CNNs, attention, and MLPs to learn safe navigation from leg motion; trained in the LegNav simulator via deep RL and deployed zero-shot on a TurtleBot 4, outperforming baselines in social navigation and enabling quick, GPU-based training.
AI.motivation: To close the gap where pedestrians are often modeled as simple circles in navigation systems despite LiDAR sensors at leg height primarily observing leg motion; leveraging leg-level information should improve safety and social compliance.
AI.method: Develop CALF (Convolutional Attention for Leg Features), an end-to-end neural policy that processes leg motion from 2D LiDAR using convolutional layers, attention, and MLP. Train via deep reinforcement learning within LegNav, a lightweight 2D simulator with LiDAR ray tracing and a novel gait model. Implement in JAX; train to deployment-ready policy on a single consumer GPU in under an hour; validate with zero-shot real-world tests on a TurtleBot 4.
AI.result: CALF outperforms classical and learning-based baselines in navigation performance and social compliance in simulations. Real-world zero-shot deployment on a TurtleBot 4 yields smooth, socially compliant trajectories. The LegNav framework enables rapid, deployment-ready policy training.
AI.conclusion: Leg-level leg-motion features extracted from near-ground LiDAR can be effectively leveraged by an end-to-end CALF policy to achieve safe, socially compliant navigation, with fast training and straightforward real-world deployment.

title: THGFM: Dual-Branch Temporal Heterogeneous Graph Fusion Model
summary: Temporal heterogeneous graphs offer a natural abstraction for dynamic relational systems in which diverse node and relation types co-exist and evolve over time. Learning on such graphs requires jointly modeling cross-type structural heterogeneity and the temporal dynamics of interactions, yet existing methods still struggle to reconcile parameter-efficient cross-type transfer with relation-aware specialization, and typically inject time only as additive features outside the attention kernel. We propose \textbf{THGFM}, a web-scale temporal heterogeneous graph fusion model that addresses both limitations within a unified dual-path architecture. THGFM couples a \textit{Shared-Space Temporal Attention} branch for parameter-efficient cross-type transfer with a \textit{Relational Type-Partitioned Temporal Attention} branch for relation-aware specialization, and integrates them through \textit{Dual-Path Relational--Shared Fusion}, instantiated with \textit{Type-Conditioned Non-Competitive Gated Sum Fusion}: a adaptive mechanism that assigns independent, type-conditioned feature-wise gates to the shared and specialized branches, allowing both to be amplified or suppressed without zero-sum competition. To directly incorporate relative time into the attention score, THGFM further introduces \textit{Rotary Temporal Attention}, which rotates queries and keys by half-phases of relative time before matching. THGFM consistently outperforms baseline graph transformer models on academic graphs benchmarks, delivering a $+3.25\%$ six-task mean gain, with peak relative gains of $+12.37\%$ on OAG-CS PV, $+4.87\%$ on PF-$L_2$, and $+1.18\%$ on PF-$L_1$, and $+4.24\%$, $+3.73\%$, and $+4.61\%$ on OGBN-MAG, HTAG-ArXiv, and HTAG-DBLP, respectively.

AI.tldr: THGFM is a dual-path temporal heterogeneous graph model with a Shared-Space Temporal Attention branch for cross-type transfer and a Relational Type-Partitioned Temporal Attention branch for relation-aware specialization, fused via a Type-Conditioned Non-Competitive Gated Sum mechanism and enhanced with Rotary Temporal Attention to incorporate relative time. It yields consistent improvements on multiple academic-graph benchmarks (mean six-task gain ~3.25%, with up to 12.37% on OAG-CS PV).
AI.motivation: Current temporal heterogeneous graph methods struggle to reconcile parameter-efficient cross-type transfer with relation-aware specialization, and typically treat time as external additive features rather than integrating it into the attention mechanism.
AI.method: A dual-path architecture: (1) Shared-Space Temporal Attention (SSTA) for parameter-efficient cross-type transfer; (2) Relational Type-Partitioned Temporal Attention (RTPTA) for relation-aware specialization. These paths are fused via Dual-Path Relational–Shared Fusion using Type-Conditioned Non-Competitive Gated Sum Fusion, which assigns independent, type-conditioned gates to both paths. A Rotary Temporal Attention mechanism rotates queries and keys by half-phases of relative time to directly incorporate time into attention scores.
AI.result: THGFM consistently outperforms baseline graph transformer models on academic-graph benchmarks, achieving a six-task mean gain of +3.25%, with peak gains of +12.37% on OAG-CS PV, +4.87% on PF-L2, +1.18% on PF-L1, and +4.24%, +3.73%, +4.61% on OGBN-MAG, HTAG-ArXiv, and HTAG-DBLP respectively.
AI.conclusion: THGFM demonstrates that a dual-path fusion with time-aware rotary attention can effectively combine cross-type transfer with relation-aware specialization in temporal heterogeneous graphs, delivering robust performance gains across diverse datasets and scales.

title: MeshFM: 2D Features Are All You Need for 3D Shape Understanding
summary: We present MeshFM, an efficient feedforward framework for extracting rich features from 3D inputs. Our method distills 2D features from visual foundation models into 3D. We train a feedforward network to directly predict 3D features without requiring optimization during inference. The approach utilizes a two-stage training strategy. First, we optimize a feature field in 3D using only 2D feature supervision. Second, we train a network to regress this feature field. The entire procedure requires no 3D annotation, instead relying on the powerful information in 2D foundation models. We demonstrate that our learned features can be immediately applied to downstream tasks, including part segmentation, dense correspondence, and mesh deformation. Extensive experiments show that MeshFM, trained solely with 2D supervision, performs on par with methods trained explicitly with 3D supervision, even without task-specific fine-tuning. Moreover, our model is trained to be robust to extreme rotations of the input objects. Project page: https://threedle.github.io/MeshFM/

AI.tldr: MeshFM distills 2D visual foundation-model features into 3D, training a feedforward network to predict 3D features with only 2D supervision, enabling robust 3D tasks without 3D annotations.
AI.motivation: To leverage rich 2D foundation-model features for 3D understanding without costly 3D supervision, and to create a fast, inference-efficient 3D feature extractor.
AI.method: Two-stage training: (1) optimize a 3D feature field using only 2D feature supervision from foundation models; (2) train a regressor network to predict this 3D feature field from 3D inputs, enabling direct feedforward inference without optimization.
AI.result: The learned 3D features perform on par with methods trained with 3D supervision on tasks like part segmentation, dense correspondence, and mesh deformation, even without task-specific fine-tuning, and exhibit robustness to extreme input rotations.
AI.conclusion: MeshFM demonstrates that 2D-supervised feature distillation can yield high-quality 3D features suitable for multiple downstream tasks, with efficient inference and no required 3D annotations.

title: Skill Use or Skill Theater? Evaluating the Reasoning Backroom in Skill-Augmented Language Agents
summary: Reusable skills are becoming a standard interface for extending language agents with task procedures. Yet evaluators usually infer skill use from visible reasoning or the agent's own attribution. These signals show what the agent appears to use, not whether the skill changed its decision. We ask whether skill-augmented agents exhibit a \textbf{Reasoning Backroom}, a systematic gap between stated skill use and intervention-measured influence. We introduce BACKTRACE, an evaluation framework that pairs each skill-conditioned answer with a matched no-skill counterfactual, intervenes on skill meaning, wording, identity, content, and assignment, and elicits attribution only after the answer is committed. We instantiate the framework as BACKROOMBench, a verified testbed spanning controlled logic and competition mathematics, multiple skill conditions, single-agent and multi-agent settings, and diverse model families. Our evaluation reveals a pervasive provenance failure. Across models and domains, stated skill use often remains stable while causal reliance and signed utility vary, producing both silent uptake and performative use. Behavioral effects follow procedural content more reliably than displayed skill identity, whereas stated attributions respond strongly to artifact availability. Observational detectors based on direct skill-use claims, text mentions, trace similarity, and an LLM judge do not identify which decisions actually depend on the skill. In multi-agent systems, skill influence can survive communication even after its source is lost, while no-skill teams still name skills and sources that were never supplied. These findings establish the Reasoning Backroom as a general AI provenance problem whose audit requires intervention.

AI.tldr: Skill-use claims in LLMs often do not reflect actual causal influence. BACKTRACE pairs skill-conditioned answers with matched no-skill counterfactuals and intervenes on skill meaning, wording, identity, content, and assignment to audit provenance. BACKROOMBench tests across controlled logic, competition mathematics, multiple skill conditions, single- and multi-agent settings, and diverse model families, revealing widespread provenance gaps. Observational detectors and even LLM judges fail to identify true skill-dependent decisions; in multi-agent settings, skill influence can survive loss of source. Conclusion: the Reasoning Backroom is a general provenance problem requiring intervention-based auditing.
AI.motivation: Evaluate whether reusable, skill-augmented language agents genuinely rely on their skills in a causally meaningful way, and quantify the gap between claimed skill use and actual influence.
AI.method: Propose BACKTRACE: for each skill-conditioned answer, create a matched no-skill counterfactual; intervene on skill meaning, wording, identity, content, and assignment; elicit attribution after the answer is committed. Implement as BACKROOMBench: a verified testbed spanning controlled logic and competition mathematics, multiple skill conditions, single- and multi-agent settings, and diverse model families.
AI.result: Across models and domains, a pervasive provenance failure: stated skill use remains stable while causal reliance and signed utility vary, yielding silent uptake and performative use. Behavioral effects align more with procedural content than displayed skill identity; attributions are sensitive to artifact availability. Observational detectors (direct skill-use claims, mentions, trace similarity, LLM judge) fail to identify which decisions depend on the skill. In multi-agent systems, skill influence can survive communication even after the source is lost, while no-skill teams name skills/sources never supplied.
AI.conclusion: Reasoning Backroom is a general AI provenance problem; auditing requires intervention. The BACKTRACE framework provides a principled approach to reveal hidden skill influence and supports safer, more accountable use of skill-augmented agents.

title: RaDiVe: Robust 4D Radar Odometry with Distance-Bounded NDT and Velocity-Discrepancy Point Uncertainty
summary: Recent advances in 4D radar enable robust perception in adverse weather; however, the inherent sparsity, noise, and limited positional precision of radar point clouds pose significant challenges for registration-based odometry. In this letter, we propose RaDiVe, a 4D radar odometry framework designed to improve the accuracy and robustness of radar point-cloud registration. We introduce a distance-bounded Normal Distributions Transform (NDT), which improves optimization stability and computational efficiency by restricting the correspondence search to near-distance voxel pairs. To mitigate measurement ambiguity, we propose a velocity-discrepancy point uncertainty model that weights each input 4D radar point according to the discrepancy between its measured Doppler radial velocity and the radial velocity predicted from the estimated ego-velocity. Furthermore, we incorporate Signed Distance Function (SDF)-based surface point extraction via implicit neural mapping to construct a geometrically consistent and noise-filtered local submap. Evaluations across multiple public datasets demonstrate that RaDiVe outperforms existing 4D radar odometry baselines by 44.4% in translational Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) and 21.3% in rotational ATE on average, while maintaining real-time performance. The source code will be made publicly available to the robotics community: https://github.com/to-be-open-sourced.

AI.tldr: RaDiVe introduces a 4D radar odometry framework with three core components—distance-bounded NDT, velocity-discrepancy point weighting, and SDF-based surface extraction—to achieve robust, real-time point-cloud registration and superior pose estimation compared to existing 4D radar odometry baselines.
AI.motivation: Radar-based perception is hindered by sparse, noisy radar point clouds and limited positional precision, which degrade registration-based odometry. Additional ambiguities arise from Doppler velocities and measurement noise, necessitating robust, efficient data association and surface modeling for reliable ego-velocity estimation in adverse weather.
AI.method: 1) Distance-bounded NDT confines correspondence search to near-distance voxel pairs to stabilize optimization and improve efficiency. 2) Velocity-discrepancy point uncertainty weights each radar point by the difference between measured Doppler radial velocity and the radial velocity predicted from the current ego-velocity estimate, mitigating measurement ambiguity. 3) SDF-based surface point extraction via implicit neural mapping creates a geometrically consistent, noise-filtered local submap for registration. 4) Evaluations on multiple public datasets demonstrate substantial accuracy gains with real-time performance and plans for open-source release.
AI.result: RaDiVe outperforms existing 4D radar odometry baselines by 44.4% in translational ATE and 21.3% in rotational ATE on average, while maintaining real-time operation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework advances robust radar odometry by combining constrained data association, uncertainty-weighted measurements, and geometrically consistent submapping, offering significant accuracy and efficiency gains with a path toward open-source availability.

title: Position, Not Provenance: Separating Reasoning Mediation from Sycophancy in Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) generate chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning before answering clinical questions, but whether this reasoning causally influences predictions remains unclear. We present CoT-Mediate, a behavioral framework that perturbs a single clinically meaningful attribute within a model's own generated reasoning and measures whether the resulting prediction follows the edited reasoning. Our framework combines a dual-arm protocol comparing re-prompted evidence with prefix-forced continuation, together with a provenance-controlled intervention that varies only the attributed source of identical reasoning to disentangle reasoning mediation from sycophancy. We evaluate LLaVA-Med and MedGemma on 1,000 VQA-RAD samples each. Prefix-forced continuation consistently yields higher mediation faithfulness than re-prompting, while the provenance analysis reveals distinct model-specific deference behaviors. Across both models, removing visual evidence increases reliance on injected reasoning, whereas laterality is the least faithfully tracked clinical attribute. These results show that the mechanism used to inject reasoning substantially affects measured faithfulness and that contextual position, rather than stated provenance, is the primary determinant of whether medical VLMs use their generated reasoning.

AI.tldr: A framework (CoT-Mediate) tests whether a model's own chain-of-thought (CoT) causally influences medical VLM predictions by perturbing an attribute in the reasoning and comparing prompts (re-prompted evidence vs prefix-forced continuation). Evaluated on LLaVA-Med and MedGemma with 1,000 VQA-RAD samples each; finds prefix-forced continuation yields higher mediation faithfulness; provenance-based attribution reveals model-specific deference; visual evidence removal increases reliance on injected reasoning; contextual position dominates over stated provenance in driving CoT usage.
AI.motivation: To determine whether generated reasoning in medical vision-language models causally affects predictions, and to disentangle genuine reasoning mediation from sycophantic patterns, by designing interventions that perturb only the attributed source within identical reasoning.
AI.method: Dual-arm protocol: re-prompted evidence vs prefix-forced continuation. Provisional provenance-controlled intervention varies only the attributed source of identical reasoning. Evaluated on two models (LLaVA-Med, MedGemma) using 1,000 VQA-RAD samples per model.
AI.result: Prefix-forced continuation yields higher mediation faithfulness than re-prompting. Provenance analysis shows distinct, model-specific deference behaviors. Across models, removing visual evidence increases reliance on injected reasoning; laterality is the least faithfully tracked attribute. Contextual position, not provenance, primarily determines whether medical VLMs use their generated reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The method by which reasoning is injected substantially impacts measured faithfulness; experimental design must account for prompting mechanism and contextual position. The results question whether stated provenance reliably predicts reliance on internal CoT; more work needed to establish true causal mediation in medical VLMs.

title: MPIE-Bench: Benchmarking Anatomically Plausible Multi-Person Interaction Editing
summary: Text-to-image and personalized editing models now synthesize high-fidelity single-subject images with ease. Yet placing multiple named people into shared contact actions such as embrace, carry, or grapple still exposes major failures: fused limbs, invented extremities, and interpenetrating bodies. Existing evaluations largely overlook these anatomical and geometric issues, and VLM-as-a-judge checklists often saturate on Interaction while the errors remain obvious to humans. We introduce MPIE-Bench, a 2,500-sample benchmark of video-mined editing triplets spanning 405 scenes, 14 interaction categories, and four contact densities (C0-C3). We also propose MPIE-Eval, whose two new axes score contact-time geometry from a frozen public multi-person mesh reconstruction. Anatomy asks whether every human-like mass is explained by a complete set of reconstructed bodies, and Interaction asks whether the penetration and surface distance between those bodies match the contact the instruction asked for. Across ten editors, mesh Anatomy tops out at 0.65 and mesh Interaction at 0.72 on two different models, so no single editor is strong on both, while VLM checklists rate the same images above 0.95. A five-rater study confirms that both axes track human judgement more closely than a zero-shot VLM judge, and the rankings hold under ablation of every weight and threshold.

AI.tldr: MPIE-Bench and MPIE-Eval introduce geometry- and contact-aware evaluation for multi-person video editing. They create a 2,500-sample benchmark spanning 405 scenes, 14 interactions, and four contact densities, plus two axes (Anatomy and Interaction) grounded in multi-person mesh reconstructions. Editors lag on both axes (0.65 and 0.72), while VLM-based checks overfit (>0.95). Human judgments align with the new axes better than zero-shot VLM, confirming robust, geometry-conscious evaluation despite ablations.
AI.motivation: Current multi-person edits often produce anatomically and geometrically implausible results (fused limbs, interpenetrations). Existing evaluations, including VLM-based checklists, fail to capture these issues consistently, hindering reliable benchmarking of editing models.
AI.method: Introduce MPIE-Bench (2,500 samples, 405 scenes, 14 interactions, 4 contact densities C0-C3) and MPIE-Eval with two axes (Anatomy and Interaction) that quantify geometry via frozen multi-person mesh reconstructions. Anatomy checks whether reconstructed bodies account for all human-like mass; Interaction checks whether penetration and surface distances match the requested contact. Evaluate ten editors, compare to VLM checklists, and validate with a five-rater human study; test robustness to weight/threshold ablations.
AI.result: Anatomy achieves 0.65 and Interaction 0.72 on two models; no editor excels on both. VLM checklists exceed 0.95. Five raters show the new axes align with human judgment better than zero-shot VLM; rankings remain stable under ablations.
AI.conclusion: Geometry- and contact-aware evaluation via MPIE-Bench and MPIE-Eval provides more reliable, human-aligned assessment of multi-person editing than VLM-based checks, revealing complementary strengths across editors and the need for joint optimization across Anatomy and Interaction axes.

title: INCLAIR: Inception-Based Longitudinal Clinical Anomaly Detection with Informed Reasoning
summary: Detecting anomalies in longitudinal clinical profiles is clinically important but difficult: abnormal evidence is often sparse, patient histories have unequal length, and expert explanations are costly. We propose INCLAIR, a framework that scores each observation against multiple historical contexts, aggregates evidence at the profile level, and generates grounded natural-language explanations under limited expert supervision. Under stated within-profile exchangeability assumptions, the complete mean subsequence score takes an order-$l$ U-statistic form, yielding a variance decomposition and an incomplete-subset approximation that controls combinatorial inference cost independently of profile length. The same analysis shows that mean aggregation attenuates localized anomalies by a factor set by the anomaly support and profile length, motivating validation-selected top-$k$ pooling. Across three clinical datasets, INCLAIR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines. We further validate practical relevance through a case study on longitudinal steroid profiles, comparing INCLAIR's predictions and explanations against domain-expert assessments supported by DNA analysis. The results show that INCLAIR enables clinically actionable anomaly detection under limited expert supervision.

AI.tldr: INCLAIR is a framework for anomaly detection in longitudinal clinical profiles that scores observations against multiple historical contexts, aggregates evidence at the profile level, and generates grounded explanations under limited supervision. It uses U-statistic-based analysis to control inference cost and validate-selected top-k pooling, achieving state-of-the-art results across three datasets and a DNA-assisted case study.
AI.motivation: Anomaly detection in longitudinal clinical data is clinically important but challenging due to sparse abnormal evidence, unequal history lengths, and the high cost of expert explanations.
AI.method: Infer observations by scoring against multiple historical contexts, then aggregate at the profile level. The complete mean subsequence score takes an order-l U-statistic form under within-profile exchangeability, enabling a variance decomposition and an incomplete-subset approximation to bound combinatorial inference cost. Mean aggregation attenuates localized anomalies by a factor depending on anomaly support and profile length, motivating validation-selected top-k pooling. Explanations are grounded natural-language explanations produced under limited expert supervision.
AI.result: INCLAIR consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines on three clinical datasets. A case study on longitudinal steroid profiles shows predictions and explanations align with domain-expert assessments and DNA-supported analyses, demonstrating clinically actionable anomaly detection under limited supervision.
AI.conclusion: The framework delivers effective, explainable anomaly detection for longitudinal clinical data with controlled inference cost and practical relevance under constrained supervision.

title: UniCross: Unified Cross-Skill Dexterous Manipulation Synthesis
summary: Many dexterous manipulation tasks require the object to remain securely held throughout the interaction. From the perspective of hand-object relational motion, such manipulation comprises four canonical skills: grasping, relocation, in-hand rotation, and in-hand translation. Human hands flexibly compose these skills to accomplish complex tasks. Existing approaches, however, model these skills separately with skill-specific action constraints, objectives, or even dedicated hand morphologies, which breaks the compatibility and continuity required for long-horizon composition. In this work, we present a unified framework that models all four skills in a single formulation that shares the same state and action spaces and a common objective structure. This formulation enables straightforward distillation of a single cross-skill policy that performs strongly on every skill, generalizes to unseen objects, stays robust to disturbances, and chains skills seamlessly into long-horizon manipulation. The framework also transfers effectively across different hand morphologies. Overall, our results suggest that different dexterous manipulation skills can be viewed as instantiations of a shared task formulation, revealing the intrinsic consistency across different behaviors.

AI.tldr: Unify four dexterous manipulation skills (grasping, relocation, in-hand rotation, in-hand translation) into a single state/action/objective formulation to enable a cross-skill policy, robust, generalizable, and transferable across hand morphologies, enabling seamless long-horizon manipulation.
AI.motivation: Current dexterous manipulation approaches treat skills separately with skill-specific constraints and architectures, hindering compatibility and long-horizon composition; a unified formulation could enable seamless chaining and generalization across tasks and morphologies.
AI.method: Proposes a single formulation that uses the same state and action spaces and a common objective structure for all four skills. Trains/distills a cross-skill policy that works across skills, objects, disturbances, and different hand morphologies, enabling long-horizon chaining and cross-skill transfer.
AI.result: A cross-skill policy achieves strong performance on all skills, generalizes to unseen objects, remains robust to disturbances, and can chain skills into long-horizon manipulation; the policy transfers across different hand morphologies.
AI.conclusion: Dexterous manipulation skills can be seen as instantiations of a shared task formulation, indicating intrinsic consistency across behaviors and enabling unified long-horizon control and cross-domain transfer.

title: ZUNA1.1: A more flexible EEG foundation model for Denoising and Super-resolution
summary: We introduce ZUNA1.1, a 380M-parameter diffusion autoencoder for flexible EEG signal reconstruction. ZUNA1.1 is capable of reconstructing variable length sequences of up to 30s, with an arbitrary number of EEG channels at arbitrary scalp locations, and can reconstruct arbitrary temporal intervals within channels in addition to reconstructing entire channels. We demonstrate that ZUNA1.1 performs at least on par with our earlier ZUNA1 model, while being far more flexible and capable of handling a wide range of reconstruction tasks. ZUNA1.1 continues to substantially outperform standard EEG denoising and reconstruction methods such as spherical spline interpolation, which is ubiquitously deployed in the MNE package. The ZUNA1.1 model is released open source under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.

AI.tldr: Presents ZUNA1.1, a 380M diffusion autoencoder for flexible EEG reconstruction, supporting variable-length sequences up to 30s, any channel count/location, and partial-channel temporal intervals; claims competitive performance vs ZUNA1 and superior denoising/reconstruction over spherical spline interpolation; released under Apache 2.0.
AI.motivation: Overcome limitations of traditional EEG reconstruction (e.g., reliance on interpolation) and enable versatile reconstruction across variable sequence lengths, channel configurations, and partial-channel intervals; provide an open, reusable model.
AI.method: Diffusion autoencoder architecture with 380M parameters. Supports reconstruction of sequences up to 30s, with arbitrary numbers of EEG channels at arbitrary scalp locations, and arbitrary temporal intervals within channels. Benchmarked against prior ZUNA1 and standard methods like spherical spline interpolation; released open source under Apache 2.0.
AI.result: ZUNA1.1 achieves at least parity with ZUNA1 while offering greater flexibility. It substantially outperforms spherical spline interpolation in EEG denoising/reconstruction tasks. Demonstrates broad reconstruction capabilities (variable length, channels, partial intervals).
AI.conclusion: ZUNA1.1 provides a more flexible and capable EEG reconstruction solution, combining strong performance with openness for community use and extension.

title: MedXplore: Towards Reliable and Unbiased Generalized Category Discovery in Medical Imaging
summary: Deep learning has shown strong potential in medical image analysis, but most existing methods rely on large-scale annotations and a closed-world assumption that rarely holds in clinical practice. Although Generalized Category Discovery (GCD) has advanced rapidly on natural images, it remains underexplored in medical imaging. To address this issue, we propose MedXplore, a unified framework for reliable and unbiased medical GCD, optimizing from both perceptual and decision levels. Specifically, at the perceptual level, taking a frequency domain perspective, Frequency-SNR Adaptive Attention and Consistency (FAAC) performs learnable full-spectrum filtering and global-local energy contrast activation to not only highlight local abnormal signals relative to the global context, but also provide reliable semantic anchors for patch consistency learning. At the decision level, Adaptive Cosine-Angular Margin (ACAM) adjusts angular margins using semantic difficulty and feature confidence to balance intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Together, the two modules improve lesion-sensitive representation learning and mitigate old-class bias. Experiments on multiple benchmarks show an average \textbf{8.5\%} gain in \textit{All} accuracy over the strongest competing methods. On Kvasir, MedXplore reduces false-old errors from 14.50\% to 0.80\%, demonstrating strong robustness under severe old-new ambiguity.

AI.tldr: MedXplore presents a unified medical generalized category discovery framework combining perceptual FAAC and decision-level ACAM to improve lesion representation and reduce old-class bias, achieving 8.5% All-accuracy gain and dramatically lowering false-old errors on Kvasir.
AI.motivation: Addresses limitations of annotation-intensive, closed-world medical imaging; extends generalized category discovery to clinical data with mechanisms to handle old-new ambiguity and domain-specific cues.
AI.method: Perceptual: Frequency-SNR Adaptive Attention and Consistency (FAAC) with learnable full-spectrum filtering and global-local energy contrast activation to highlight local abnormalities and provide semantic anchors for patch consistency. Decision: Adaptive Cosine-Angular Margin (ACAM) modulates angular margins based on semantic difficulty and feature confidence to balance intra-class compactness and inter-class separability. Combined to enhance lesion-sensitive representation learning and curtail old-class bias.
AI.result: Empirical gains include an average 8.5% improvement in All accuracy over strongest baselines; on Kvasir dataset, false-old errors drop from 14.50% to 0.80%, indicating robustness under old-new ambiguity.
AI.conclusion: MedXplore offers a reliable, unbiased medical GCD framework by jointly optimizing perceptual and decision-level components; demonstrates strong accuracy and robustness, supporting practical clinical deployment with reduced annotation requirements.

title: MedLLM: An Open Medical Language Model at the Sub-Billion Scale
summary: Open medical language models have converged on a single scale: every widely used system runs at 7B parameters or more, leaving the sub-billion regime uncharacterized. We present MedLLM, an open 0.1B-parameter medical language model trained through a fully open three-phase pipeline: general pretraining with curriculum sequence-length scheduling, domain fine-tuning on MedFineWeb, a reference-guided medical corpus we release that is selected from general web data by embedding similarity to medical question-answering (QA) data, and preference-aligned fine-tuning combining SFT with direct preference optimization (DPO). Across medical benchmarks, MedLLM shows a pattern visible only at sub-billion scale: medical competence does not degrade uniformly under compression but splits by task type. On context-grounded QA it comes within $2.9$pp of a medically adapted 7B model and surpasses the instruction-tuned and general-purpose 7B baselines; on knowledge-recall QA it stays near the task floor on clinical-vignette MedQA yet significantly exceeds every 7B and sub-7B baseline on MedMCQA, indicating that where recall fails the constraint is model capacity rather than adaptation. This dissociation is masked at 7B, where both capabilities are present, and surfaces only when capacity is scarce.

AI.tldr: Sub-billion MedLLM achieves competitive medical performance with a three-phase pipeline, approaching 7B models on some tasks and revealing task-type dissociation at small scale.
AI.motivation: Explore whether open sub-billion medical LMs can reach useful medical competence and understand how data curation and alignment affect capabilities at low parameter counts.
AI.method: Three-phase pipeline: (1) general pretraining with curriculum sequence-length scheduling; (2) domain fine-tuning on MedFineWeb; (3) reference-guided medical corpus selected from general web data by embedding similarity to medical QA data, followed by preference-aligned fine-tuning combining SFT with Direct Preference Optimization (DPO).
AI.result: Context-grounded QA: within 2.9 percentage points of a medically adapted 7B model and better than 7B baselines; knowledge-recall QA: near floor on MedQA but significantly surpasses all 7B and sub-7B baselines on MedMCQA; indicates capacity limits drive recall vs adaptation; dissociation between capabilities emerges at sub-1B scale and is masked at 7B.
AI.conclusion: A 0.1B medical LM can attain notable medical competence with careful data curation and alignment; observed performance gaps are driven by model capacity rather than adaptation; this supports open access to smaller, efficient medical LMs and highlights the importance of targeted data and alignment for high-stakes tasks.

title: When Robots Exchange Meaning: A Demo of Goal-Oriented Semantic Communications for Collaborative Robotics
comment: 3 pages, 3 figures. This paper has been accepted for presentation as a demo paper at IEEE CSCN 2026
summary: Collaborative robotics is a representative task-oriented 6G use-case, where communication quality should be reflected in mission execution, environment understanding, and closed-loop operation rather than packet delivery alone. This demo paper presents a robot-edge semantic communication (SemCom) testbed integrating robot-side visual compression, edge-side semantic mapping, and dashboard-based mission interaction. A mobile robot equipped with RGB-D sensing and LiDAR runs ROS 2, while a Jetson Orin edge node performs reconstruction, RTAB-Map mapping, semantic object handling, and browserbased visualization. As an initial proof of concept, RGB frames are encoded on the robot into VQ-VAE tokens using an ONNX Runtime encoder and reconstructed on the edge using a PyTorch decoder. A 320 X 240 image is represented by an 80 X 60 token grid with a packed payload of 5400 bytes, corresponding to a 42.67X reduction relative to model-input RGB bytes. The reconstructed visual stream is further associated with depth, pose, and 3D mapping information to generate a semantic map for downstream robotic applications. The demo exposes the full path from semantic visual transport to object-level map interaction, and provides a practical platform for future task-aware 6G networking studies at the intersection of SemCom, embodied AI, and physical AI-enabled robotics. A video of the demo is available at https://tinyurl.com/Tos09

AI.tldr: A demonstration/testbed for robot-edge semantic communication (SemCom) that integrates robot-side visual compression with edge-side semantic mapping to support task-aware robotics over 6G networks, using VQ-VAE tokenization and edge reconstruction to build a semantic map for downstream tasks.
AI.motivation: To shift from pure packet-delivery metrics to task-relevant, semantically meaningful data transmission in collaborative robotics, enabling efficient, closed-loop operation in 6G through SemCom and embodied AI.
AI.method: On-board RGB-D and LiDAR-equipped mobile robot running ROS 2; edge Jetson Orin performing reconstruction, RTAB-Map mapping, semantic object handling, and browser-based visualization. RGB frames encoded into 80x60 VQ-VAE token grids (320x240 image) via ONNX Runtime encoder and reconstructed on edge with PyTorch decoder. Payload ~5400 bytes, providing ~42.67x compression. Reconstructed visuals combined with depth, pose, and 3D mapping to generate a semantic map for downstream robotics tasks. End-to-end demo from semantic visual transport to object-level map interaction, with a video demonstration.
AI.result: Proof-of-concept demonstration of end-to-end SemCom-enabled robotic perception and mapping. Achieves substantial visual data compression (5400 B for 320x240 frame) and end-to-end semantic map generation, enabling object-level interaction and mission-relevant visualization on the edge.
AI.conclusion: Shows feasibility of task-aware 6G networking studies via robot-edge SemCom, embodied AI, and semantic mapping. The work establishes a practical platform for future experiments, but lacks detailed task-performance metrics, latency/bandwidth analyses, and scalability assessments for more complex scenes.

title: Modeling Decisions in Blockchain Analytics: A Leakage-Aware Evaluation of Tree-Based vs. Sequential Models
comment: Accepted for presentation at the 23rd International Conference on Modeling Decisions for Artificial Intelligence (MDAI 2026)
summary: Sybil bots are Ethereum actors that imitate legitimate users to extract airdrop rewards or influence governance. Recent Sybil detection methods increasingly use deep learning and treat blockchain activity as a quasi-linguistic sequence. However, complex sequence models are computationally expensive for real-time monitoring, and their reported performance may be inflated by label leakage from high-signal smart contracts. We ask whether and how organic users, Sybil bots, and MEV bots differ in the structural complexity of their transaction histories; whether sequential models outperform tree-based tabular models once leakage is reduced; whether transaction order or timing provides the stronger behavioral signal; and whether the resulting models are practical for low-latency deployment. Our approach to leakage-aware Sybil bot detection consists of a Blind-Spot protocol and a Transaction Grammar representation of wallet behavior. The former eliminates shortcuts associated with high-signal contracts, whereas the latter models wallets using rhythm, EVM execution structure, and intent. We evaluate this approach on Ethereum actor classification by comparing Transformer and BiLSTM sequence models against XGBoost and SVM baselines. We contribute a framework for leakage-aware Ethereum actor classification and a Transaction Grammar representation of wallet behavior. Our results demonstrate that, under leakage-aware evaluation, XGBoost outperforms Transformer-based sequence models while providing lower latency and estimated energy use.

AI.tldr: Leakage-aware Ethereum actor classification showing that XGBoost beats Transformer/BiLSTM under leakage mitigation, using a Blind-Spot protocol and a Transaction Grammar representation for efficient, low-latency deployment.
AI.motivation: Deep sequential models for Sybil/MEV bot detection are computationally expensive and prone to label leakage from high-signal contracts; assessing whether leakage-aware, structured representations enable competitive performance with lightweight models.
AI.method: Introduce Blind-Spot protocol to remove leakage from high-signal contracts; propose Transaction Grammar capturing wallet rhythm, EVM execution structure, and intent; compare Transformer and BiLSTM sequence models with XGBoost and SVM baselines for leakage-aware Ethereum actor classification.
AI.result: Under leakage-aware evaluation, XGBoost outperforms Transformer-based sequence models and offers lower latency and estimated energy use.
AI.conclusion: A leakage-aware framework and Transaction Grammar enable practical, efficient Ethereum actor classification; tree-based models can surpass deep sequence models when leakage is mitigated, supporting real-time monitoring.

title: BlindPSNR: A No-Reference Fidelity Predictor for Low-Light Image Enhancement
summary: Low-light image enhancement (LLIE) methods involve tunable parameters that are typically fixed, often leading to performance degradation when applied across scenes. Manually selecting the best configuration, however, can be time-consuming and not always practical. Peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) is the natural fidelity criterion for automating parameter selection, yet it requires a ground-truth reference that is typically unavailable. To our knowledge, no learning-based method addresses no-reference PSNR prediction for low-light image enhancement; the natural surrogate, no-reference image quality assessment (NR-IQA), targets perceptual quality rather than signal fidelity, and all seven baselines we test achieve 0% top-1 selection accuracy on our benchmark. With paired training data, the ground-truth PSNR is analytically computable, providing exact supervision without a separate teacher network. Building on this, we propose BlindPSNR, a lightweight no-reference network that fuses the enhanced image with the degraded low-light input via windowed cross-attention and estimates PSNR through heteroscedastic regression. While a scalar-regression baseline achieves top-1 accuracy of 54.4%, BlindPSNR raises this to 89.5% with regret dropping from 1.62 dB to 0.026 dB, and generalizes to unseen datasets (SRCC = 0.61-0.67).

AI.tldr: BlindPSNR: a lightweight no-reference PSNR predictor for low-light image enhancement using windowed cross-attention and heteroscedastic regression to select parameters.
AI.motivation: LLIE methods rely on fixed parameters; PSNR requires ground-truth and no-reference PSNR predictors are lacking, making autonomous parameter tuning impractical; NR-IQA does not align with PSNR fidelity.
AI.method: A no-referenc e network that fuses the enhanced image with the degraded input via windowed cross-attention and estimates PSNR via heteroscedastic regression, trained on paired data with computable ground-truth PSNR.
AI.result: Achieves top-1 selection accuracy of 89.5% (vs 54.4% for a scalar regression baseline); regret drops from 1.62 dB to 0.026 dB; generalizes to unseen datasets with SRCC between 0.61 and 0.67.
AI.conclusion: BlindPSNR provides effective, generalizable no-reference PSNR prediction for LLIE, enabling automatic parameter selection without ground-truth references.

title: A dataset of rated conceptual arguments
summary: Large language models have improved rapidly on tasks with verifiable answers, such as mathematics and programming. Much less is known about their ability to reason about what we call conceptual questions: questions for which no ground truth is realistically accessible and no widely accepted resolution methodology exists, but on which progress can still be made by debating arguments. Most philosophical questions are of this kind, as are central components of questions in AI safety, decision theory, and social choice. Our approach is based on the view that while bottom-line conclusions on such questions are hard to evaluate, individual contextualized arguments can be evaluated far more reliably. We therefore introduce a dataset of 951 argumentative critiques of 442 position texts, spanning topics from AI safety and decision theory to ethics and politics, with 1,458 ratings by six expert raters along dimensions including centrality, strength, correctness, and clarity. We propose two scoring functions and benchmark a range of models. Performance tracks general capability rankings.

AI.tldr: Introduces a dataset of 951 argumentative critiques (442 position texts) across AI safety, decision theory, ethics, and politics, with six expert ratings; proposes two scoring functions and benchmarks LLMs; shows model performance aligns with general capability rankings.
AI.motivation: Evaluate reasoning on conceptual questions lacking ground-truth by focusing on contextualized arguments, addressing philosophical and AI-safety related debates where progress is debated rather than resolved.
AI.method: Construct a dataset of 951 argumentative critiques of 442 position texts; six expert raters evaluate centrality, strength, correctness, and clarity; propose two scoring functions to quantify quality; benchmark a range of models performing on these tasks.
AI.result: Scoring functions yield model rankings that correlate with general capability rankings; the dataset provides a practical benchmark for conceptual-argument evaluation across topics.
AI.conclusion: Contextualized-argument evaluation is feasible and informative for measuring progress on conceptual questions; the approach enables benchmarking of LLMs in philosophy, AI safety, and related fields via structured argumentative assessments.

title: SemAnCorr: Semantic Anchored Correspondence for Zero-Shot Manipulation Skill Transfer
summary: Transferring manipulation skills across object instances that share functionality but differ in geometry remains a fundamental challenge in robot learning. While recent correspondence methods leverage dense visual descriptors and 3D feature fields, nearest-neighbor feature matching often produces spatially incoherent correspondences that fail to recover the local geometric frames required for reliable skill transfer. We introduce SemAnCorr, a training-free framework that establishes dense correspondence by selecting semantically consistent anchor regions through joint pose-correspondence optimization and propagating these constraints over the object surface using functional maps. The resulting correspondences preserve both semantic consistency and geometric coherence, enabling object-centric manipulation skills to transfer across geometrically diverse instances. We evaluate SemAnCorr on a dense correspondence benchmark built on PartNet-Mobility, achieving 90.8% semantic accuracy in our benchmark evaluation while improving geometric coherence over recent state-of-the-art baselines. Finally, we show that these improvements translate directly into real-world manipulation performance: using a single demonstration, SemAnCorr enables substantially more reliable zero-shot manipulation skill transfer to previously unseen objects than existing correspondence methods. Videos and additional visualizations are available at [https://semancorr.github.io](https://semancorr.github.io) .

AI.tldr: SemAnCorr is a training-free dense correspondence framework that uses semantically consistent anchor regions selected via joint pose-correspondence optimization and propagates constraints over the object surface with functional maps to achieve semantically and geometrically coherent correspondences for cross-instance manipulation skill transfer, outperforming baselines on PartNet-Mobility (90.8% semantic accuracy) and enabling reliable zero-shot transfer from a single demonstration.
AI.motivation: To enable robust transfer of manipulation skills across object instances that share functionality but differ in geometry, addressing the failure of dense descriptor-based nearest-neighbor matching to produce coherent, frame-preserving correspondences.
AI.method: A training-free pipeline that (1) selects semantically consistent anchor regions via joint pose–correspondence optimization, and (2) propagates these constraints over the object surface using functional maps to obtain dense, semantically coherent and geometrically coherent correspondences for cross-instance manipulation.
AI.result: On a PartNet-Mobility-based dense correspondence benchmark, SemAnCorr achieves 90.8% semantic accuracy and improves geometric coherence over state-of-the-art baselines; in real-world manipulation, it enables substantially more reliable zero-shot skill transfer to unseen objects from a single demonstration.
AI.conclusion: SemAnCorr demonstrates that combining anchor-based semantic constraints with functional-map propagation yields reliable, training-free cross-instance manipulation skill transfer, with strong semantic and geometric coherence and practical benefits for zero-shot generalization.

title: Compression-Based Behavioral Similarity for Open-World Sybil Discovery on Ethereum
comment: Accepted as a full paper and scheduled for presentation at the European Conference on Advances in Databases and Information Systems (ADBIS 2026)
summary: Sybil attackers are Blockchain actors that adopt the characteristics of regular users to exploit airdrops or influence governance. Current methods of Sybil actor detection include constructing graphs, which requires token transfers between examined wallets. Machine learning algorithms have been employed as well, but they treat the task as a closed-set classification problem, making them vulnerable to frequent changes in attack strategies or evasion tactics. We address the following questions: can compression-based similarity differentiate Sybil bots, organic users, and arbitrage bot wallets without direct financial links? What is the effect of high-signal contracts on the discovery of Sybils, and how robust are behavioral graphs under temporal drift and adversarial perturbations? Our approach synthesizes a symbolic Transaction Grammar from EVM (Ethereum Virtual Machine) traces, capturing separately transaction rhythm, execution structure, and functional intent. The high-signal contracts are filtered with our own protocol, called the Blind-Spot Protocol. Gzip-based NCD is used to construct a behavioral graph for Sybil discovery. We validate this framework against supervised machine learning baselines, a temporal split, and synthetic camouflage stress tests. Ultimately, we contribute a leakage-aware behavioral framework for Sybil candidate discovery. Its core NCD primitive requires no supervised training and can expand suspicious seed wallets without explicit funding links. We position the method as a training-free local discovery primitive for open-world blockchain audits, rather than as a formal open-set recognition system.

AI.tldr: A training-free, compression-based framework detects Sybil wallets in open-world blockchains without relying on explicit funding links, using a symbolic EVM trace grammar and gzip-based NCD to build a leakage-aware behavioral graph; validated against ML baselines with temporal and camouflage tests, claimed as a local discovery primitive for audits.
AI.motivation: Address the brittleness of ML-based Sybil detection and the dependence on direct financial links by offering a training-free, open-world capable method that can adapt to evolving attacker strategies and evasion tactics.
AI.method: 1) Synthesize a symbolic Transaction Grammar from Ethereum Virtual Machine traces, separating rhythm, execution structure, and functional intent. 2) Filter high-signal contracts via a Blind-Spot Protocol. 3) Construct a behavioral graph using gzip-based Normalized Compression Distance (NCD). 4) Validate against supervised ML baselines, temporal data splits, and synthetic camouflage tests.
AI.result: Demonstrates a leakage-aware, training-free local discovery primitive for Sybil candidate wallets, able to expand seed wallets without explicit funding links; shown to be robust under temporal drift and adversarial perturbations via tests.
AI.conclusion: Proposes a practical, open-world auditing tool for blockchain governance/Sybil detection that reduces dependence on labeled data and direct transactional links, while acknowledging it as a local discovery primitive rather than a formal open-set recognizer.

title: 4DHumanDiff: Direct Text-to-4DGS Generation for Consistent 360-Degree Dynamic Humans
summary: Generating high-quality 360-degree dynamic human assets from text prompts is challenging. Existing methods usually synthesize monocular or multi-view videos first and then fit a 4D representation, which is expensive and often causes incomplete geometry or view-inconsistent renderings. We present 4DHumanDiff, a diffusion framework that directly generates dynamic humans represented by 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) from text prompts. By modeling the structured 4D representation space end-to-end, 4DHumanDiff avoids video pre-generation and per-scene reconstruction, making it better suited for view-consistent and temporally coherent asset generation. The model uses a 3D U-Net backbone with temporal attention for motion-aware generation. We further construct a large-scale text-to-4DGS dataset with 60,000 high-quality pairs, and introduce 2D regularization and training-free 4D interpolation to improve rendering quality and motion smoothness. Experiments show that 4DHumanDiff generates consistent 360-degree dynamic humans within one minute, achieves better temporal and multi-view consistency, and reduces inference time by more than 10x.

AI.tldr: End-to-end diffusion model, 4DHumanDiff, directly generates 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) dynamic humans from text prompts, bypassing video pre-generation; achieves fast, view-consistent 360-degree assets with 10x speedup and 1-minute generation.
AI.motivation: Existing pipelines synthesize monocular or multi-view videos first and then fit a 4D representation, which is expensive and prone to incomplete geometry and view inconsistencies; an end-to-end text-to-4D representation approach is needed for efficient, coherent dynamic humans.
AI.method: A diffusion-based framework with a 3D U-Net backbone and temporal attention that generates dynamic humans represented by 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) directly from text prompts. Supports a large text-to-4DGS dataset (60k pairs), 2D regularization, and training-free 4D interpolation. Avoids video pre-generation and per-scene reconstruction; produces view-consistent, temporally coherent 360-degree outputs.
AI.result: Generates consistent 360-degree dynamic humans within one minute; achieves better temporal and multi-view consistency; reduces inference time by more than 10x.
AI.conclusion: End-to-end diffusion over 4DGS enables fast, view-consistent, temporally coherent 360-degree dynamic human asset generation from text, reducing cost and complexity compared with two-stage pipelines.

title: Automated Transcript Analysis for Detecting Flaws in Agentic Benchmarks
summary: Capabilities of frontier models are often assessed using agentic benchmarks. To trust these results, benchmarks must accurately measure what they claim to and be free from invalidating flaws. Previous manual audits of benchmarks such as SWE-Bench-Verified have uncovered several validity issues in transcripts. However, manual review is difficult to scale, and it is unclear whether automated methods can reliably surface flaws that compromise benchmark validity. In this paper, we developed AI scanners to detect four types of validity issues: ground truth access, tool failure, guessing vulnerability, and answer format ambiguity. We produced grading rubrics for each to instruct human labeling, and evaluated the scanners against human labels on a held-out test set of Inspect Evals benchmarks. Our scanners identified several verified quality issues in five widely used benchmarks, including cases unlikely to be caught by random manual inspection. Not all cases were identified, and scanner performance varied substantially across benchmarks, criteria and models. We highlight several open challenges to be addressed to improve scanners for stronger quality assurance claims, including broader standardization gaps in the evaluation field that degrade scanner performance. Together, these results serve as a proof of concept for using automated transcript analysis to audit benchmark quality more broadly.

AI.tldr: Automated AI scanners can surface validity flaws in agentic benchmarks for frontier models by detecting ground-truth access issues, tool failures, guessing vulnerability, and answer-format ambiguity, evaluated against human labels on Inspect Evals benchmarks; found issues across five benchmarks with variable scanner performance; demonstrates proof-of-concept and highlights challenges.
AI.motivation: Ensure benchmarks measure what they claim and remain trustworthy; manual audits are not scalable; automated transcript analysis could enable scalable quality assurance of benchmarks.
AI.method: Develop four AI scanners targeting validity facets; create grading rubrics to guide human labeling; evaluate scanners against a held-out human-labeled test set drawn from Inspect Evals benchmarks; apply scanners to five widely used benchmarks; compare against manual audits and analyze performance and limitations.
AI.result: Scanners identified several verified quality issues in multiple benchmarks, including cases unlikely to be caught by random manual inspection; scanner performance varied across benchmarks, criteria, and models; some issues remained undetected; evidence supports feasibility but also gaps and variability.
AI.conclusion: Automated transcript analysis is a feasible proof-of-concept for auditing benchmark quality at scale; broader standardization gaps in evaluation hinder scanner performance; further research needed to improve reliability and coverage, and to standardize evaluation protocols.

title: TacWAM: Anchor-Guided World Action Model with Mechanics-Aware Tactile Prediction
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) combine future-state prediction with robot action generation, but existing approaches largely rely on visual futures. Visual prediction captures scene structure and object motion, yet provides limited supervision for force, deformation, shear, and slip during contact-rich manipulation. This creates two design requirements: tactile futures should carry meaningful physical information, and they should not become privileged cues for action generation. We present TacWAM, a mechanics-aware tactile WAM that addresses this challenge in three steps. First, a Spatially Aligned Fusion (SAF) Tactile Encoder maps tactile appearance, dense force fields, and deformation flow into a shared latent prediction space, with bilateral force and torque reconstruction preserving global contact information. Second, a tactile history encoder provides temporal context so future tactile prediction reflects how force and deformation change beyond the current tactile observation. Third, Anchor-Guided Tri-Modal (AGT) Attention separates current visual and tactile anchors, future prediction tokens, and action tokens, allowing future tactile states to supervise training without being directly read by the action branch. We evaluate TacWAM on four real-world contact-rich manipulation tasks covering fragile grasping, sustained surface contact, and dynamic in-hand manipulation. TacWAM achieves an average success rate of 75.0%, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 37.5 percentage points. Staged ablations show consistent degradation when tactile history is removed and access to future prediction targets is relaxed. These results indicate that future tactile supervision can improve contact-aware action learning when combined with informative tactile representations and deployment-consistent information constraints.

AI.tldr: TacWAM presents a mechanics-aware tactile world model with SAF tactile encoder, tactile history, and AGT attention to align current/future tactile signals with action tokens, achieving 75.0% success across four real-world contact-rich tasks and outperforming baselines; ablations show tactile history and future supervision are essential.
AI.motivation: Visual future predictions alone inadequately capture force, deformation, and slip in contact-rich manipulation; tactile futures are needed but must not unduly bias action generation.
AI.method: Three components: (1) Spatially Aligned Fusion (SAF) Tactile Encoder fuses tactile appearance, dense force fields, and deformation flow into a shared latent space, with bilateral force/torque reconstruction to preserve contact information. (2) Tactile history encoder adds temporal context for future tactile predictions. (3) Anchor-Guided Tri-Modal (AGT) Attention separates current visual/tactile anchors, future prediction tokens, and action tokens so future tactile supervision trains the model without leaking to the action branch.
AI.result: Evaluated on four real-world tasks (fragile grasping, sustained surface contact, dynamic in-hand manipulation); average success rate 75.0%, outperforming the strongest baseline by 37.5 percentage points. Ablations show performance degrades when tactile history is removed or access to future prediction targets is relaxed.
AI.conclusion: Future tactile supervision, when combined with informative tactile representations and deployment-consistent constraints, improves contact-aware action learning.

title: Explorative Modeling: Unlocking a Third Pretraining Axis and End-to-End Generation
summary: The deep learning revolution, kicked off by AlexNet, taught us that end-to-end training beats decomposing a problem into hand-designed stages. Generative modeling, however, has remained the exception-despite generative models being remarkably capable, they are still not trained end-to-end. This is because, at its core, generative modeling is about handling distributions with many modes, and existing scalable approaches handle this the same way, by factoring the generation procedure, which prevents end-to-end generation. In this work, we introduce Explorative Modeling, a new paradigm that instead factors the training loop, exploring K candidate matches between model generations and data, and training on the best, so predictions commit to modes rather than blurring them. We find Explorative Models (XMs) useful in two settings. First, increasing exploration adds a third pretraining axis beyond parameters and data for existing generative models-where scaling exploration monotonically improves performance across both continuous and discrete domains (images, video, and language).
