To eliminate mesh dependency and provide a unified representation that bridges point clouds and G-code, we propose Geometric plan (G-plan) map, a compact 2D representation composed of occupancy, region, and flow maps that encode the geometric and extrusion properties required for toolpath synthesis in 3D printing. As a result, our proposed method accurately generates printable G-code directly from point clouds, enabling a practical and fully mesh-free pipeline for 3D printing. The code is publicly available at \href{https://github.com/Sangminhong/PrintAnything}{https://github.com/Sangminhong/PrintAnything}.

AI.tldr: Mesh-free pipeline PrintAnything directly converts 3D point clouds into executable 3D printing G-code by introducing slice-wise projection and a G-plan map, enabling direct fabrication without mesh reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Overcome reliance on watertight meshes and mesh reconstruction artifacts in 3D printing pipelines; enable direct fabrication from point clouds.
AI.method: Proposes slice-wise point projection to align unstructured point clouds to 2D slices; introduces G-plan map (occupancy, region, flow) as a compact 2D representation bridging point clouds and G-code; learns to synthesize G-code from these representations.
AI.result: Demonstrates accurate generation of printable G-code from point clouds, enabling a fully mesh-free 3D printing pipeline; code released.
AI.conclusion: Mesh-free point-cloud to G-code pipeline is viable and reduces printing failures due to mesh artifacts; broadens input modalities for 3D printing.

title: Wiring diagram extraction and gluing: a case study in classifying figure skating jumps using 3D dataset
summary: Hasse clustering is an algorithm that extracts common patterns in sequential data and represents them in graphical forms. As the number of expected clusters grows, however, the algorithm can become infeasible to run due to combinatorial complexity. In this article, we describe a theory of gluing wiring diagrams, allowing iterative applications of Hasse clustering to achieve the same result as a single application. We test our theory in the context of classifying videos of figure skating jumps.

AI.tldr: Hasse clustering suffers combinatorial blow-up with many clusters; this work proposes gluing wiring diagrams to enable iterative clustering that equates to a single application, and validates the approach on classifying figure skating jump videos.
AI.motivation: Address the scalability issue in Hasse clustering by providing a compositional, reusable theory (gluing wiring diagrams) that preserves the clustering outcome across iterative steps.
AI.method: Develop a theory of gluing wiring diagrams to compose multiple Hasse clustering steps; show equivalence to a single application; apply the framework to sequential data and test on video data of figure skating jumps.
AI.result: Empirical validation demonstrating that iterative clustering via the gluing framework can reproduce the single-pass clustering outcomes on the tested video-classification task.
AI.conclusion: The gluing wiring diagram framework provides a scalable, compositional approach to Hasse clustering in sequential data and is applicable to real-world pattern discovery tasks such as video classification.

title: PAC-MAN: Perception-Aware CBF-RL for Whole-Body Safety in Humanoid Dodgeball
summary: We present PAC-MAN, a perception-aware CBF-RL framework that couples control-barrier safety with deployment-realistic onboard sensing for whole-body humanoid dodgeball. The deployed policy sees the ball only as segmentation-masked depth from a head-mounted camera, while training-time CBF guidance represents clearance to every body link, and an adversarial motion prior regularizes the resulting evasive reflexes. We evaluate on a controlled any-link contact benchmark with seeded throws in two regimes: single throws and a deployment loop in which the robot walks back to its station and recovers between throws. On this benchmark, the policy comes within a few points of a privileged state oracle: a fixed onboard camera alone is adequate for evasion. We find that usable barrier structure depends on perceptual observability: Joint-CBF gives the best performance with accurate ball states, degrades under fixed-camera observations when used only as training guidance, and recovers with a ball-tracking gimbal or privileged runtime filter. We therefore deploy a lightweight Link-CBF policy zero-shot on the Unitree G1 in the real world, where it tolerates imperfect perception, succeeds on 95% of throws, and uses semantic segmentation to dodge different balls.

AI.tldr: PAC-MAN merges perception-aware CBF-RL with realist onboard sensing for humanoid dodgeball; achieves near-privileged safety and 95% success in real-world deployment using segmentation depth and motion priors.
AI.motivation: Address safety and perceptual observability gaps in robotic high-speed contact tasks; link perception to barrier-based safety across body links; enable zero-shot deployment with limited perception.
AI.method: CBF-RL with joint-CBF; training-time CBF guidance; adversarial motion prior; segmentation-masked depth from head camera; evaluation on any-link contact benchmark; deployment loop with re-stationing; ablations using ball-tracking gimbal or privileged runtime filter.
AI.result: Policy approaches a privileged-state oracle under favorable perceptual observability; single onboard camera can suffice for evasion; Joint-CBF best with accurate ball states, degrades with fixed-camera training guidance, recovers with tracking or runtime filter; real-world deployment on Unitree G1 achieves 95% success and uses segmentation to dodge diverse balls.
AI.conclusion: Perception-observability governs barrier structure efficacy; with enhanced perception (ball-tracking or runtime filtering) barrier methods remain robust; zero-shot deployment viable for safe, dynamic humanoid tasks using segmentation-based perception.

title: Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN for Channel Modeling in Low-SNR Regimes
summary: Accurate multipath parameter estimation is critical for modern wireless communication systems, particularly in challenging low-SNR environments. Traditional Maximum Likelihood Estimation algorithms, such as CLEAN, provide high-resolution parameter extraction but suffer from prohibitive computational complexity due to exhaustive grid search. Conversely, purely data-driven deep learning approaches lack physical grounding and struggle to generalize across variable multipath densities and off-grid parameters. To address these limitations, this paper proposes Neural Network-Assisted CLEAN (NN-CLEAN), a hybrid framework that embeds a multi-head residual network directly into the iterative CLEAN extraction loop. By replacing the exhaustive grid search with rapid, parallelizable forward passes while delegating residual subtraction to exact mathematical models, NN-CLEAN isolates physical multipath parameters without accumulating non- physical errors. Extensive Monte Carlo simulations demonstrate that NN-CLEAN achieves estimation accuracy exceeding 96% at 5 dB SNR, matching the traditional Grid-Search CLEAN (GS- CLEAN) baseline, while providing a massive reduction in computational complexity and substantially outperforming subspace methods and standalone one-shot neural networks. Crucially, NN-CLEAN exhibits a near-flat scaling in execution runtime and memory consumption as batch sizes increase. This highly efficient parallelization establishes NN-CLEAN as a robust, real- time solution for channel estimation in MIMO systems.

AI.tldr: Hybrid NN-assisted CLEAN (NN-CLEAN) replaces exhaustive grid search with a multi-head residual network inside CLEAN, achieving near GS-CLEAN accuracy with massive speedups and scalable runtime.
AI.motivation: Traditional grid-search CLEAN is computationally prohibitive; pure DL lacks physical grounding and generalization over multipath densities/off-grid parameters. A hybrid approach aims for fast, accurate, physically-consistent parameter estimation in challenging low-SNR scenarios.
AI.method: Integrate a multi-head residual network into the iterative CLEAN loop. Use rapid, parallel forward passes for parameter proposals while performing exact physical residual subtraction. Leverage batch processing to maintain near-constant computational scaling; evaluate via extensive Monte Carlo simulations.
AI.result: Estimation accuracy >96% at 5 dB SNR, matching Grid-Search CLEAN (GS-CLEAN); substantial reduction in computational complexity; outperforms subspace methods and standalone neural nets; near-flat scaling of runtime and memory with batch size, enabling real-time operation in MIMO channel estimation.
AI.conclusion: NN-CLEAN offers a robust, efficient, real-time capable solution by fusing data-driven speed with physics-based modeling, addressing the main limitations of both grid-search CLEAN and pure DL approaches.

title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
summary: Building interactive digital twins requires recovering both 3D geometry and the kinematic structures that govern how objects articulate. Yet existing methods for articulated object reconstruction require explicitly observable motion from multiple articulation states. We introduce a rest-state formulation that reconstructs articulated objects from a single closed configuration, an inherently ill-posed setting where geometry, semantics, and motion priors compensate for the absence of motion cues. Our framework adopts an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation for cross-model verification and fusion, reconciling noisy outputs from vision-language and segmentation models into spatially consistent part structures. To estimate joint parameters without observed motion, we use a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses and validate them through geometric consistency. Our approach achieves accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, performing competitively with motion-observing reconstruction-based, generation-based, and modular pretrained-model baselines.

AI.tldr: Rest-state articulated-object reconstruction from a single configuration using an explicit mesh intermediary to synthesize and validate articulation hypotheses with a video diffusion model, achieving competitive accuracy without motion cues.
AI.motivation: Enable reconstruction of articulated objects when only a single closed configuration is available, addressing the ill-posed nature of jointly recovering geometry, semantics, and motion priors without motion cues.
AI.method: Propose a rest-state formulation with an explicit mesh as an intermediate representation to fuse noisy vision-language and segmentation outputs into consistent part structures; use a video diffusion model to synthesize articulation hypotheses and validate them via geometric consistency.
AI.result: Accurate part decomposition and physically plausible articulation, with performance competitive with motion-observing reconstruction-based, generation-based, and modular pretrained-model baselines.
AI.conclusion: The rest-state approach demonstrates that articulated geometry and kinematic structure can be recovered from a single configuration by combining mesh-based cross-model verification with diffusion-based articulation synthesis, enabling plausible interactive digital twins.

title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
summary: Building generalizable agents for diverse applications remains a fundamental challenge. While imitation learning-based policies succeed in specific training environments, they often fail to generalize to novel scenes and tasks. In this work, we propose World Action Planner, a robot planning system that leverages the reasoning capabilities of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and the physical grounding of a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model. Our system enables an agent to propose initial action plans and iteratively refine them via optimization and search, reasoning over imagined world model rollouts. We demonstrate that our approach achieves superior performance across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot generalization scenarios, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art end-to-end policy models such as VLAs and WAMs. Project website at worldactionplanner.github.io

AI.tldr: A planning-based robot control framework that combines Vision-Language Models (VLMs) with a pose-image conditioned world model to generate and iteratively refine action plans via imagined rollouts, enabling robust generalization to unseen tasks and layouts.
AI.motivation: Imitation-learning policies perform well in training environments but struggle to generalize to novel scenes and tasks; there is a need for planning-based approaches that reason about actions and their physical consequences.
AI.method: World Action Planner uses VLMs to propose initial action plans and a multi-task pose-image conditioned world model to ground these plans in the physical world. The agent iteratively refines plans through optimization and search by reasoning over imagined world-model rollouts.
AI.result: The approach achieves superior performance across compositional tasks, new layouts, and zero-shot generalization, significantly outperforming state-of-the-art end-to-end policy models such as VLAs and WAMs.
AI.conclusion: Integrating vision-language reasoning with grounded world models in a planning framework improves generalization to unseen tasks and layouts over traditional imitation-learning policies; further details available on the project website.

title: FADEx: Feature Attribution and Distortion-based Explanation of Dimensionality Reduction
comment: 18 pages, 17 figures, to be published in IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
summary: Dimensionality Reduction (DR) is a fundamental tool for high-dimensional data exploration, reducing the complexity of latent spaces of machine learning models, and assisting in the explanation of complex opaque models. However, non-linear DR techniques often function as opaque transformations themselves, making it challenging to understand how individual features influence instance positioning in the reduced space. This lack of transparency complicates the analysis and interpretation of structural patterns, hindering the ability to reason about the organization of high-dimensional data based on the projected layout. In order to address this challenge, dimensionality reduction explanation methods have shown promise in improving the understanding of the observed groups and cluster structures. Unfortunately, existing DR explanation approaches tend to suffer from limitations such as multiple attributions per feature and restricted applicability to specific dimensionality reduction methods, which hinder their use. In this work, we propose FADEx, a novel local per-instance feature attribution method that leverages local linear approximation via first-order Taylor expansion and Singular Value Decomposition to provide explanations. FADEx computes the local linear models via weighted least squares, eliminating the need for out-of-sample data mapping, making it agnostic to the DR method, while simultaneously providing local feature attributions and distortion analysis. Through qualitative and quantitative evaluations, comparisons with existing methods, and case studies, we demonstrate FADEx's effectiveness and versatility in providing explanations and analytical resources for analyzing the behavior of DR methods. The results indicate FADEx yields robust and reliable explanations, outperforming existing approaches in several aspects.

AI.tldr: FADEx provides local per-instance feature attributions for dimensionality reduction (DR) methods using local linear approximations via Taylor expansion and SVD; DR-agnostic, with distortion analysis, and strong empirical results compared to existing explanations.
AI.motivation: DR techniques yield opaque projections; existing DR explanations face issues such as multiple attributions per feature and limited applicability across DR methods; there is a need for a DR-agnostic, per-instance, efficient explanation tool that also analyzes distortion.
AI.method: Compute local linear models around each data point via a first-order Taylor expansion of the DR mapping, use Singular Value Decomposition to derive influential directions, and fit these models with weighted least squares; method does not require out-of-sample data mapping and is agnostic to the DR technique; provides local feature attributions and distortion metrics.
AI.result: Qualitative and quantitative evaluations, comparisons with existing DR explanation methods, and case studies indicate that FADEx yields robust, reliable explanations and outperforms existing approaches in several aspects, while also offering distortion analysis.
AI.conclusion: FADEx delivers a versatile, DR-agnostic explanation framework that enhances the interpretability of non-linear DR projections, enabling better reasoning about data organization in reduced spaces, with strong empirical support.

title: EgoGVAE: Ego-body Mesh Reconstruction via Guided Variational Autoencoder
summary: We address the problem of recovering the full-body mesh from only the head pose. This task has become essential for various applications based on head-mounted devices or smart glasses. The challenge of this task lies in estimating the pose information of unobserved body parts based solely on a single joint (i.e., head) trajectory. Several studies have begun to adopt head-conditioned generative models, however, such previous methods are costly and time-consuming due to the diffusion-based iterative process. As an alternative, we propose a simple yet novel method that leverages the latent space of the guidance network, which is designed as a variational autoencoder taking full-body poses as inputs. By enforcing latent distributions of this guidance network and our head-to-motion network to be similar, latent features sampled from the 'guided' distribution, i.e., distribution learned in our head-to-motion network, can be reliably decoded for natural representations of full-body poses even only with the head pose. One important advantage of the proposed method is that one-step sampling scheme achieves remarkably fast inference (more than 50 times faster) compared to diffusion-based approaches. Experimental results on benchmark datasets show that the proposed method efficiently improves the performance of ego-body mesh reconstruction.

AI.tldr: One-step latent-guided full-body pose reconstruction from head pose, using a VAE-based guidance network with latent-space distribution alignment to enable fast, diffusion-free sampling; improves ego-body mesh reconstruction speed by >50× while maintaining or improving accuracy on benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Recover full-body mesh from head pose for AR/VR and head-mounted devices; current diffusion-based methods are accurate but slow; need real-time solutions.
AI.method: Train a guidance network as a variational autoencoder on full-body poses; enforce similarity between latent distributions of the guidance network and a head-to-motion network; during inference sample from the guided distribution and decode to full-body pose in a single step (no iterative diffusion).
AI.result: In experiments on benchmark datasets, the method achieves substantially faster inference (over 50×) and improves or preserves performance in ego-body mesh reconstruction compared to diffusion-based baselines.
AI.conclusion: Latent-space alignment between a VAE-guidance network and head-to-motion network enables efficient, one-shot full-body pose reconstruction from head pose, offering real-time viability for head-mounted AR/VR applications.

title: CORE: In-Context Reconstruction for Unified Tabular Anomaly Detection
summary: Tabular anomaly detection (TAD), which focuses on identifying abnormal samples that deviate from the majority in tabular data, has received growing attention. Recently, there has been an emerging trend towards unified TAD, which seeks to detect anomalies across different datasets using a single generalizable model. In unified TAD, aligning heterogeneous data remains challenging. While existing methods often rely on distance-based unified feature construction, they may obscure the semantics of the original features. Moreover, existing approaches typically formulate anomaly detection as a binary classification task, which may overlook diverse anomaly patterns from various datasets and be misled by unrepresentative synthetic anomalies. To address these challenges, we propose an in-COntext REconstruction approach for unified TAD (CORE for short). It introduces a decorrelated feature alignment module to directly align heterogeneous features into a unified representation space, which retains their semantic information. Meanwhile, CORE formulates unified TAD as an in-context reconstruction problem, eliminating the need for labeled or synthesized anomalies. Specifically, the in-context reconstruction module reconstructs each sample by leveraging contextual normal samples to capture dataset-specific distributions, such that reconstruction errors reflect its deviation from normality, facilitating unified TAD on arbitrary unseen datasets.

AI.tldr: CORE introduces an in-context reconstruction approach for unified tabular anomaly detection, combining decorrelated feature alignment and context-based reconstruction to handle unseen datasets without labeled or synthetic anomalies.
AI.motivation: To address challenges in unified TAD: aligning heterogeneous tabular features while preserving their semantics, moving beyond binary classification and synthetic anomalies, and enabling robust anomaly detection across diverse, unseen datasets.
AI.method: 1) A decorrelated feature alignment module that maps heterogeneous features into a unified representation space while retaining semantic information. 2) An in-context reconstruction module that reconstructs each sample using contextual normal samples to capture dataset-specific distributions, so reconstruction errors reflect deviation from normality.
AI.result: The abstract argues that CORE enables unified TAD on arbitrary unseen datasets by preserving semantics through feature alignment and leveraging context-based reconstruction, avoiding reliance on labeled or synthesized anomalies.
AI.conclusion: CORE provides a generalizable, label-free framework for unified TAD by combining decorrelated feature alignment with in-context reconstruction to handle dataset heterogeneity and diverse anomaly patterns across unseen data.

title: HALO: Heterogeneous Admission through Localized Obligations for Safe Agentic Execution
summary: Recent agentic AI systems may return a heterogeneous response containing notices, requests, handoffs, and actions. Conditions can change before external use, so components from the same response need not remain supported together. Rejecting the whole response discards useful components, whereas checking components independently can leave a dependent without its prerequisite. We present Heterogeneous Admission with Localized Obligations (HALO), a runtime protocol that preserves supported components whose declared prerequisites also remain supported, rechecks each exact action before dispatch, and allows blocked actions to be replaced only by fresh candidates. HALO matched all 96 admission expectations and passed all 20 protocol tests. In structured-response replay, it retained 248/248 supported components, including 128/128 unaffected by unrelated changes, while a whole-response policy retained 0/248. Across ten cold-start PX4/Gazebo sessions, HALO blocked every tested stale route, observed no matching stale setpoint, and completed all fresh recoveries.

AI.tldr: HALO is a runtime policy for heterogeneous responses that preserves components whose prerequisites remain supported, rechecks each action before dispatch, and substitutes blocked actions with fresh candidates. It avoids discarding useful parts of a response and prevents execution of stale routes, achieving high adherence to admission expectations and strong recovery behavior in robotics simulations.
AI.motivation: Agentic AI systems often produce multi-part responses (notices, requests, handoffs, actions) where prerequisites and support can change independently. Rejecting whole responses wastes useful components and independent checks can miss dependencies. A robust runtime that preserves valid components while ensuring safety and consistency is needed.
AI.method: HALO introduces a runtime protocol that (1) retains components whose declared prerequisites remain satisfied, (2) rechecks each exact action before execution, and (3) replaces blocked actions only with fresh candidates. It evaluates component-level validity via admission expectations, protocol tests, structured-response replay, and cold-start PX4/Gazebo experiments to demonstrate correctness and robustness against stale information.
AI.result: HALO matched all 96 admission expectations and passed all 20 protocol tests. In structured-response replay, it retained 248/248 components (128/128 unaffected by unrelated changes). A whole-response policy retained 0/248. In ten cold-start PX4/Gazebo sessions, HALO blocked every tested stale route, observed no matching stale setpoint, and completed all fresh recoveries.
AI.conclusion: HALO provides fine-grained, dependency-aware admission for heterogeneous responses, minimizing waste and enhancing safety by ensuring only valid components are dispatched and stale paths are blocked. Empirically, it demonstrates strong completeness and robustness across simulations and robotics workloads.

title: Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring
summary: The information flow in the graph neural networks (GNNs) is fundamentally constrained by over-squashing, where structural bottlenecks impede long range information propagation. Graph-rewiring methods, which modify graph topology, have been extensively used to alleviate this. However, existing approaches often introduce prohibitive structural and computational bottlenecks, fail to preserve the critical properties of original graphs, and increase the edge counts massively. We introduce a novel method Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring , a group-theoretic rewiring method that augments the input graph with a Schreier-Coset graph derived from a special linear group. Our method provides theoretical guarantees, a graph that exhibits spectral gap and a bounded effective resistance, creating a low-resistance bypass for long-range communication. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that SCGR reduces effective resistance by 5-40% across various learning tasks, effectively mitigating connectivity bottlenecks while maintaining competitive accuracy.

AI.tldr: Introduces Schreier-Coset Graph Rewiring (SCGR), a group-theoretic graph augmentation using a Schreier-Coset graph from SL(n, q); reduces effective resistance and alleviates over-squashing while preserving accuracy.
AI.motivation: Over-squashing limits long-range information flow in GNNs; existing rewiring methods impose structural/computational bottlenecks and can distort original graphs; a principled, scalable rewiring with theoretical guarantees is desirable.
AI.method: Construct SCGR by augmenting the input graph with a Schreier-Coset graph derived from the special linear group; provide theoretical guarantees: spectral gap and bounded effective resistance, enabling a low-resistance bypass for long-range communication.
AI.result: Empirically reduces effective resistance by 5-40% across tasks; mitigates connectivity bottlenecks while maintaining competitive accuracy.
AI.conclusion: SCGR offers a principled, scalable graph augmentation that preserves essential properties and improves long-range information propagation in GNNs, with theoretical guarantees and empirical gains.

title: DS@GT ARC at ImageCLEFmedical 2026: Architectural Diversity for Concept Detection and Foundation-Model Scaling for Caption Prediction in Medical Image Analysis
summary: We describe the DS@GT submissions to the ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 challenge, which continues a long-running benchmark on the ROCOv2 dataset with two tracks: Concept Detection (Task 1), assigning UMLS Concept Unique Identifiers (CUIs) to radiology images, and Caption Prediction (Task 2), generating natural-language captions. For Task 1, our primary submission was a three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, and DenseNet-169 with a regularized ''Honest Threshold Tuning'' procedure designed to avoid validation overfitting on rare concepts; this submission ranked first on the official submission with a primary $F_1$ of $0.5790$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9657$. In parallel, we submitted a training-free KNN retrieval pipeline over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings, which reached a primary $F_1$ of $0.5780$ and a secondary $F_1$ of $0.9599$-essentially matching the fine-tuned ensemble on the primary track at a fraction of the cost. For Task 2, our submissions included a fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B model (overall $0.3571$, ranking third in the official submission), a fully fine-tuned BLIP pipeline with custom Vizwins merging ($0.3564$), and a zero-shot MedGemma-4B run with a PubMed-style prompt ($0.3186$), spanning a wide range of model scales and training costs. Code: https://github.com/dsgt-arc/imageclef-caption-2026.

AI.tldr: DS@GT's submission to ImageCLEFmedical Caption 2026 achieves top primary F1 on Task 1 (0.5790) with a three-way late fusion and competitive KNN retrieval (0.5780); Task 2 sees competitive results across model scales, with Gemma-3 27B at 0.3571 (3rd), BLIP + Vizwins at 0.3564, and MedGemma-4B zero-shot at 0.3186; code available.
AI.motivation: Extend the long-running ROCOv2 benchmark on radiology data by evaluating both a concept-detection track (CUIs) and a caption-generation track, enabling cross-task insights on model fusion, retrieval, and large-language-model captioning.
AI.method:
Task 1: three-way late-fusion ensemble of ConvNeXt-V2, BiomedCLIP ViT-B/16, DenseNet-169 with Honest Threshold Tuning; training-free KNN over frozen BiomedCLIP embeddings.
Task 2: fine-tuned Gemma-3 27B; fully fine-tuned BLIP with Vizwins merging; zero-shot MedGemma-4B with PubMed-style prompt.
AI.result: Task 1 primary F1=0.5790; secondary F1=0.9657; KNN primary F1=0.5780; secondary F1=0.9599. Task 2: Gemma-3 27B overall=0.3571 (rank 3); BLIP with Vizwins=0.3564; MedGemma-4B zero-shot=0.3186. Code: https://github.com/dsgt-arc/imageclef-caption-2026.
AI.conclusion: Ensembling with Honesty Threshold Tuning yields state-of-the-art Task 1 performance; a cost-efficient KNN approach nearly matches the ensemble. Task 2 results span a spectrum of model scales and training costs, showing competitive captioning performance across large and small models, with a public codebase.

title: Hidden APIs in Language Models: Discovering Reusable Causal Interfaces from Forked Futures
summary: Identical language-model answers can arise from hidden states that support different future computations, so current-answer probes do not establish a reusable internal interface. We introduce forked futures: future operations are sampled only after a prefix state has formed, and states are compared through the response distributions induced by those operations. This yields an empirical causal quotient over hidden states without requiring researcher-specified latent labels. Shared, Local, Mixture, and Distributed interfaces then compete under prequential causal description length subject to future-signature fidelity and matched capacity constraints. In the two detailed model evaluations, Shared has the lowest held-out description length, with gains of 0.216 nats on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.294 nats on Llama-3-8B, while maintaining tightly clustered mean future-signature distortion; a five-backbone sweep preserves the positive direction of Sharedness Gain. The figure-aligned transplantation analysis gives Shared the strongest joint target-correctness, locality, copy-preservation, and composite profile, and API-aligned paths mediate 0.749 of the target effect versus 0.150 for matched null paths. In the blind four-class model-organism test, 14/16 architectures are recovered, with one observed non-Shared to Shared error among 12 non-Shared organisms. These results support an economical reusable causal interface within the tested operation banks, while keeping the claim explicitly conditional on the candidate architectures, interventions, and held-out futures.

AI.tldr: Forked futures sample future operations after a prefix state to compare representations via induced response distributions, yielding a causal quotient over hidden states without latent labels. Across Shared, Local, Mixture, and Distributed interfaces, Shared achieves the best trade-off under prequential causal description length with strong future-signature fidelity; in two-model evaluations Shared minimizes held-out description length and preserves locality and transfer properties, and in a blind model-organism test, most architectures are recovered with few misclassifications.
AI.motivation: Address the problem that identical LM outputs can arise from different hidden-state computations, which undermines the identification of a reusable internal interface. The goal is to characterize interfaces between internal states and future computations without requiring explicit latent labels.
AI.method: Introduce forked futures. Sample future operations only after a prefix state forms; compare states by the response distributions induced by these operations. Define shared, local, mixture, and distributed interfaces. Use prequential causal description length subject to future-signature fidelity and capacity constraints to evaluate interfaces. Evaluate on two models (Qwen2.5-1.5B and Llama-3-8B) with a five-backbone sweep; perform figure-aligned transplantation analysis; conduct a blind four-class model-organism test to assess recoverability of architectures.
AI.result: Shared interface achieves the lowest held-out description length in both model evaluations (gains of 0.216 nats on Qwen2.5-1.5B and 0.294 nats on Llama-3-8B) while maintaining tightly clustered mean future-signature distortion. Five-backbone sweep preserves the positive Sharedness Gain. Transplantation analysis shows Shared yields strongest joint target-correctness, locality, copy-preservation, and composite profile; API-aligned paths mediate 0.749 of the target effect versus 0.150 for matched null paths. In the blind four-class model-organism test, 14/16 architectures are recovered with one non-Shared to Shared error among 12 non-Shared organisms.
AI.conclusion: The results support an economical reusable causal interface within the tested operation banks, with conclusions conditioned on the candidate architectures, interventions, and held-out futures.

title: Latent States in Neural Networks: Recovering the Temporal Structure of Drifting Data from Model Weights
summary: A temporally drifting data stream may pass through discrete regimes rather than changing continuously. We ask whether such regimes are recoverable from the weights of models trained on the stream, using a hidden Markov model (HMM) fit to the chronologically ordered trajectory of those weights. We study this question in two domains known to drift over time: multimodal misinformation detection, using the Fakeddit dataset; and sentiment analysis, using the Yelp dataset. We train classifiers on consecutive temporal windows and fit an HMM to the trajectory of their aligned weights, recovering latent states that partition each timeline into coherent phases. On both datasets, classifiers generalize better to data from windows sharing the state of their training window than to windows across state boundaries. This within-state transfer advantage survives a control for temporal proximity and modestly exceeds the advantage recovered by a naive partition into contiguous states of equal size. Although the states are estimated solely from model weights, they correlate more strongly with shifts in the data's class distribution than with the weight-space geometry used to estimate them. After class divergence and lag are residualized out, the within-state advantage exceeds its permutation null on both tasks, indicating that the states recover structure relevant to transfer beyond the data distribution. Every effect replicates on both tasks but is attenuated on Yelp, whose label distribution is more temporally stable.

AI.tldr: Hidden Markov model on the trajectory of model weights identifies discrete, temporally drifting regimes in two text-related tasks, enabling within-regime transfer that outperforms across-regime transfer and permutation baselines; the regimes align with data distribution shifts rather than weight-space geometry. Replicated on multimodal misinformation detection (Fakeddit) and sentiment analysis (Yelp), though effects are stronger when label distributions drift more.
AI.motivation: To determine whether discrete regimes under temporal drift can be recovered from the weights of models trained on a data stream, enabling better understanding of transfer dynamics and regime-aware training.
AI.method: Train classifiers on consecutive temporal windows for two tasks (Fakeddit and Yelp). Align and collect their weight trajectories across windows. Fit a hidden Markov model (HMM) to the chronologically ordered weight sequence to recover latent states (regimes). Evaluate generalization: within-state vs across-state transfer, controlling for temporal proximity; compare to partitioning data into equal-sized contiguous states; residualize effects of class divergence and lag; test significance against a permutation null. Also assess correlations between recovered states and data distribution shifts vs weight-space geometry.
AI.result: Latent states partition timelines into coherent phases. Classifiers generalize better to data from windows sharing the training state than across state boundaries. The within-state transfer advantage persists after controlling for temporal proximity and modestly exceeds equal-sized partition baselines. States correlate more with shifts in the data’s class distribution than with weight-space geometry used to estimate them. After residualizing class divergence and lag, within-state advantage remains above permutation null on both tasks, indicating transfer-relevant structure beyond data distribution. Effects replicate across tasks; attenuation observed on Yelp due to more temporally stable label distribution.
AI.conclusion: Weight trajectories via HMMs reveal discrete, transferable regimes in drifting streams that capture structure beyond simple data distribution changes. The approach succeeds across two domains, suggesting regime-aware analysis of model adaptation; the strength of effects depends on how rapidly label distributions drift.

title: Private Face Recognition Training Dataset Publication via Identity-Decoupled and Geometry-Preserving Face Distillation
summary: Publishing private face recognition~(FR) training datasets is privacy-sensitive because faces expose identity information. Private FR training dataset publication mitigates this risk by releasing protected proxies as substitutes for private training faces. However, training FR models with such data introduces an identity paradox: \emph{the identity cues that make released faces useful for recognition supervision are also the cues that make them linkable to real individuals.} A protected face should be decoupled from the original identity, yet still behave as a reliable identity sample for training. Removing these cues too aggressively may destroy the class structure needed for recognition learning, whereas preserving them too faithfully may increase source-identity linkability. We argue that this paradox stems from conflating source-aligned identity semantics with recognition-useful proxy identity geometry. The former should be suppressed to reduce linkage to private individuals, while the latter should be preserved for FR learning. Based on this insight, we propose \textbf{Private Face Distillation}, an identity-decoupling and geometry-preserving framework. It uses Orthogonal Geometry Preservation to construct decoupled proxy identities from private identity representations while maintaining hyperspherical geometry, and Relational Topology Alignment to preserve identity relations for recognition learning. Experiments across multiple domain-shifted FR scenarios show that Private Face Distillation achieves stronger utility than the evaluated publication baselines. On IJB-C surveillance, it improves $\mathrm{TAR}@\mathrm{FAR}{=}1\text{e-}{3}$ by 3.94\% over the baseline while reducing source-identity linkability. These results suggest that private FR training dataset publication should decouple source-identity correspondence while preserving proxy identity geometry.

AI.tldr: Private Face Distillation decouples source identity while preserving proxy geometry to enable private FR dataset publication with maintained recognition utility.
AI.motivation: To publish private FR training data without leaking identities, by decoupling identity semantics from recognition cues and preserving geometry for learning.
AI.method: Orthogonal Geometry Preservation to derive decoupled proxy identities while preserving hyperspherical geometry; Relational Topology Alignment to maintain intra-class relationships for learning.
AI.result: Outperforms baselines on domain-shifted FR tasks; TAR@FAR=1e-3 on IJB-C improves by 3.94% and reduces source-identity linkability.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling source-identity with geometry-preserving proxies enables private FR data publication without sacrificing recognition performance.

title: SCOPE: Synthetic Conditional Objectives for Policy Evolution in Black-Box Combinatorial Optimization
comment: 43 pages; Kiet, Duc, and Bang contributed equally
summary: Black-box combinatorial optimization requires systematically identifying high-quality solutions under a limited evaluation budget, yet the unknown objective function provides little guidance for deciding where the search should explore next. We introduce SCOPE, a general framework for Synthetic Conditional Objectives for Policy Evolution in Black-Box Combinatorial Optimization. Rather than directly optimizing the inaccessible objective, SCOPE learns a set of synthetic objectives conditioned on the accumulated search history, where each objective is designed to expose a distinct and potentially useful preference over candidate solutions. These objectives are then used to evolve search policies that generate diverse candidates, whose true quality is subsequently assessed through black-box evaluations. The outer loop adaptively updates and selects synthetic objectives according to how effectively their induced policies discover promising regions. In contrast, the inner loop returns a portfolio of top-performing policies to reduce the risk of relying on a single surrogate preference. This formulation reframes objective design as a mechanism for guiding policy exploration, enabling the search process to exploit observed evidence while maintaining structured diversity across discrete solution spaces. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmark problems demonstrate that SCOPE consistently improves black-box search performance under limited evaluation budgets and generalizes well across diverse combinatorial structures.

AI.tldr: SCOPE introduces Synthetic Conditional Objectives to guide search policies in black-box combinatorial optimization. It learns multiple synthetic objectives conditioned on search history, each exposing a distinct preference over candidates, and uses them to evolve diverse policies. An outer loop adaptively selects effective objectives; an inner loop returns a portfolio of top policies to reduce reliance on any single surrogate. This yields improved performance under limited evaluations and broad generalization across problem structures.
AI.motivation: In black-box combinatorial optimization the objective is unknown and evaluations are costly, making direct optimization infeasible. There is a need for a generic framework that guides exploration using surrogate preferences while preserving diversity and robustness across discrete search spaces.
AI.method: SCOPE defines an outer loop that (i) maintains a set of synthetic objectives conditioned on accumulated search history and (ii) adaptively selects among them based on their ability to drive discovery of promising regions. The inner loop optimizes multiple policies for the chosen synthetic objective, producing a portfolio of top-performing policies rather than a single surrogate. Policies generate candidate solutions which are evaluated by the true black-box objective, informing updates to both the objective set and policy selection.
AI.result: Empirical studies across multiple benchmarks show that SCOPE consistently improves black-box search performance under limited evaluation budgets and generalizes well across diverse combinatorial structures, outperforming baselines that rely on a single surrogate or non-diverse search strategies.
AI.conclusion: Recasting objective design as guidance for policy-driven exploration yields robust, diverse search behavior in black-box combinatorial optimization. SCOPE provides a general, adaptable framework for leveraging synthetic objectives to improve sample efficiency and generalization in discrete search spaces.

title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
summary: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (\textbf{PT-Flow}), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct \textbf{ODEWorld}, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. \href{https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/}{Project Website}.

AI.tldr: Introduces PT-Flow for a continuous latent velocity field governed by ordinary differential equations in physical time, and ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that mitigates representation collapse, enables arbitrary temporal resolution and backward prediction, and enhances planning for control; shows strong performance in video generation and robotics.
AI.motivation: Discrete-time world models are inefficient at capturing continuous physical dynamics and often suffer from representation collapse over long horizons. A continuous-time, well-structured latent space with ODE-based dynamics can better model physical processes and support planning.
AI.method: Learn a continuous latent velocity field in physical time, with dynamics parameterized by an ODE embedded in a structured latent space. Predictions are obtained by integrating the ODE with a solver. Build ODEWorld on PT-Flow by extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE-consistent properties on both the dynamical space and the latent velocity field to combat collapse. The model supports arbitrary time steps and backward prediction, and provides planning-oriented representations for downstream policy learning.
AI.result: ODEWorld yields high-quality long-horizon reconstructions, flexible temporal resolution (including backward time), and planning-friendly dynamics, excelling in video generation and robotic control tasks.
AI.conclusion: Continuous-time latent world modeling via ODE-based dynamics offers an efficient, versatile framework that reconciles accurate dynamics abstraction with visual realism and planning utility, as demonstrated by PT-Flow/ODEWorld and their empirical results.

title: A Lightweight Foundation Model for Collider Physics with Multi-Domain Adaptation
summary: We present a lightweight approach to foundation modeling (\textbf{NEXUS}) that leverages pre-trained learning from collider physics data towards out-of-domain tasks in other scientific datasets, using a fully connected autoencoder model with approximately 3 million parameters. The model pre-trains with no supervision over a large-scale collision dataset from the Large Hadron Collider modeled by charged particle track features. Downstream tasks for collider analyses, such as kinematic regression and event classification, are developed on pre-trained model weights and achieve improved accuracy with only small labeled datasets when compared to equivalent architectures trained from scratch. The benefits of pre-training are additionally investigated through latent space interpretation and application to other domains, including gravitational waves, flood forecasting, and neural activity. Furthermore, the relative computational simplicity of NEXUS is demonstrated compared to transformer approaches at comparable scale, opening the door to power-efficient inference and real-time or edge applications of foundation models in scientific experiments.

AI.tldr: A lightweight, autoencoder-based foundation model (NEXUS) trained on LHC collider data enables out-of-domain scientific tasks with minimal labeled data and low compute, showing competitive performance and potential edge deployment.
AI.motivation: Extend foundation-model benefits to data-rich but computation- or label-constrained scientific domains by using domain-specific unsupervised pretraining and compact architectures.
AI.method: Unsupervised pretraining of a fully connected autoencoder (~3M parameters) on large-scale charged-particle track features from LHC data; downstream tasks (kinematic regression, event classification) via pre-trained weights; latent-space analysis; cross-domain evaluation on gravitational waves, flood forecasting, and neural activity; comparison to transformer baselines highlighting computational efficiency.
AI.result: Improved downstream accuracy with small labeled datasets compared to scratch-trained architectures; interpretable latent representations; evidence of cross-domain transferability; lighter computation than transformers at similar scale enabling potential real-time/edge use.
AI.conclusion: Domain-specific, compact autoencoder pretraining can yield effective, transferable foundation models for scientific data, offering efficiency and practicality advantages over transformer-based approaches; encourages broader exploration of autoencoder-based foundation models in diverse scientific domains.

title: CXR-Retrieve: Compositional Text-to-Image Retrieval in Chest Radiography
summary:
Large chest radiography archives are difficult to search because most studies are paired only with free-text reports rather than structured clinical annotations. Vision-language models offer a natural interface for text-to-image retrieval, but current biomedical models are primarily optimized for report-to-image matching rather than for satisfying short clinical search queries. This creates an objective mismatch: a model may retrieve images related to words in the query while failing to satisfy the full clinical constraint, especially for conjunctions and negations such as ``atelectasis and no pneumonia.''
  We introduce CXR-Retrieve, a structured benchmark for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval. The benchmark contains 5,159 test images from the official test-split of MIMIC-CXR-JPG and 145 textual queries spanning single and conjunction findings, both positive and negative. Relevance is defined by whether a retrieved image satisfies all asserted pathology constraints, rather than by whether it matches a paired report.
  We further propose a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective for clinical retrieval. Our method attracts image-text pairs with compatible asserted pathology constraints, including shared confirmed absences, while explicitly repelling contradictory pairs. Starting from the in-domain CXR-CLIP checkpoint, our method improves Precision@5 over CXR-CLIP by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and by 22.0 percentage points on negation queries. These results show that reliable chest X-ray retrieval requires training objectives that model not only which findings are mentioned, but also how they are clinically asserted.

AI.tldr: Introduces CXR-Retrieve, a benchmark and label-aware fine-tuning method for compositional chest X-ray text-to-image retrieval, addressing the mismatch between query semantics and report-based training.
AI.motivation: Current biomedical vision-language models optimize for report-to-image matching and fail to satisfy complex clinical search queries (e.g., conjunctions, negations). There is a need for benchmarks and training objectives that reflect clinical constraints.
AI.method: Proposes CXR-Retrieve with 5,159 test images from MIMIC-CXR-JPG test split and 145 textual queries (single, conjunctions, positive/negative). Relevance requires fulfilling all asserted pathology constraints. Introduces a label-aware contrastive fine-tuning objective starting from an in-domain CXR-CLIP, pairing compatible constraints and repelling contradictions.
AI.result: Starting from CXR-CLIP, the method improves Precision@5 by 8.5 percentage points on two-pathology conjunctions and 22.0 points on negation queries.
AI.conclusion: Reliable chest X-ray retrieval demands training objectives that model both which findings are mentioned and how they are clinically asserted; the proposed benchmark and objective yield substantial gains on conjunction and negation retrieval tasks.

title: ReDiPPO: Reference-Guided Value Calibration and Discrepancy-Aware Token Reweighting for Mathematical Reasoning
summary: Reinforcement learning has emerged as an effective paradigm for enhancing the mathematical reasoning capabilities of large language models. Among existing policy optimization methods, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) remains particularly appealing because its learned critic can, in principle, provide token-level credit assignment. However, in mathematical reasoning tasks characterized by long reasoning horizons and sparse outcome rewards, reliable token-level credit assignment remains challenging. The standard critic often fails to accurately evaluate intermediate reasoning states, resulting in noisy advantage estimates and suboptimal policy updates. In this paper, we propose ReDiPPO, a Reference-guided and Discrepancy-aware PPO framework for mathematical reasoning. ReDiPPO introduces a reference-guided critic that uses reference answers as training-time privileged signals to provide more accurate value estimation. Meanwhile, it retains a standard critic and quantifies the token-level reference-standard discrepancy between the standard value estimate and the reference-guided value estimate. This discrepancy serves as an indicator of difficult reasoning states and is used to reweight the corresponding token-level advantages during PPO optimization. Extensive experiments on diverse mathematical reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that ReDiPPO improves value-estimation accuracy and consistently outperforms strong policy optimization baselines, including PPO, DAPO, and GSPO, in final reasoning performance. Our code is available on https://github.com/cii030/ReDiPPO.

AI.tldr: ReDiPPO proposes a reference-guided and discrepancy-aware PPO framework to improve token-level credit assignment in long-horizon mathematical reasoning by using privileged reference answers to guide value estimation and reweighting token-level advantages.
AI.motivation: Token-level credit assignment is difficult in long-horizon mathematical reasoning with sparse rewards. Standard critics provide noisy estimates, hindering policy updates.
AI.method: Introduce a reference-guided critic that leverages reference answers as privileged signals for value estimation, alongside a standard critic. Compute the discrepancy between the two value estimates to identify difficult reasoning states and reweight token-level advantages in PPO accordingly.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on diverse mathematical reasoning benchmarks shows improved value-estimation accuracy and consistent improvement over strong baselines (PPO, DAPO, GSPO) in final reasoning performance.
AI.conclusion: Reference-guided value estimation plus discrepancy-aware reweighting effectively enhances token-level credit assignment in math reasoning with PPO, yielding better final performance and reliable value estimates; code is released.

title: Filling the Pareto-Optimal Front for Affordance Segmentation on Embedded Devices Using RGB-D Cameras
summary: While depth sensors have the potential to complement RGB data for affordance segmentation in wearable robots, their usage seems to remain underexplored. The paper proposes two approaches: a reformulated version of hardware-aware neural architecture search, endowed with a newly designed search space to integrate depth (D) information into small-sized deep networks, and a dedicated fine-tuning approach, including a preprocessing layer to merge depth information with RGB data and make it compatible with conventional architectures. In both cases, those methods aim to generate solutions that benefit from modern (portable) hardware accelerators and overcome existing tiny-like approaches, which often fail to tackle critical scenarios due to the severe constraints set by the supporting hardware. Extensive experiments on a pair of real-world datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method as compared with existing solutions. The approach presented in the paper generates, in most cases, solutions that identify the Pareto optimal front to balance generalization performance and hardware requirements. The paper also describes the supporting prototype, including a Jetson Nano board and a RealSense RGB-D camera. When considering the energy profile of the device, the overall system can attain real-time performances within an energy budget that is compatible with standard batteries, such as those used in smartphones.

AI.tldr: Two hardware-aware approaches for RGB-D affordance segmentation on wearables: NAS with depth-aware search space and a depth-RGB fusion fine-tuning layer, achieving Pareto-optimal energy/accuracy trade-offs on Jetson Nano with RealSense, enabling real-time performance within smartphone-like energy budgets.
AI.motivation: Leverage depth data to improve affordance segmentation in wearable robots while satisfying strict on-board compute and energy constraints; existing tiny models underperform in critical scenarios; need hardware-aware methods that exploit accelerators.
AI.method: 1) Reformulated hardware-aware NAS with a depth-integrated search space to design small networks that leverage depth; 2) A dedicated fine-tuning approach with a preprocessing layer to fuse depth with RGB to produce inputs compatible with standard architectures.
AI.result: Experiments on two real-world datasets show the methods often achieve Pareto-optimal front between accuracy/generalization and hardware metrics; prototype demonstration on Jetson Nano and RealSense; system achieves real-time performance under energy budgets comparable to smartphone batteries.
AI.conclusion: Depth-aware, hardware-conscious design is effective for RGB-D affordance segmentation in wearables; practical for portable accelerators; the two approaches offer complementary means to balance performance and hardware constraints; potential for deployment on consumer devices.

title: Sparsity Induced Identifiability in Matrix Tri-Factorisation
summary: Matrix factorisation is a fundamental tool for exploiting low-dimensional structure in high-dimensional data, with applications such as data compression, denoising, structure discovery, interpretable representation learning, and dimensionality reduction. Compared to conventional two-factor models, matrix tri-factorisation provides greater modelling flexibility, while sparsity constraints often improve both interpretability and recovery performance. Although the role of sparsity has been extensively studied for two-factor matrix factorisation, rigorous theoretical guarantees for general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation remain largely unexplored. To address this gap, we establish, to the best of our knowledge, the first rigorous theoretical study for sparsity-induced identifiability in general real-valued matrix tri-factorisation. Our analysis is enabled by a novel decomposition strategy that transforms the original problem into two coupled auxiliary factorisation problems, while preserving the structural information necessary to the recovery of the original factor matrices from the observations. Building upon this decomposition, we derive recovery guarantees and structural consistency results that characterise how coefficient sparsity influences the sufficient recovery conditions, convergence behaviour, spectral approximation error, high-probability bounds, and structure preservation. Comprehensive Monte Carlo experiments validate the proposed theory and demonstrate close agreement between the theoretical results and empirical observations.

title: FDDWAN: A Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Network for Watermarking Attack
summary: Existing invisible watermark removal methods often struggle to accurately capture the watermark-bearing features, leading to an unfavorable trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity. In this paper, we propose the Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Watermark Attack Network (FDDWAN), a coarse-to-fine framework that performs watermark removal through wavelet-domain decomposition and residual diffusion refinement. In the initial stage, the Wavelet-based Frequency-domain Preliminary Attack Module (WFPAM) decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands and applies frequency-specific attack strategies tailored to their respective contributions to watermark robustness and perceptual quality. In the next stage, the Frequency-domain Residual Diffusion Attack Module (FRDAM) separately models the residual distributions between the preliminarily attacked outputs and the corresponding watermark-free references during training. Rather than reconstructing the entire image, FRDAM selectively refines frequency-domain residuals, directing the diffusion process toward the remaining watermark related discrepancies while minimizing modifications to image content. Extensive experiments on CelebA and ImageNet across four representative watermarking schemes demonstrate that FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attack methods.

AI.tldr: Proposes Frequency-Decoupled Diffusion Watermark Attack Network (FDDWAN), a two-stage wavelet-domain diffusion framework that improves watermark removal while preserving perceptual quality, validated on CelebA and ImageNet across four watermarking schemes.
AI.motivation: Existing invisible watermark removal methods struggle to accurately capture watermark-bearing features, leading to an unfavorable trade-off between watermark suppression and perceptual fidelity. A frequency-aware, coarse-to-fine approach can target watermark cues more precisely without over-editing the image.
AI.method: Stage 1 WFPAM (Wavelet-based Frequency-domain Preliminary Attack Module): decomposes the watermarked image into low- and high-frequency subbands via wavelets and applies frequency-specific attack strategies that leverage their distinct contributions to watermark robustness and perceptual quality. Stage 2 FRDAM (Frequency-domain Residual Diffusion Attack Module): models the residual distributions between preliminarily attacked outputs and watermark-free references; diffusion refinement focuses on frequency-domain residuals, guiding edits toward remaining watermark-related discrepancies while minimizing changes to content.
AI.result: Empirical results on CelebA and ImageNet across four representative watermarking schemes show FDDWAN achieves a more favorable trade-off between watermark removal effectiveness and visual fidelity than conventional and learning-based attack methods.
AI.conclusion: FDDWAN demonstrates the effectiveness of a frequency-decoupled, diffusion-based, coarse-to-fine framework for watermark removal. It achieves improved trade-offs and suggests potential for generalization, though considerations include generalization to unseen schemes and the method’s computational cost and reliance on accurate watermark-free references.

title: HealthCAT: An Interpretable Encoder-only Transformer Framework for Health Indicator Prediction and Temporal Interpretation of Wearable Sensor Data
summary: Wearable sensors continuously capture fine-grained multivariate time-series data, providing opportunities to model behavioural patterns associated with health outcomes. However, existing deep learning methods prioritise predictive accuracy over interpretability, limiting their application in health research. In this study, we present HealthCAT, a flexible framework that integrates an Encoder-only Transformer with an Attentive Class Activation Token (AttentiveCAT) to generate class-specific, time-step-level interpretations. These interpretations can be mapped back onto behavioural cycles that are relevant to the domain (e.g., time-of-day), supporting individual-level analysis of wearable sensor data. We evaluated HealthCAT using two real-world wearable sensor datasets (306 participants in total). HealthCAT outperformed deep learning baselines by up to 17\% in F1-score and 12\% in accuracy on both datasets ($p<0.05$). In masking experiments, the time steps identified by HealthCAT carried significantly more predictive value than random selection across all masking conditions ($p<0.05$), indicating that the identified time steps are predictively informative. By coupling predictive performance with validated time-step-level interpretability, HealthCAT moves wearable sensor analysis beyond aggregated metrics towards temporal patterns that support health monitoring, behavioural pattern analysis, and intervention design in health research. The significance of this work is that it enables accurate prediction of health indicators from wearable sensor data while providing insights into when and how physical activity patterns occur, rather than relying solely on aggregated summary measures.

AI.tldr: HealthCAT combines an Encoder-only Transformer with an Attentive Class Activation Token to produce class-specific, time-step-level explanations for wearable sensor time-series, achieving strong predictive performance and interpretable temporal patterns aligned with behavioural cycles.
AI.motivation: Address the interpretability gap in deep learning for wearable sensor data by delivering class-specific, time-resolved explanations that map onto domain-relevant cycles (e.g., time-of-day).
AI.method: Introduce HealthCAT: an Encoder-only Transformer architecture augmented with Attentive Class Activation Token (AttentiveCAT) to generate time-step-level, class-specific interpretability. Interpretations are mapped to behavioural cycles relevant to the domain. Evaluated on two real-world wearable datasets (n=306). Compared against deep learning baselines. Conducted masking experiments to assess the predictive value of identified time steps.
AI.result: HealthCAT outperformed baselines by up to 17% in F1-score and 12% in accuracy with p<0.05 on both datasets. Time steps highlighted by HealthCAT showed significantly higher predictive value than random across masking conditions (p<0.05).
AI.conclusion: By coupling strong predictive performance with validated time-step-level interpretability, HealthCAT advances wearable sensor analysis from aggregated metrics to temporally-resolved patterns, enabling improved health monitoring, behavioural analysis, and intervention design.

title: QQWorld: Quantile-Quantile Matching for World Model Regularization
summary: Latent world models enable efficient planning by predicting future states in a compact representation space, but their performance depends critically on the quality of the learned latent distribution. LeWorldModel (LeWM) regularizes its latents toward an isotropic Gaussian using the Epps-Pulley (EP) objective. We show that the corrective gradients of EP rapidly vanish for isolated tail samples, leaving heavy-tailed deviations insufficiently controlled. To address this limitation, we propose QQWorld, which replaces EP with a quantile-quantile matching objective that directly aligns projected latent samples with rank-matched Gaussian quantiles, thereby maintaining effective corrective gradients in the tails. We further develop cross-batch QQ, which enlarges the effective ranking pool using detached samples from previous batches, and characterize its bias-variance trade-off. Across four control environments, QQWorld effectively improves the average planning success rate of LeWM, while consistently yielding better Gaussian alignment and thinner latent tails.

AI.tldr: QQWorld replaces Epps-Pulley with a quantile-quantile matching objective to align latent samples with Gaussian quantiles, maintaining corrective gradients in tails; cross-batch QQ enlarges the ranking pool and reveals a bias-variance trade-off.
AI.motivation: Epps-Pulley (EP) regularization can cause corrective gradients to vanish for isolated tail samples, leaving heavy-tailed latent deviations under-regularized; robust tail control in latent space is crucial for reliable planning with latent world models.
AI.method: Replace the EP objective with a quantile-quantile (QQ) matching objective that directly aligns projected latent samples with rank-matched Gaussian quantiles. Develop cross-batch QQ by using detached samples from previous batches to enlarge the effective ranking pool and analyze the resulting bias-variance trade-off.
AI.result: In four control environments, QQWorld improves the average planning success rate of LeWM, yields better Gaussian alignment, and produces thinner latent tails.
AI.conclusion: QQWorld provides effective latent-space Gaussian alignment and improved planning performance; the cross-batch QQ variant offers insight into the bias-variance dynamics and can further enhance or complicate regularization depending on batch composition.

title: Expanding Data-Agnostic Pivotal Instances Selection Models with Proximity Trees and Ensemble Learning
summary: As decision-making processes grow more complex, machine learning tools have become essential for tackling business and societal challenges. However, many existing methods rely on decision-making procedures that are difficult to interpret. Since humans naturally make decisions by comparing new cases with a few representative examples, we aim to design an approach that selects such pivots to construct an interpretable predictive model. Inspired by decision trees, we propose a hierarchical, interpretable-by-design pivot selection model based on the similarity between pivots and input instances. Our method functions both as a pivot selection technique and a standalone predictive model. Extending beyond single pivots, we incorporate pairs of pivots that are used by proximity and oblique trees, as well as ensembles, which enhance the versatility and effectiveness of our proposal. Additionally, our approach is data modality-agnostic, leveraging pre-trained networks for data transformation. Experiments across diverse datasets, including tabular data, text, images, and time series, demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, outperforming alternative instance selection strategies and achieving competitive results against state-of-the-art interpretable models while maintaining a minimal number of pivots.

AI.tldr: A hierarchical, pivot-based, interpretable predictive model that selects representative pivots (and pivot pairs) via similarity to inputs; data-agnostic and extensible to ensembles, achieving competitive performance across diverse data modalities with few pivots.
AI.motivation: Improve ML interpretability by aligning decision logic with human-like case-based reasoning (comparing to representative examples) and reduce reliance on opaque procedures.
AI.method: Propose a pivot selection framework inspired by decision trees; uses similarity between pivots and inputs to build a predictor; supports single pivots, pivot pairs for proximity and oblique trees, ensembles; data-modality agnostic through pre-trained feature transforms.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation on tabular, text, image, and time-series data shows superior pivot-selection efficiency and competitive accuracy against state-of-the-art interpretable models while using a minimal number of pivots and outperforming other instance-selection strategies.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates a versatile, interpretable pivot-based modeling paradigm that generalizes across modalities, with potential for deeper ensembles and richer pivot representations, offering a practical balance between interpretability and predictive performance.

title: LoMeVQA: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Longitudinal Medical VQA
comment: 23 pages, 17 figures, 7 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA
summary: In clinical practice, patients often undergo multiple imaging examinations over successive visits, yielding longitudinal data. Modeling such temporal information is crucial for reliable assessment of disease progression and treatment response. However, despite the rapid advancement of multimodal large language models (MLLMs), longitudinal medical visual reasoning remains largely underexplored. To fill this gap, we propose LoMeVQA, a comprehensive benchmark consisting of 206K longitudinal visual question answering (VQA) pairs for temporal medical image analysis. LoMeVQA covers five tasks: progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, and differential region description. To construct the dataset, we develop an automated pipeline that (1) organizes patient records chronologically, (2) extracts clinically meaningful entities via a medical knowledge graph, and (3) models their temporal evolution to guide large language models in generating high-quality longitudinal VQA pairs. Extensive evaluations demonstrate that both general-purpose and medical-domain MLLMs perform poorly on LoMeVQA, revealing substantial limitations in temporal reasoning. To address these limitations, we introduce MedLong-8B, which achieves state-of-the-art performance across all tasks. Beyond benchmarking, we conduct detailed analyses that uncover key failure modes and shed light on how to improve longitudinal medical visual reasoning. Our data is available at: https://github.com/pepperbubble/LoMeVQA

AI.tldr: A new LoMeVQA benchmark with 206K longitudinal medical VQA pairs across five tasks; introduces MedLong-8B; general MLLMs underperform on temporal medical reasoning; dataset release provided.
AI.motivation: Longitudinal imaging is crucial for tracking disease progression and treatment response, but multimodal large language models struggle with temporal reasoning in medical settings; there is a lack of scale datasets for longitudinal VQA.
AI.method: An automated pipeline orders patient records, extracts entities via a medical knowledge graph, and models temporal evolution to guide LLMs in generating high-quality longitudinal VQA pairs. LoMeVQA covers five tasks: progress classification, progress description, progress report generation, differential region grounding, and differential region description. MedLong-8B (8B parameters) is proposed to achieve state-of-the-art performance.
AI.result: Extensive evaluations show both general-purpose and medical-domain MLLMs perform poorly on LoMeVQA, indicating significant gaps in temporal reasoning. MedLong-8B achieves state-of-the-art results across all five tasks. Detailed analyses identify common failure modes and provide guidance for improving longitudinal medical visual reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The dataset and the MedLong-8B model advance longitudinal medical visual reasoning and benchmarking. The LoMeVQA data is publicly available at the linked GitHub repository.

title: Latent-Kernel Discrete Flow Maps for Few-Step Generation
summary: Discrete diffusion and flow-matching models denoise a sequence over many steps, but to keep each step cheap, they factorize the transition across positions and decide every token independently. This makes few-step generation challenging for text when the target couples two positions, such as a subject and a verb that must agree. An independent update commits to them separately, and many function evaluations are spent repairing the mismatch. Existing few-step methods buy back the lost correlation by distilling or rectifying a slow teacher, and so inherit the teacher's quality ceiling. We ask instead whether a model can express correlated steps natively, and answer with Latent-Kernel Discrete Flow Maps (LKF), a from-scratch flow-map kernel that is a mixture of M factorized components tied by a single shared latent. Conditioned on the latent, each component is cheap, and the mixture is summed over the latent in closed form for small M. We show that a single step places mass on correlated completions with the same sampling time complexity as a factorized model, since one latent is drawn per sequence and reused across the entire denoising trajectory. We also show that the Masked Diffusion Language Model (MDLM) is a special case of our LKF model at M=1. The experiments for unconditional text generation on the One-Billion-Word (LM1B) and WikiText-103 benchmarks show that our LKF model learns strongly heterogeneous components and improves generative perplexity by 2.1x to 3.3x over the likelihood baselines without losing diversity. The gain grows with M, and at M=8, it surpasses distilled and rectified few-step samplers. The source code is available at: https://github.com/mansoor181/lkf.git

AI.tldr: Latent-Kernel Discrete Flow Maps (LKF) jointly model position correlations in discrete diffusion for text, enabling few-step generation without external teachers; MDLM is the M=1 case.
