AI.motivation: Overcome the limitation of independently updated tokens in discrete diffusion for text, which hurts multi-position coherence (e.g., subject-verb agreement) and often relies on slow teacher distillation/rectification.
AI.method: Introduce LKF: a mixture of M factorized flow-map components tied by a shared latent. Conditioning on the latent makes components cheap; the mixture is summable in closed form for small M; one latent is reused across an entire denoising trajectory. MDLM is a special case with M=1.
AI.result: One-step sampling places mass on correlated completions with the same time complexity as a factorized model; LKF learns heterogeneous components; perplexity improves 2.1x–3.3x over likelihood baselines without sacrificing diversity; gains grow with M, and M=8 surpasses distilled/rectified few-step samplers.
AI.conclusion: LKF provides a native mechanism to capture cross-position correlations in discrete diffusion for text, enabling more efficient, higher-quality few-step generation without teacher reliance; MDLM is embedded as a special case; code available at the referenced GitHub repository.

title: SPFM-Net: Semantic-Prior-Guided Frequency-Constrained Mamba for Invisible Watermark Attack
summary: Existing watermark attacks typically rely on predefined signal-processing operations or locally constrained restoration networks, making it difficult to capture the long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals and resulting in an unfavorable trade-off between removal effectiveness and visual fidelity. In this paper, we propose SPFM-Net, a semantic-prior-guided and frequency-constrained Mamba framework for invisible watermark attack. SPFM-Net first employs high-ratio masking to disrupt the spatial coherence of invisible watermark signals, and then utilizes a partially fine-tuned pretrained Masked Autoencoder to reconstruct semantically consistent image from sparse observations while suppressing watermark-related information. A Multi-scale Residual Frequency Feature Interaction module subsequently aggregates watermark-related residual features across multiple receptive fields, while adaptively suppressing responses from watermark-irrelevant regions. To further capture the long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals, a lightweight Mamba-based Global State-space Feature Modeling (GSFM) unit is introduced to separate watermark-related features from natural image content and suppress the remaining watermark traces. In addition, SPFM-Net is optimized using a multi-level objective that jointly imposes spatial-, frequency-, and edge-domain constraints, enabling effective watermark suppression while preserving perceptual quality. Extensive experiments on representative spatial-domain, transform-domain, orthogonal moment-based, and deep learning-based watermarking schemes demonstrate that SPFM-Net achieves a favorable trade-off between watermark attack effectiveness and perceptual fidelity.

AI.tldr: SPFM-Net is a semantic-prior-guided, frequency-constrained watermark attack framework that suppresses invisible watermarks while preserving perceptual quality, using masking, a partially fine-tuned Masked Autoencoder, a Multi-scale Residual Frequency Feature Interaction module, a GSFM unit, and multi-level spatial-, frequency-, and edge-domain constraints to handle long-range, globally distributed watermark signals across various schemes.
AI.motivation: Existing watermark attacks rely on predefined signal-processing operations or locally constrained restoration networks, which fail to capture long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals and force a trade-off between removal effectiveness and visual fidelity.
AI.method: SPFM-Net employs (1) high-ratio masking to disrupt spatial coherence of watermark signals; (2) a partially fine-tuned pretrained Masked Autoencoder (MAE) to reconstruct semantically consistent images from sparse observations while suppressing watermark information; (3) a Multi-scale Residual Frequency Feature Interaction module to aggregate watermark-related residuals across multiple receptive fields and suppress watermark-irrelevant regions; (4) a lightweight Mamba-based Global State-space Feature Modeling (GSFM) unit to capture long-range dependencies and separate watermark-related features from natural content; (5) a multi-level objective enforcing spatial-, frequency-, and edge-domain constraints to balance suppression and perceptual quality.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on representative spatial-domain, transform-domain, orthogonal moment-based, and deep learning-based watermarking schemes demonstrate that SPFM-Net achieves a favorable trade-off between watermark attack effectiveness and perceptual fidelity.
AI.conclusion: SPFM-Net effectively suppresses invisible watermark traces while preserving perceptual quality, addressing long-range dependencies of globally distributed watermark signals across diverse watermarking schemes.

title: Evaluating and Pricing Advertisements in AI-Generated Responses
summary: As search increasingly shifts toward LLM-driven answer engines, advertising is becoming embedded within the generated response itself and should therefore be evaluated for both user utility and commercial value. The key challenge is click-through intent: behavioural logs are unavailable, human annotation resists calibration, and frontier LLM judges conflate intent with linguistic fluency. These gaps compound, as principled pricing presupposes a continuous intent signal, while generating such a signal presupposes supervision that is currently unavailable. We construct the missing supervision through a psychologically grounded agent simulation framework, and distil it into a parameter-efficient evaluator that predicts click-through intent, together with the three companion dimensions of ad quality, as smooth, differentiable estimates. Validated through sign-certain behavioural perturbations, the evaluator surpasses frontier zero-shot judges on relevance sensitivity (79% versus 60-67%), tracks graded content degradation, generalises without error to 103 fictional products, and agrees with human preference in 86% of pairwise judgements across five annotators, with agreement rising in the evaluator's confidence. Upon its estimates we build the pricing layer directly, deriving the unique payment rule under which truthful bidding is optimal, demonstrating it on a best-of-k allocation, and extending the mechanism to non-monotone allocations. The same differentiable signal stands ready as a training objective for ad generation.

AI.tldr: Introduces a differentiable evaluator of click-through intent and ad quality, built from a simulation-based supervision framework, enabling truthful auction-based pricing for ads embedded in LLM outputs; demonstrates superior alignment with human judgments, broad generalization, and applicability to ad generation training.
AI.motivation: As ads appear within LLM-generated answers, there is a need for user-centric and monetization signals; current logs and judgments fail to produce a continuous, reliable supervision signal for pricing; there is a gap between intent and linguistic fluency; a principled pricing mechanism requires continuous intent signal.
AI.method: Construct psychologically grounded agent simulation to generate supervision; distill into a parameter-efficient evaluator predicting click-through intent plus ad-quality dimensions (smooth, differentiable). Validate via sign-certain perturbations; compare to frontier zero-shot judges; test on 103 fictional products; evaluate human-preference agreement across five annotators; build pricing layer deriving truthful bidding in best-of-k allocations, extend to non-monotone allocations; propose differentiable signal as training objective for ad generation.
AI.result: Evaluator achieves higher relevance sensitivity (79% vs 60-67%), tracks content degradation, generalizes to 103 fictional products without error, aligns with human preferences in 86% of pairwise judgments, with higher agreement as confidence grows; pricing rule yields truthful bidding optimization; demonstration on best-of-k; extended to non-monotone allocations; differentiable signal suitable for training ads.
AI.conclusion: This framework provides a practical, differentiable, supervision-derived signal for ad valuation in LLM outputs, enabling truthful auctions and scalable ad generation, with broad generalization and alignment to human preferences.

title: When Does Explicit View Routing Work? A Controlled Study of Multi-View Graph-Text Alignment
summary: Graph-text retrieval typically maps a graph and its description to a single embedding, even when a query concerns only one semantic aspect, such as a class label or molecular property. Multiple heads can separate these aspects, but a change in the query head may alter retrieval even when the wrong text is sent to that head. Such behavior demonstrates architectural channelization, not necessarily semantic routing. We examine the conditions under which this distinction can be resolved. Our controlled version of MV-GTA uses deterministic, verifiable text segments; isolated text encoders; view-specific graph heads; and relevance derived from external labels or RDKit descriptors. Correct routing and per-sample derangements form a causal test of whether retrieval depends on content. On BBBP and BACE, correct routing improves label and property nDCG by 0.305 to 0.685 over deranged training. The expected graph head exceeds the best wrong head by 0.303 to 0.453. Topology does not specialize consistently across the two datasets. In a matched three-seed comparison, one joint model obtains mean topology, label, and property nDCG of 0.720/1.000/0.877; three separately trained Single specialists obtain 0.633/0.976/0.859. Property paraphrase augmentation also improves unseen-template nDCG by 0.140 and 0.147 over a matched-exposure canonical control. Consistency and hard-template extensions, however, reduce canonical retrieval in some settings. The evidence is therefore limited to explicit, externally grounded label and property routing and observed multi-interface consolidation. It does not establish free-form routing, consistent three-view specialization, statistical equivalence to specialists, or superior downstream prediction.

AI.tldr: This work investigates whether multi-head graph-text retrieval truly routes by content (semantic aspects) or remains architectural channelization; using a controlled MV-GTA setup with deterministic text segments, isolated encoders, view-specific graph heads, and external-label relevance; finds limited evidence for free-form routing, but explicit routing to external labels/properties yields measurable gains; results show joint models can outperform single-specialists on some metrics, but topology is inconsistent; augmentation helps unseen templates yet sometimes hurts canonical retrieval; overall evidence supports explicit routing only under strong external grounding.
AI.motivation: To distinguish semantic routing from mere architectural channelization in multi-head graph-text retrieval and to establish causal tests for content-based routing.
AI.method: Propose a controlled variant of MV-GTA with deterministic segments, isolated encoders, view-specific graph heads, and relevance derived from external labels or RDKit descriptors; use per-sample derangements as a causal test; evaluate on BBBP and BACE; compare joint model vs single specialists; test property paraphrase augmentation; examine topology specialization and three-seed matched comparisons.
AI.result: Correct routing improves label/property nDCG by 0.305–0.685 over deranged training; expected graph head exceeds best wrong head by 0.303–0.453; joint model achieves 0.720/1.000/0.877 vs 0.633/0.976/0.859 for single specialists; paraphrase augmentation improves unseen-template nDCG by 0.140/0.147; topology inconsistent; hard-template and consistency reductions in some settings.
AI.conclusion: Evidence supports externally grounded routing; does not establish free-form routing, universal three-view specialization, or superior downstream prediction.

title: Hallucinations Leave a Grounding Signature:Verifier-Guided Decoding for Selective Object Correction
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) often hallucinate objects that are absent from an image. Despite recent progress, existing mitigation methods still lack reliable object-level grounding diagnostics and therefore tend to apply coarse-grained interventions, which can impair visual understanding, shorten responses, and reduce coverage of genuinely grounded objects. The key challenge is thus to detect, during generation, whether each emerging object mention is supported by reliable visual evidence, so that hallucination can be mitigated selectively. Yet output confidence reflects next-token plausibility rather than visual support, allowing language priors to make absent objects appear certain. We show that the missing diagnostic evidence is encoded in an Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS), a distributed signed attention pattern that remains informative for such confident hallucinations. Based on IGS, we propose Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD), a decoding framework in which a lightweight verifier examines each emerging object mention, rolls back the KV cache when the mention is identified as high risk, suppresses the object and its synonyms, and regenerates the affected continuation. Because VGD intervenes only on object mentions identified as high risk, it reduces object hallucination while preserving the model's original visual understanding and grounded object coverage. Experiments on CHAIR and AMBER-G show that VGD achieves state-of-the-art object hallucination reduction: at @rec90, it cuts AMBER-G CHAIR by 43.6\% while retaining 99.6\% of grounded-object coverage, and reduces CHAIR-MSCOCO CHAIR$_i$/CHAIR$_s$ by 37.0\%/30.4\% without shortening captions.

AI.tldr: Proposes Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS) and Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD) to mitigate object hallucinations in large vision-language models by per-mention verification; achieves strong reduction with minimal loss of grounded-object coverage.
AI.motivation: Current mitigation methods rely on coarse, post-hoc interventions and model confidence is misaligned with true visual support, making reliable object-level grounding diagnostics essential for selective suppression of hallucinations.
AI.method: Intrinsic Grounding Signature (IGS) is a distributed signed attention pattern that encodes missing diagnostic evidence for grounded objects. Verifier-Guided Decoding (VGD) uses a lightweight verifier to inspect emerging object mentions during generation, roll back the KV cache when high-risk mentions are detected, suppress the object and synonyms, and regenerate the affected continuation, thus preserving grounded understanding while reducing hallucinations.
AI.result: State-of-the-art object hallucination reduction: at rec90, reduction by 43.6% for AMBER-G CHAIR with 99.6% of grounded-object coverage retained; CHAIR-MSCOCO CHAIR_i/CHAIR_s reductions by 37.0% and 30.4% respectively, without shortening captions.
AI.conclusion: VGD enables selective, minimally invasive mitigation of object hallucinations by verifying emerging mentions with a lightweight verifier, preserving visual understanding and grounded object coverage.

title: Rehearse: Stepping Back from the Confidence Cliff in Self-Improving Autoresearch
summary: Autoresearch improves machine-learning code by proposing changes, running full training jobs, and keeping changes that improve the metric. The efficiency of this loop depends not only on generating ideas, but also on the agent's ability to decide, before spending a training run, whether a proposed modification is likely to work. We study how the reliability of this pre-execution judgment changes over the course of an autoresearch trajectory. In public AutoSOTA logs (Li et al., 2026; Tsinghua FIB Lab, 2026), the fraction of helpful modifications falls from 70% in the first two iterations to 43% by iteration 6+. On 296 same-baseline modification pairs from 39 paper-derived AutoSOTA tasks, each containing one modification that improved the metric and one that did not, with measured outcomes hidden, an LLM judge given candidate rationales but no prior-attempt history reaches 79.5% accuracy on the pairs where strict consensus returns a verdict. On the full 366-pair benchmark, however, this ability weakens substantially late in the loop. As successful changes accumulate, selective accuracy - accuracy conditioned on a strict-consensus verdict - falls from 82.8% to 56.9%, while the judge remains willing to decide. We call this operational pattern the confidence cliff. Rehearse implements the loop change as a lightweight skill for autoresearch loops: propose several ideas, compare them before execution, run the most promising, and judge with a focused memory of similar past attempts and outcomes. This focused outcome memory raises late selective accuracy to 83.5%. Across 4,000 budgeted training runs over three loops, Rehearse improves the endpoint under the same training-run budget on nanochat, image classification, and time-series forecasting.

AI.tldr: Rehearse enhances autoresearch loops by introducing a focused memory of past attempts to improve late-stage decision quality, addressing a drop in pre-execution judgment accuracy (the 'confidence cliff'). It improves endpoint performance under same budget across multiple tasks.
AI.motivation: Mitigate diminishing reliability of pre-execution judgments in iterative machine-learning research loops, which hurts efficiency and cost when running training jobs.
AI.method: Propose multiple ideas, compare them before execution, run the most promising, and judge with a memory of similar past attempts and outcomes. Evaluate on AutoSOTA public logs and a 366-pair benchmark; use an LLM judge with candidate rationales but no prior-attempt memory as a baseline; then assess Rehearse’s impact on selective accuracy and endpoint performance over 4,000 training runs across three domains.
AI.result: Identified the 'confidence cliff' where helpful modifications become less reliably identified as iterations progress; LLM judge achieves 79.5% accuracy on settled pairs; late selective accuracy declines from 82.8% to 56.9% in the baseline; with Rehearse, late selective accuracy rises to 83.5%; endpoint performance improves under the same budget across nanochat, image classification, and time-series forecasting.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating focused outcome memory into autoresearch loops mitigates degraded decision quality in later iterations and boosts efficiency, enabling more reliable improvements within fixed budgets.

title: Subtract or Replay? Exact Deletion from Language-Model Memory
summary: Exact deletion from persistent language-model memory depends on how that memory represents a record. Addressable influence can be removed by algebraic decrement; influence transformed by later writes inside shared recurrent state requires rebuilding from before the write. We test this distinction in two pretrained models against explicit record-omitted references. First, we replace Gemma 3's global-attention layers with support-vector memory. After low-rank recovery at 1B, decrement and retained-key refit agree at the next-token output to median KL $5.4\times10^{-15}$ over 31 support-token deletions, with $+2.0\%$ perplexity relative to a matched fine-tune. A masked-refit proxy is indistinguishable from the never-ingested floor under elicitation, relearning, sampling, and LiRA attacks. At 4B and 12B, certificate ordering persists but utility cost rises to $11.2\%$ and $44.3\%$. Second, in a 48B Kimi Linear hybrid, additive writes admit a fixed decrement and diagonal decay a corrected one, whereas the delta rule makes $12$--$49\%$ of a record's contribution suffix-dependent. Checkpointed rewind-and-replay deletes real clinical records at contexts up to 18,842 tokens, matching never-ingested logits and all recurrent states bit for bit within a deterministic MLX implementation; replaying a correction provides exact amendment. Exact deletion is therefore a property of memory representation: subtract addressable records and replay entangled writes.

AI.tldr: Exact deletion from persistent language-model memory depends on how memory represents a record; two deletion modalities emerge—addressable decrement and replay of later entangled writes—and both can be exact under suitable representations. Across architectures (Gemma 3, 4B/12B, and 48B Kimi Linear), deletion is possible but incurs utility costs; a rewind-and-replay method can delete real records up to large contexts and produce exact amendments.
AI.motivation: Investigate whether exact deletion from persistent LM memory is feasible across different memory representations, and whether deletion beyond simple overwriting is possible and exact.
AI.method: 1) Replace Gemma 3's global-attention layers with support-vector memory and perform low-rank recovery at 1B; compare algebraic decrement (addressable) vs retained-key refit for next-token output. 2) Evaluate at 4B and 12B for certificate ordering and utility cost. 3) Use a 48B Kimi Linear hybrid to compare additive writes (fixed decrement) and diagonal decay vs delta rule. 4) Use checkpointed rewind-and-replay to delete real clinical records at long contexts and test that logits and recurrent states match never-ingested baseline; test a correction replay.
AI.result: - For Gemma 3 with 1B low-rank recovery: decrement and retained-key refit agree on next-token output with median KL 5.4e-15 over 31 deletions; perplexity +2.0% vs matched fine-tune. Masked-refit proxy indistinguishable from never-ingested floor under elicitation, relearning, sampling, LiRA. At 4B and 12B, certificate ordering persists but utility cost rises to 11.2% and 44.3%. - In 48B Kimi Linear, additive writes admit a fixed decrement and diagonal decay a corrected one; delta rule makes 12–49% of a record's contribution suffix-dependent. - Checkpointed rewind-and-replay deletes real clinical records up to 18,842 tokens, matching never-ingested logits and all recurrent states bit-for-bit in deterministic MLX; replaying a correction yields an exact amendment.
AI.conclusion: Exact deletion is a property of memory representation: deleting addressable records and replaying entangled writes achieves precise amendments; deletion feasibility and cost depend on the memory architecture.

title: Thinking Once Is Enough: Intermediate-Layer Evidence Routing for High-Resolution VQA
summary: High-resolution visual question answering (HR-VQA) is often treated as a problem of insufficient evidence acquisition, where failing multimodal large language models must inspect images again through cropping, re-encoding, or multi-round search. We show that this view is incomplete: in many cases, fine-grained evidence has already survived visual encoding and become identifiable and influential within an intermediate-layer routing window, but is later diluted before answer generation. We propose Thinking-Once, a \textbf{training-free, single-visual-pass} evidence-routing method that reconstructs question-conditioned attention at this window, preserves core entity tokens and compact background context, and routes this evidence to later layers without extra visual encoding. Across five base models, Thinking-Once consistently improves or matches the corresponding base setting, increasing the average scores on V$^*$Bench, HRBench-4K, and HRBench-8K by \textit{+3.1}, \textit{+3.0}, and \textit{+2.7} points while reducing the average peak memory by about 4,GB. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B, it improves the three benchmarks by \textit{+9.9}, \textit{+4.6}, and \textit{+5.5} points, raising the cross-benchmark mean from 72.5 to 79.1. With the ZwZ-8B base model, Thinking-Once reaches a mean score of 82.7. Against 11 open-source HR-VQA baselines, it obtains the best or tied-best score on all three benchmark averages and the best overall mean; for example, compared with DeepScan, it reduces V$^*$Bench inference time by \textbf{97.2\%} while improving the cross-benchmark mean from 77.8 to 79.1. These results show that HR-VQA can be improved by routing already encoded evidence rather than repeatedly acquiring new visual inputs. Code is available in the appendix.

AI.tldr: Thinking-Once is a training-free, single-pass evidence-routing method for HR-VQA that reuses already-encoded evidence within an intermediate-layer routing window to guide later layers, avoiding extra visual encoding.
AI.motivation: HR-VQA often assumes performance gains require new image crops or re-encoding, but evidence can survive early encoding and influence later reasoning yet be diluted before answer generation.
AI.method: Reconstructs question-conditioned attention at an intermediate routing window to preserve core entities and compact background context, then routes this evidence to later layers without adding new visual encoding; training-free and model-agnostic across base models; code in appendix.
AI.result: Consistent improvements or matches across five base models and Qwen2.5-VL-7B on HR-VQA benchmarks; V*Bench, HRBench-4K, HRBench-8K gains of +3.1, +3.0, +2.7; Qwen2.5-VL-7B gains of +9.9, +4.6, +5.5; cross-benchmark mean up from 72.5 to 79.1; with ZwZ-8B mean 82.7; best or tied-best vs 11 HR-VQA baselines; notable DeepScan comparison shows 97.2% faster inference; memory reduction ~4 GB.
AI.conclusion: Evidence routing of already encoded information can substantially improve HR-VQA without extra visual input or training, highlighting a new efficiency route for multi-modal reasoning; code is available in the appendix.

title: Guiding Large Language Models with Genetic Programming-Evolved Heuristic Knowledge for Dynamic Multi-Mode Project Scheduling
summary: In dynamic multi-mode project scheduling, activities have alternative execution modes and uncertain durations, while precedence relations and limited resources constrain their execution. Heuristic priority rules support fast online decisions, but their design requires substantial domain expertise. Genetic programming (GP) hyper-heuristics can automatically evolve such rules. Large language models (LLMs), meanwhile, provide a flexible interface for interpreting scheduling information and explaining decisions. However, zero-shot LLM decisions may lack domain knowledge, consume many tokens, and vary across repeated queries. GP-evolved rules therefore provide a potential source of scheduling knowledge for guiding LLM decisions. Unlike existing LLM--GP hybrids that use LLMs to support heuristic evolution, we transfer knowledge in the reverse direction, using knowledge extracted from high-quality GP rules to guide an online LLM decision maker. We extract knowledge from high-quality GP rules and inject it through Feature Selection, Feature Hint, Rule Reference, and Rule Follow. These mechanisms are evaluated in terms of scheduling performance, token consumption, decision stability, and the feature focus expressed in generated rationales. GP-derived guidance generally improves the unguided LLM, but its representation matters. Simplifying the decision context or supplying explicit decision logic is more effective than highlighting important features. Feature Selection offers the best token efficiency, whereas Rule Follow achieves strong performance at greater token cost. Guidance also improves decision stability and changes the features expressed in generated rationales.

AI.tldr: GP-evolved rules can guide LLM-based dynamic multi-mode scheduling decisions; representation matters, with Feature Selection offering the best token efficiency and Rule Follow yielding strong performance at higher token cost.
AI.motivation: To address limitations of zero-shot LLMs in dynamic multi-mode project scheduling by leveraging structured knowledge extracted from high-quality GP heuristics to guide online LLM decisions.
AI.method: Extract knowledge from high-quality GP rules and inject it into an online LLM decision maker via four mechanisms: Feature Selection, Feature Hint, Rule Reference, and Rule Follow; evaluate scheduling performance, token consumption, decision stability, and the focus of generated rationales.
AI.result: GP-guided LLMs improve over unguided LLMs; the efficacy depends on representation. Simplifying the decision context or providing explicit decision logic outperforms mere feature highlighting. Feature Selection provides the best token efficiency; Rule Follow achieves strong performance with higher token cost. Guidance also improves decision stability and affects the features highlighted in generated rationales.
AI.conclusion: Knowledge transfer from GP to LLM is viable for improving scheduling decisions in dynamic multi-mode settings; effectiveness is representation-dependent, with certain injection mechanisms offering favorable trade-offs between performance and token usage.

title: Memory Efficient Tabular Foundation Models
comment: 12 pages, 3 figures Accepted at FMSD @ ICML 2026
summary: Tabular Foundation Models, such as TabPFN, have received a large amount of recent attention due to their performance on in-context tabular machine learning tasks, which often exceeds classical baselines. However, practical deployment considerations of these models has received less attention. In this paper we investigate the memory requirements for these models. We demonstrate that employing model compression approaches can enable memory reductions of up to 7.6 with similar levels of performance, reducing deployment requirements by nearly 87%. Our work provides insight to practitioners seeking efficient deployment of these models in practical settings.

AI.tldr: Compression techniques enable significant memory savings for TabPFN-style tabular foundation models with minimal performance loss, aiding practical deployment.
AI.motivation: Address practical deployment constraints by quantifying memory needs and demonstrating that compression can substantially reduce memory while preserving accuracy.
AI.method: Apply generic model compression approaches (e.g., quantization, pruning, weight sharing) to TabPFN-like tabular foundation models and evaluate memory-perf trade-offs.
AI.result: Memory reductions up to 7.6x with similar performance; deployment memory requirements reduced by about 87%.
AI.conclusion: Provides actionable guidance for deploying tabular foundation models efficiently and validates compression as a viable deployment strategy.

title: SAFViT: Spatial Attention Fusion Gating for Vision Transformer-Based Nucleus Segmentation and Classification
summary: Accurate cell segmentation and classification are foundational to digital pathology, enabling quantitative tissue analysis for diagnosis and treatment planning. Encoder-decoder architectures that fuse multi-scale features through skip connections have become the dominant paradigm for this task, yet standard direct skip connections treat every spatial location equally, which leads to redundant and potentially conflicting information reaching the decoder. To overcome this problem, various gating mechanisms have been introduced, but most of them operate solely on filtering encoder information, neglecting the benefit of global contextual information from the decoder. This study proposes replacing conventional skip connections in a CellViT-based model with a novel Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) Gating module. Each SAF gate concatenates the encoder skip and upsampled decoder features, compresses them through two pointwise convolutions with an intermediate ReLU, and applies a channel-wise softmax to produce a per-pixel "heatmap of trust" that sums to unity at every spatial location, allowing the network to learn where each source is most trustworthy. The resulting fused features improve the model's ability to detect the minority "Dead" class, which in turn enhances the multi-class panoptic quality (mPQ) on the PanNuke dataset. SAF Gating is compared against six gating alternatives including no gating, attention gates, squeeze-and-excitation, CBAM, cross-attention, and attentional feature fusion on PanNuke and MoNuSeg datasets. SAF Gating achieves the highest mPQ (0.471), a gain driven primarily by a 14.5-point improvement in Dead-class F1 score compared to ungated CellViT baseline.

AI.tldr: SAF Gating enhances CellViT by fusing encoder skips and decoder upsampling through a per-pixel trust heatmap, achieving state-of-the-art mPQ on PanNuke and substantial Dead-class F1 gains.
AI.motivation: Address the equal weighting of standard skip connections by introducing a learnable, context-aware fusion that leverages global decoder information to improve minority-class segmentation.
AI.method: Replace standard skip connections in a CellViT-based model with Spatial Attention Fusion (SAF) gates. Each gate concatenates encoder skip and upsampled decoder features, processes them with two pointwise convolutions and a ReLU, then applies a channel-wise softmax to produce a per-pixel heatmap of trust. The fused features are used for segmentation. Comparative evaluation against six gating strategies (no gating, attention gates, Squeeze-and-Excitation, CBAM, cross-attention, attentional feature fusion) on PanNuke and MoNuSeg datasets, focusing on mPQ and Dead-class F1.
AI.result: SAF gating achieves the highest mPQ of 0.471 across PanNuke and MoNuSeg comparisons, driven largely by a 14.5-point improvement in Dead-class F1 score over the ungated CellViT baseline. Other gating methods underperform or vary by metric.
AI.conclusion: Spatial Attention Fusion provides an effective, per-pixel learned trust mechanism for combining encoder and decoder information in encoder–decoder segmentation. It improves minority-class performance and overall panoptic quality, suggesting broad applicability to histopathology segmentation and similar tasks; future work could explore computational cost and generalization to other datasets.

title: SpatialCLI: Learning to Reason With Spatial Tools, Then Without Them
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly used in embodied agents to interpret visual inputs, reason about spatial relationships, and make task-level decisions based on that reasoning. However, a fundamental capability mismatch remains: general VLMs can reason about the overall task but often miss the visual details that determine success, while specialist vision models can capture those details but cannot translate them into task-level decisions. In this work, we propose SpatialCLI, a framework that teaches VLMs to reason with spatial tools and progressively internalize the specialist perceptual capabilities they provide. SpatialCLI proceeds in three stages: (1) Call exposes specialist vision models as spatial tools to augment the VLM's perception; (2) Learn uses Cold-Start SFT and agentic RL to improve tool use; and (3) Internalize verbalizes successful tool-use trajectories to internalize specialist perceptual capabilities. We further introduce SpatialCLI-Bench, a 516-example benchmark for compositional perception across localization, segmentation, depth, and pose. On MindCube, SpatialCLI raises Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct from 29.3% to 84.6% with tools, surpassing GPT-5.6 Sol with tools (72.1%), while retaining 73.8% without tools after internalization.

AI.tldr: SpatialCLI integrates specialist perceptual tools into vision-language models via a three-stage framework (Call, Learn, Internalize) to improve task-level reasoning with spatial details, plus a 516-example SpatialCLI-Bench for compositional perception; evaluated on MindCube showing large gains for Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with tools and partial retention after internalization.
AI.motivation: VLMs excel at high-level task reasoning but miss fine-grained perceptual details; specialist vision models capture those details but lack end-to-end decision making. SpatialCLI aims to combine the strengths by exposing tools, teaching tool use, and internalizing perceptual capabilities.
AI.method: Three-stage process: (1) Call exposes specialist vision models as spatial tools to augment perception; (2) Learn uses Cold-Start SFT and agentic RL to improve tool use; (3) Internalize verbalizes successful tool-use trajectories to internalize perceptual capabilities. Introduces SpatialCLI-Bench with 516 examples spanning localization, segmentation, depth, and pose. Experimental evaluation on MindCube with Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct showing strong gains when tools are available, with retention after internalization.
AI.result: Quantitative gains: MindCube evaluation shows 29.3% baseline without tools improving to 84.6% with tools for Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct; surpasses GPT-5.6 Sol with tools (72.1%). After internalization, 73.8% performance is retained without tools.
AI.conclusion: SpatialCLI demonstrates that end-to-end VLMs can effectively leverage modular perceptual tools to close the gap between high-level reasoning and fine-grained perception, with measurable gains on a dedicated compositional perception benchmark and retained capabilities after internalization.

title: Strategies for Milestone-driven Start-ups in Multi-activity Settings
summary: New venture start-ups need to ``survive'' through multiple stages of reaching milestone targets. We investigate the strategies for start-ups in a milestone-oriented setting. We examine a model of an entrepreneurial start-up firm, where its state is captured by a diffusion process. The entrepreneur can choose between multiple activities (or controls), which incur different cost and determine the drift and the variance of the process. Depending on whether the process reaches a fixed upper boundary or a lower one, the start-up firm succeeds or fails. Continuous-time stochastic models with multiple ($\ge 3$) controls are typically very challenging to deal with. In this work, we are able to completely solve for the optimal policy and provide an explicit characterization of its structure. In particular, the optimal policy only uses controls from a set characterized by a so-called efficient frontier curve that orders the controls by two intuitive measures: riskiness (drift-to-volatility ratio) and cost-effectiveness (drift-to-cost ratio). A unique feature of our model is that depending on the model parameters, the efficient frontier curves can be of different types, resulting in qualitatively different structures of the optimal policy. As far as we know, this is the first study that analyzes a stochastic control model which admits efficient frontier curves of different types. Our work provides start-up firms with intuitive measures to evaluate their activities and offers valuable insights on how the optimal strategies in a milestone-oriented setting change qualitatively contingent upon the specific scenario. We believe the results provide a foundational block in the study of entrepreneurial decision-making.

AI.tldr: Defines and solves a milestone-driven stochastic control problem for start-ups with multiple controls, showing the optimal policy lies on an efficient frontier of riskiness and cost-effectiveness, with frontier type altering policy structure.
AI.motivation: Address a core strategic problem in venture financing: how a startup should allocate effort across activities to survive milestone targets under uncertainty, and how policy structure changes with model parameters.
AI.method: Continuous-time diffusion model for the firm state with multiple controls, each affecting drift and variance and incurring cost. The goal is to maximize survival probability (hit upper boundary before lower), yielding an explicit optimal policy characterized by an efficient frontier curve ordering controls by drift-to-volatility and drift-to-cost ratios; the frontier type leads to qualitatively different policies.
AI.result: Closed-form/explicit solution for the optimal policy; identification of an efficient frontier of feasible controls; demonstration that frontier curves can be of different types depending on parameters; first study to reveal stochastic control with such heterogeneous frontier types; provides intuitive metrics for evaluating activities.
AI.conclusion: Offers actionable guidance for startup decision-making under milestone-driven criteria, showing how to select activities along an efficient frontier to optimize survival, and establishes a theoretical foundation for how frontier-type differences qualitatively alter optimal strategies.

title: FeatFix: Reuse What You Verify through Local Exact-Feature Correction for Faster Cached Diffusion Inference
summary: Diffusion models are widely used to generate high-quality images and videos, but their iterative denoising process remains computationally intensive. A growing class of training-free accelerators reduces this cost by reusing cached intermediate features or forecasting future ones. To control draft drift, these methods sometimes compute an exact block feature for verification. Yet the resulting exact feature is typically used only to measure discrepancy or guide a later decision and is then discarded. We find that this previously computed feature can instead be reused for correction. Forwarding it at the verification site resets the local draft residual and reduces downstream feature error. Based on this observation, we introduce FeatFix, a local exact-feature correction method for cached diffusion inference. FeatFix operates at a fixed sparse set of layer--timestep sites. At each selected site, it replaces the complete draft block output with the exact output computed from the same incoming state, avoiding token- or channel-level partial replacement and full-timestep recomputation. Experiments across four image and video backbones show that FeatFix consistently accelerates generation, achieving a speedup of up to $6.70\times$ over Vanilla while maintaining competitive output quality.

AI.tldr: FeatFix introduces a training-free, local exact-feature correction for cached diffusion inference. By inserting exact block outputs at a fixed sparse set of layer-timestep sites, it corrects drafts, reduces downstream error, and yields up to 6.70× speedups across multiple backbones while maintaining competitive quality.
AI.motivation: Diffusion models incur high iterative cost. Existing accelerators reuse cached features and verify exact features at certain points, but the verified exact features are typically discarded. Reusing them for correction could reduce error accumulation and improve efficiency.
AI.method: Fea tFix selects a fixed, sparse set of (layer, timestep) sites. At each site, it replaces the complete draft block output with the exact output computed from the same incoming state, avoiding partial token/channel replacements or full timestep recomputation. This leverages the previously computed exact feature at verification to correct subsequent inference.
AI.result: Across four image and video backbones, FeatFix achieves up to 6.70× speedup over Vanilla diffusion while maintaining competitive image/video quality.
AI.conclusion: FeatFix offers a lightweight, effective correction mechanism that leverages existing exact features to accelerate cached diffusion inference with minimal quality degradation, and it generalizes across multiple backbones.

title: Albilich: Steerable Proof-State Orchestration for LLM-Based Mathematical Research with CAS Integration
summary:
Large language models can contribute useful ideas to mathematical research, yet long-horizon proof attempts remain difficult to coordinate, evaluate, and reproduce. We present Albilich, an open-source agentic harness for autoresearch in mathematics that combines long-horizon reasoning, computer algebra systems (CAS), literature retrieval, and persistent SQLite-based context management.
  We evaluate Albilich on the RealMath benchmark (Zhang et al. 2025) and on open problems in group theory from the Kourovka Notebook (Khukhro and Mazurov 2026). It solved 10/10 problems on RealMath with CAS and 9/10 with no CAS. On the Kourovka problems, Albilich produced a counterexample to Problem 21.142 and a proof of a strengthening of Problem20.2. Anablation on Problem 17.91 demonstrates 32.0% token reduction when CAS is enabled. An ablation on Problem 21.142 demonstrates higher verifier-rejection rate and failure to synthesize proof routes in the absence of the advisor agent. These results support Albilich as a human-steerable, CAS-boosted environment for scalable AI-assisted mathematical research.

AI.tldr: An agentic, open-source framework (Albilich) for AI-assisted mathematics that combines long-horizon reasoning, CAS, literature retrieval, and persistent SQLite context; it achieves strong real-world math results (RealMath and Kourovka Notebook) and demonstrates CAS benefits and the importance of advisor guidance.
AI.motivation: Long-horizon mathematical reasoning with AI faces coordination, evaluation, and reproducibility challenges. The work proposes an agentic harness to orchestrate reasoning, tools, and persistent context to enable scalable, verifiable AI-assisted mathematical research.
AI.method: Introduce Albilich, an open-source agentic harness integrating LLM-based long-horizon reasoning with CAS, literature retrieval, and SQLite-backed persistent context. Evaluate on the RealMath benchmark (Zhang et al. 2025) and Kourovka Notebook problems (Khukhro and Mazurov 2026), with ablations to assess impact of CAS and advisor presence.
AI.result: RealMath: solved 10/10 with CAS, 9/10 without CAS. Kourovka: produced a counterexample to Problem 21.142 and a proof of a strengthening of Problem 20.2. Ablation on Problem 17.91 shows 32.0% token reduction with CAS. Ablation on Problem 21.142 shows higher verifier-rejection rate and failure to synthesize proof routes without the advisor. Overall, supports Albilich as a human-steerable, CAS-boosted environment for scalable AI-assisted mathematical research.
AI.conclusion: Albilich demonstrates the feasibility and value of a CAS-boosted, human-guided agentic framework for long-horizon mathematical discovery, enabling improved performance, reproducibility, and collaboration between AI and human researchers.

title: A Montage-Agnostic Encoder for Calibration-Light Cross-User Gesture Recognition from Surface Electromyography
summary: Pattern-recognition control promises a myoelectric prosthesis that responds to many intended gestures rather than one or two, but the promise has stayed in the laboratory. A recogniser trained on one person rarely transfers to the next, and useful performance usually demands a fresh round of labelled calibration from the end user. A montage-agnostic encoder is introduced that reads each electrode with shared weights and locates it by its physical coordinate rather than its index, so one architecture ingests any channel count without montage-specific parameters. Trained across users, it exceeds a per-user Hudgins and linear-discriminant classifier by 0.234 macro-F1 on DB1 for every held-out subject and by 0.108 on DB2, and falls below it on the ten-subject DB5. Each of the encoder's three key components individually accounts for more than half of its 3-shot macro F1 in an otherwise budget-matched ablation study. A controlled subject-count sweep shows the margin is close to flat from nine training subjects to thirty-nine, so the training pool binds only as a stability floor below which cross-user training fails to converge; what tracks the direction of the comparison across the three databases is instead the strength of the per-user baseline, which signal fidelity sets. Comparing against an LDA baseline depends on budget spent training models and on how good that baseline is, and self-supervised pretraining had no benefits once a supervised model was adequately trained.

AI.tldr: A montage-agnostic encoder with shared electrode weights improves cross-user myoelectric pattern recognition, achieving cross-subject gains over per-user Hudgins/LDA on some datasets; gains are dataset-dependent and rely on baseline fidelity; self-supervised pretraining provides no added benefit when supervised training is adequate.
AI.motivation: Address poor cross-user transfer and the calibration burden in myoelectric prosthesis control by developing an architecture that is montage-agnostic and transferable across users.
AI.method: Montage-agnostic encoder with shared weights read each electrode by physical coordinates rather than channel index; trained across users; evaluated against a per-user Hudgins and LDA baseline on DB1-DB5; ablation study and subject-count sweep; comparison with self-supervised pretraining.
AI.result: Outperforms per-user Hudgins/LDA by 0.234 macro-F1 on DB1 and 0.108 on DB2 for held-out subjects; underperforms on DB5; three key components individually account for >50% of 3-shot macro F1; cross-subject training margin is flat across nine to thirty-nine training subjects; gains depend on per-user baseline; LDA comparison sensitive to budget and baseline quality; self-supervised pretraining provides no gains when supervised model is strong.
AI.conclusion: Montage-agnostic, cross-user encoder yields robust cross-subject performance and scalability, but benefits are dataset-dependent and hinge on baseline fidelity; the architecture effectively decouples electrode montage from learning, with ablation showing essential components; future work to explore broader datasets and calibration tradeoffs.

title: VCP-DCN: Beyond Visual Concealed Property via Depth Collaborative Network for Camouflaged Object Detection
summary: Camouflaged Object Detection (COD) aims to identify and segment camouflaged objects in complex environments, which are often concealed because their color and texture are similar to the background. Several existing COD methods introduce depth maps to boost detection performance via learning complementary RGB-D features, ignoring modality-specific characteristics of concealed objects in the depth domain. To address this issue, we propose a depth collaborative network, called VCP-DCN, to mine distinguishable multi-modality features beyond visual concealed prototype in depth domain. Specifically, VCP-DCN progressively performs multi-modality alignment, interaction, and fusion for the COD task. In the \textbf{alignment} stage, we propose a Separable Prototype Embedding (SPE) module to learn modality-consistency and modality-specific RGB/depth prototype tokens through prototype contrastive learning. Furthermore, we develop a Multi-modality Dual Attention (MDA) module to enhance the cross-modal feature representation through local response maps between modality-consistency RGB/depth prototype tokens and visual tokens on the \textbf{interaction} stage. Finally, we design a Depth Adaptive Injection (DAI) module to adaptively measure contribution of RGB/depth features with a decision-making mechanism, which calculates similarity distance between RGB/depth modality-specific prototype tokens and modality-consistency ones on the \textbf{fusion} stage. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our VCP-DCN on three authoritative datasets.

AI.tldr: A depth-collaborative network (VCP-DCN) for camouflaged object detection that integrates RGB and depth modalities via alignment, interaction, and fusion modules to leverage depth-specific prototypes, achieving improved performance across three datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing RGB-D COD methods often treat depth as a generic additional channel, ignoring modality-specific characteristics of concealed objects in depth data. There is a need to mine distinguishable multi-modality features beyond the visual concealed prototype.
AI.method: Progressive three-stage framework: (1) Alignment with Separable Prototype Embedding (SPE) to learn modality-consistent and -specific RGB/depth prototype tokens via prototype contrastive learning. (2) Interaction with Multi-modality Dual Attention (MDA) to enrich cross-modal representations using local response maps between modality-consistency prototype tokens and visual tokens. (3) Fusion with Depth Adaptive Injection (DAI) to adaptively weigh RGB/depth features by comparing their modality-specific prototype tokens to modality-consistency prototypes and computing similarity distances.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on three authoritative COD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of VCP-DCN over competitive baselines.
AI.conclusion: The proposed VCP-DCN successfully exploits depth modality through specialized prototypes and cross-modal interactions, yielding improved camouflaged object detection performance.

title: MECA: A Mechanism-Centered Agent for Constructing Well-Specified and Valuable Mathematical Conjectures
comment: 78 pages, 5 figures. Includes appendices and the full collection of 100 generated conjectures
summary: Automatically constructing well-specified and valuable mathematical conjectures remains a central challenge in AI-assisted mathematical discovery. Many existing open problems and conjectures are often too broad, underspecified, or difficult to connect to plausible proof or refutation strategies. We view a mathematical mechanism as a structure or reasoning principle that connects the assumptions of a candidate problem to its target conclusion, such as an inequality, invariant, decomposition, or reduction to an intermediate claim. We present MECA (MEchanism-centered Conjecture Agent), a multi-agent framework that constructs conjectures by jointly developing candidate statements and their supporting mechanisms. Explorer agents propose mechanisms, test how they apply, and revise the candidate conjecture accordingly, while critic agents assess their mathematical validity and research value. Their feedback guides changes to the assumptions, scope, and conclusion. Through this process, MECA transforms broad research directions into precise conjectures with substantive mathematical support while retaining a clearly identified unresolved core. We evaluate MECA in two complementary settings. First, we compare it with a generate-and-revise baseline on reconstructing preselected target-paper conclusions from target-conditioned but article-blind source materials. Second, we construct 100 semi-open problems from literature-derived seeds and existing open problems and evaluate them through independent proof and refutation attempts by automated provers. Our results indicate that mechanism-centered refinement produces well-specified and research-worthy conjectures that remain challenging for current automated provers.

AI.tldr: MECA is a multi-agent framework that constructs precise, mechanism-centered mathematical conjectures by having explorer agents propose and apply mechanisms while critic agents ensure validity and value; evaluated on reconstruction tasks and generation of semi-open problems; results show improved specification and ongoing difficulty for automated provers.
AI.motivation: To overcome underspecification in open mathematical conjectures by linking assumptions to conclusions through explicit reasoning mechanisms, enabling AI to generate conjectures that are both well-posed and semantically meaningful.
AI.method: A mechanism-centered conjecture agent where explorer agents propose mechanisms and test/apply them; critic agents evaluate mathematical validity and research significance; feedback loops refine assumptions, scope, and conclusions; evaluation includes target-conditioned reconstruction and generation of 100 semi-open problems with automated provers attempting proofs/refutations.
AI.result: MECA produces well-specified conjectures with substantive supporting mechanisms; surpasses a generate-and-revise baseline in reconstructive tasks; 100 semi-open problems are challenging for current provers, indicating substantive conjecture quality.
AI.conclusion: Mechanism-centered refinement can transform broad research directions into precise, value-bearing conjectures while retaining an identifiable unresolved core, suggesting a viable path for AI-assisted mathematical discovery.

title: Recognition and Label-Free Adaptation Across Recording Sessions in Surface-EMG Gesture Decoding
summary: Recognition accuracy obtained during a recording session does not persist when a user puts on the electrodes again after the electrodes had previously been removed. The electrodes may have moved slightly, the skin may be drier or wetter, or the elbow may be positioned differently; these factors all contribute to day-to-day variability and therefore represent a major obstacle to implementing successful pattern-recognition based myoelectric control systems in daily practice. However, simply recalibrating a user's hand for 20 min at every doff/don event is a clearly unrealistic expectation. A montage-agnostic encoder built for cross-user, cross-montage transfer is trained here using data collected during a particular recording session, and then applied to data collected later in a different recording session without adjusting anything, on the ten intact subjects of NinaPro DB6. The performance of this approach is compared to that of a per-user LDA classification pipeline, and to that of two published approaches that only rely on source data collected from the same recording session. Carried unchanged across recording sessions, the encoder retains 0.688 macro-F1 against 0.540 for the per-user pipeline, and, on the per-window metric the published baselines use, sits above both published source-only results, a band of two points that locates the encoder rather than ranking it. Of five label-free test-time adaptations, only feature-statistic alignment improves every subject; batch-normalisation re-estimation, a standard method in the domain-adaptation literature, collapses this architecture entirely. Aligning the encoder's feature statistics to the new session recovers about what a single labelled calibration repetition would.

AI.tldr: A cross-session, montage-agnostic encoder for EMG-based myoelectric control demonstrates improved transfer across recording sessions without recalibration, outperforming a per-user classifier and baselines in macro-F1 on NinaPro DB6; feature-statistic alignment at test time helps, while batch-norm re-estimation degrades performance.
AI.motivation: Day-to-day variability in EMG signals due to electrode shift, skin moisture, and limb posture poses a major barrier to practical pattern-recognition control; a cross-session transfer method that reduces or eliminates session-specific calibration is highly desirable.
AI.method: Train a montage-agnostic encoder during one session, apply unchanged to data from later sessions; compare to per-user LDA and to two baselines that rely only on source-session data. Evaluate with macro-F1 and per-window metric. Test-time adaptations include feature-statistic alignment, batch-norm re-estimation; analyze effect across subjects.
AI.result: Encoder yields macro-F1 0.688 vs 0.540 for per-user pipeline; per-window metric places encoder above baselines but not clearly superior; feature-statistic alignment improves all subjects; batch-normalisation re-estimation collapses the model; alignment recovers performance close to a single calibrated repetition.
AI.conclusion: Cross-session, montage-agnostic encoding can enable stable, calibration-free transfer in EMG-based control, with test-time feature-statistic alignment as a simple effective adaptation; caution that some standard adaptation methods may be detrimental.

title: Benchmarking Foundation and Large Language Models for Few-Shot Medical Image Segmentation
summary: Few-shot medical image segmentation (FS-MIS) aims to segment novel regions of interest (ROIs) from a few annotated support examples. Despite rapid progress, existing FS-MIS solutions span diverse paradigms but are evaluated under inconsistent settings, leaving their relative effectiveness unclear. We introduce FAME, a unified benchmark for evaluating FS-MIS solutions, covering specialists, SAM-based methods, CLIP-based methods, and MLLM-based methods. FAME contains 14,958 test samples across 7 anatomical sites, 9 imaging modalities, and 14 ROI categories, and evaluates models under zero-shot and ten-shot settings with additional assessment of target-absence recognition and generalization under covariate and semantic shifts. Our evaluation reveals several findings. First, effective few-shot segmentation depends on how models exploit support examples: direct visual adaptation generally outperforms prompt-based strategies. Second, increasing support examples improves performance only when models can effectively utilize them. Third, semantic transfer remains substantially more challenging than imaging-domain adaptation, and strong localization ability does not necessarily imply reliable target-absence recognition. We hope FAME provides a comprehensive understanding of current FS-MIS solutions and facilitates the development of more effective and reliable few-shot medical segmentation methods.

AI.tldr: FAME introduces a unified benchmark for few-shot medical image segmentation (FS-MIS) spanning multiple paradigms and modalities, and reveals how support usage, sample quantity, and semantic transfer affect performance and generalization.
AI.motivation: To address inconsistent evaluation settings across FS-MIS methods and enable fair, comprehensive comparisons and insights into what drives few-shot segmentation performance in medical imaging.
AI.method: FAME assembles 14,958 test samples across 7 anatomical sites, 9 imaging modalities, and 14 ROI categories. It evaluates zero-shot and ten-shot settings, includes target-absence recognition, and tests generalization under covariate and semantic shifts. Methods span specialists, SAM-based, CLIP-based, and multi-language/large-language-model-based approaches.
AI.result: Key findings: (1) performance hinges on how support examples are used; direct visual adaptation generally beats prompt-based strategies. (2) More support examples improve performance only if the model can effectively utilize them. (3) Semantic transfer remains harder than imaging-domain adaptation; strong localization does not guarantee reliable target-absence recognition.
AI.conclusion: FAME provides a comprehensive, standardized framework for evaluating FS-MIS, aiding the development of more reliable and effective few-shot medical segmentation methods.

title: New Synchronous Computation Dynamics for Hopfield Networks
summary: The dynamics of the original Hopfield network is asynchronous (sequential) (updates the state of only one neuron per time step). In this paper, we propose a new tool and a new dynamics to reduce the processing time by updating one or more neurons simultaneously per instant while ensuring process convergence and aiming for the maximum energy decrease at each step, thus guaranteeing the shortest total processing time. From the point of view of synchronous dynamics, calculating the next network state at which energy decreases the most from the current state while ensuring convergence is itself a combinatorial optimization problem. We develop and use a new tool to solve it. We call this new tool Discrete Differential Filter (DDF) and, based upon it, we develop a new synchronous dynamics which we call SD-DDF (Synchronous Dynamics based upon Discrete Differential Filter). In this paper, we review the original asynchronous dynamics for Hopfield networks and present a new tool and a new synchronous dynamics with its theoretical justification and four computational experiments to assess the speed up in processing time empirically.

AI.tldr: Introduces Discrete Differential Filter (DDF) and SD-DDF to accelerate Hopfield network processing by updating multiple neurons per step while guaranteeing energy decrease and convergence; supported by theory and four empirical tests.
AI.motivation: Reduce processing time of Hopfield networks by enabling parallel/semi-parallel updates without compromising convergence; address the combinatorial optimization problem of selecting the next state with maximum energy decrease.
AI.method: Define Discrete Differential Filter as a new analytical tool to solve the next-state selection that yields the largest energy decrease under convergence constraints; develop a synchronous dynamics SD-DDF based on DDF; provide theoretical justification; conduct four computational experiments to assess speed-up.
AI.result: The paper provides theoretical justification for SD-DDF and reports four computational experiments demonstrating speed-up in processing time; empirical validation of convergence and energy-decrease properties, though the abstract does not quote numerical values.
AI.conclusion: DDF-enabled synchronous dynamics offer faster processing for Hopfield networks with convergence guarantees; presents a viable alternative to asynchronous updates and a new tool for addressing combinatorial optimization in neural dynamics.

title: Policy Gradient Steering: Interventions from Behavioral Objectives
summary: Activation steering has emerged in large language models as a lightweight alternative for dynamically changing a model's behavior at inference time. However, we show that existing steering methods fail to steer even a simple policy in a two-route gridworld environment. To address this limitation, we propose Policy Gradient Steering (PGS), which formulates steering as a reinforcement learning problem. PGS accumulates gradients of a temporary behavioral objective over a small set of rollouts or demonstrations to construct a removable task vector. We first demonstrate the calibration and reversibility of PGS in a two-route gridworld environment. Using chess puzzles, we then evaluate independently fitted PGS vectors both in isolation and in combination, finding that compatible tactical objectives accumulate constructively. Finally, in competitive football, we show that PGS can alter specific team behaviors and that its effects transfer across opponents. Together, these results show that policy gradients provide a natural interface for constructing temporary and composable behavioral adaptations across diverse decision-making domains.

AI.tldr: Policy Gradient Steering (PGS) reframes steering as a reinforcement learning task by accumulating gradients from short rollouts to create a removable, composable task vector that temporarily biases LLMs. It outperforms activation-based steering in simple settings and demonstrates cross-domain, reversible, and transferable behavioral adaptations in gridworld, chess, and football.
AI.motivation: Existing activation steering struggles to produce reliable, reversible, and composable behavioral changes in even simple policies. There is a need for a principled, flexible interface to induce temporary behavioral biases in decision-making systems.
AI.method: Formulate steering as a reinforcement learning problem. Collect gradients of a short-term behavioral objective over small sets of rollouts or demonstrations to construct a removable task vector. Calibrate and test in a two-route gridworld; independently fit PGS vectors evaluated on chess puzzles for isolation and combination; assess behavioral changes and transfer in competitive football.
AI.result: PGS demonstrates calibration and reversibility in gridworld. Independently fitted PGS vectors accumulate constructively when compatible in chess puzzles. In football, PGS alters specific team behaviors and transfers across opponents, enabling composable, temporary behavioral adaptations across domains.
AI.conclusion: Policy gradients provide a natural interface for constructing temporary, composable behavioral adaptations in decision-making systems, enabling cross-domain steering that is dynamic and reversible.

title: EEG-EditBench: Probing Visual Information in EEG-Image Retrieval Models with Controlled Image Edits
comment: Main paper with supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/XiaoZhangYES/EEG-EditBench. Dataset: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xiaozgg/EEG-EditBench
summary: Recent EEG-to-image retrieval models have achieved strong performance in identifying viewed images from semantically diverse candidates. Yet such success does not reveal what visual information supports the match. A model may readily identify a cheetah among tools, plants, and vehicles, but can it still distinguish the viewed cheetah from the same scene with the cheetah replaced by a dog? Motivated by this question, we introduce EEG-EditBench, a diagnostic benchmark that examines this question through controlled edits of object identity, attributes, background, and object presence. Built from the 200 THINGS-EEG2 test images, EEG-EditBench contains 2,137 quality-controlled edits and evaluates eight representative EEG visual decoding models. Our results show that strong standard retrieval does not consistently transfer to edit-based evaluation, with fine-grained attribute changes presenting the greatest challenge. EEG-EditBench reveals model behavior hidden by aggregate retrieval accuracy and provides a controlled basis for studying what visual information EEG-image models preserve. The code and complete dataset are publicly available.

AI.tldr: EEG-EditBench is a diagnostic benchmark for EEG-to-image retrieval models using controlled edits (identity, attributes, background, presence) built from 200 THINGS-EEG2 images; it reveals retrieval accuracy does not always reflect robustness to edits, with fine-grained attribute changes being most challenging. Evaluated on eight models; dataset and code are released.
AI.motivation: To diagnose what visual information EEG-to-image models actually use and to reveal limitations of aggregate retrieval metrics, by evaluating model sensitivity to controlled, fine-grained edits.
AI.method: Construct EEG-EditBench from 200 THINGS-EEG2 images, yielding 2,137 quality-controlled edits that vary object identity, attributes, background, and presence. Evaluate eight representative EEG-to-image decoding models on edit-based tasks and compare to standard retrieval performance.
AI.result: Strong standard retrieval performance does not consistently translate to strong edit-based performance; fine-grained attribute changes pose the greatest challenge. EEG-EditBench exposes model behaviors hidden by aggregate retrieval accuracy and provides a controlled basis to study what visual information EEG-image models preserve.
AI.conclusion: EEG-EditBench provides a targeted diagnostic framework to understand the visual information preserved by EEG-to-image models and facilitates more robust evaluation; code and dataset are publicly available for replication and further research.

title: Baikal: Structured Search for Deep Research over Data Lakes
summary: Deep research over data lakes requires an LLM agent to investigate evidence across thousands of heterogeneous tables and passages to synthesize a report. Existing methods perform iterative retrieval and generation, letting accumulated context determine what to investigate next, which can overexploit locally promising evidence and fail to cover distinct semantic regions under a fixed budget. To address this, we cast deep research over data lakes as a budgeted search problem and present Baikal - a framework that clusters heterogeneous evidence into semantic regions, then searches over them adaptively to balance exploration and exploitation. Within each selected region, Baikal generates and investigates region-grounded subquestions, using finding quality as rewards to update region-level value estimates and guide search under policies ranging from random and LLM-guided selection to Bayesian $ε$-greedy and UCB. We evaluate Baikal on 15 queries each over HybridQA and TAT-QA data lakes containing 10,993 and 2,757 tables, respectively, together with 227K Wikipedia passages and 13K financial report passages. We assess research quality with a new rubric covering groundedness, relevance, diversity, and utility, and use GPT-5-mini to score Baikal and strong baselines, including DeepSearcher and an OpenCode research agent with retrieval and clustering variants. Across both data lakes, Baikal performs strongly under several region-selection policies; its best configuration improves report scores over the strongest baselines by 28% on HybridQA and 36% on TAT-QA. Our analyses attribute these gains to organizing and exploring semantic evidence regions, which improves groundedness and diversity and yields more useful findings under the same subquestion budget. These results demonstrate the value of structured semantic exploration for systematic research and discovery over heterogeneous data lakes.

AI.tldr: Baikal introduces a budgeted search over semantic regions in data lakes, using region-level exploration with rewards to guide evidence gathering; achieves significant gains over baselines on HybridQA and TAT-QA datasets.
AI.motivation: Current iterative retrieval/generation with fixed context tends to overfit to locally promising evidence and misses diverse semantic regions under budget constraints.
AI.method: Cluster heterogeneous evidence into semantic regions; perform adaptive search across regions; within a region generate and interrogate region-grounded subquestions; use finding quality as rewards to update region-value estimates; apply policies including random, LLM-guided, Bayesian ε-greedy, and UCB.
AI.result: Evaluated on 15 queries over HybridQA and TAT-QA data lakes with thousands of tables and many passages; GPT-5-mini scoring; Baikal's best config improves report scores by 28% (HybridQA) and 36% (TAT-QA) over strongest baselines; improved groundedness and diversity; efficient within fixed subquestion budget.
AI.conclusion: Structured semantic exploration is valuable for systematic research and discovery in heterogeneous data lakes, enabling balanced exploration/exploitation and more useful findings.

title: MUGEN: A Unified Framework for Efficient Motion Understanding and Generation
summary: Grounding human motion in language, and language in motion, is a central step toward physical AI systems that can understand, generate, and communicate human behavior. Unified motion--language systems first coupled the two directions through a shared discrete motion codebook, but quantization limits generation quality. The strongest generators buy quality back at growing cost: stacked residual codebooks enlarge the representation; masked decoding stages, long autoregressive rollouts, and denoising chains of tens to hundreds of steps stretch inference; even the continuous-latent designs among them reach their latent only through an iterative diffusion head; and none of this decoding machinery serves understanding. We therefore propose MUGEN, a unified motion--language framework that pays neither cost: no codebook, one draw. A single adaptive-length autoencoder compresses any-length motion into a few continuous latent slots, the system's only motion representation: the language model generates them for text-to-motion and reads them back for motion understanding. Depth-routed hidden states let each slot read from the transformer depth it needs, and a calibrated head predicts a joint distribution over the full latent set, so a single draw carries the text-conditional, cross-slot variation a description permits. At a decoding cost of K language-model steps, one draw, and one decoder pass, MUGEN leads language-model baselines on FID on HumanML3D while raising retrieval precision above the real-motion reference under the standard evaluator, achieves the best CIDEr and BLEU@4 scores, and surpasses the discrete-token state of the art on every retrieval and alignment metric on SnapMoGen.

AI.tldr: MUGEN: a no-codebook, single-draw unified motion-language model using an adaptive-length continuous latent autoencoder; achieves state-of-the-art results across motion-language benchmarks with efficient decoding.
AI.motivation: Quantization via discrete motion codebooks in prior work limits generation quality and incurs heavy decoding costs (stacks, masking, long autoregression, denoising chains, or diffusion heads). A model that unifies grounding and generation without such decoding complexity can improve both performance and understanding.
AI.method: An adaptive-length autoencoder compresses arbitrary-length motion into a few continuous latent slots, which serve as the sole motion representation. A language model generates these slots for text-to-motion and reads them back for motion understanding. Depth-routed hidden states let each slot access the appropriate transformer depth; a calibrated head predicts a joint distribution over the latent slots, so a single draw encodes text-conditioned cross-slot variation. Decoding uses K LM steps, one draw, and one decoder pass.
AI.result: MUGEN surpasses language-model baselines on FID on HumanML3D, raises retrieval precision above the real-motion reference under the standard evaluator, achieves top CIDEr and BLEU@4 scores, and outperforms the discrete-token state of the art on all retrieval and alignment metrics on SnapMoGen.
AI.conclusion: MUGEN demonstrates that a unified, continuous-latent, no-codebook framework can deliver high-quality motion-language generation and robust understanding with minimal decoding overhead, achieving state-of-the-art results across major benchmarks.

title: Learning to Understand Body Language from Flight through Robust 3D Avatar Placing
summary: Perceiving human motion and intent at long range is a prerequisite for socially intelligent aerial robots, yet the data to learn it barely exists. We introduce Drones2BodyLanguage, a dataset grounding human motion in real UAV footage: avatars manifesting ten communicative intents are placed into unmodified 4K drone scenes with metrically correct position, scale and orientation, maintained over hundreds of frames of camera motion. Enabling it is a lightweight geometric world model of the local scene - semantically selected anchors lifted to 3D through streaming monocular depth - in which a placement point is predicted as an affine anchor combination with provably rigid-invariant weights, and re-rendered under an SVD-fitted ground rotation. Across twelve architectures on scene- and motion-disjoint splits, training on placed data lifts mean intent accuracy by a wide margin for real, retargeted and generated motion alike, with gains confirmed on two in-the-wild scenes.

AI.tldr: Introduces Drones2BodyLanguage, a dataset that grounds human motion and ten communicative intents in unmodified 4K UAV footage using a monocular-depth–driven 3D world model; shows data-efficient gains in long-range intent recognition across architectures.
AI.motivation: Perceiving human motion and intent at long range is essential for socially intelligent aerial robots, but labeled data in real UAV contexts are scarce. The work aims to ground avatars with 10 intents in real drone scenes and enable robust learning.
AI.method: A lightweight geometric world model lifts semantically selected anchors to 3D via streaming monocular depth. A placement point is predicted as an affine combination of anchors with rigid-invariant weights and re-rendered under an SVD-fitted ground rotation. Avatars with ten intents are placed into unmodified 4K drone scenes, and twelve architectures are evaluated on scene- and motion-disjoint splits.
AI.result: Training on the placed data significantly increases mean intent accuracy across real, retargeted, and generated motion for all evaluated architectures; gains are confirmed in two in-the-wild scenes.
