AgenticASR implements this task through an ASR--Refiner architecture that repeatedly transforms a bounded active context and replaces its corresponding output span as audio arrives. This enables continual emission and revision over streams of arbitrary duration. We also introduce AASR-Bench, a bilingual benchmark with fine-grained atomic rubrics. Across multiple ASR front ends, AgenticASR attains the highest AASR-Bench scores among evaluated systems. A human--AI agreement study shows that rubric-based judgments align with independent expert assessments. Ablations characterize Refiner capacity, context length, and the quality--latency trade-off between online and offline inference. Together, these results establish AgenticASR as a practical framework for intent-preserving clean transcription during ongoing speech. Code, AASR-Bench, and a demo will be released at https://github.com/AnXMuy/AgenticASR.

AI.tldr: Proposes AgenticASR, an online, revisable ASR framework that continually refines mis-transcriptions as streaming audio arrives to produce clean, intent-preserving text. Demonstrates superiority on AASR-Bench and shows strong human-AI agreement; provides code and benchmark release.
AI.motivation: Verbatim ASR outputs retain disfluencies, repetitions, and self-corrections that hinder readability and downstream tasks. Existing methods process completed audio/transcripts and cannot revise earlier text when later speech alters interpretation. A need exists for intent-preserving, clean transcription in ongoing speech.
AI.method: Introduce AgenticSR with an ASR--Refiner architecture that maintains a bounded active context and repeatedly transforms output spans as new audio arrives. Enables continual emission and revision over streams of arbitrary duration. Evaluate across multiple ASR front ends on the bilingual AASR-Bench; perform ablations on Refiner capacity, context length, and online vs offline latency. Conduct a human–AI agreement study.
AI.result: AgenticASR achieves the highest AASR-Bench scores among evaluated systems across tested front ends. Human–AI judgments align with independent expert assessments. Ablations quantify the impact of Refiner capacity, context length, and the quality–latency trade-off.
AI.conclusion: AgenticASR provides a practical, intent-preserving clean transcription framework for ongoing speech, combining real-time revision with accuracy improvements. The approach is empirically validated and released with code, benchmark, and a demo.

title: GVR-Coder: A Visual-Feedback Framework for Structured SVG Generation in Complex Document and Meeting Scenarios
summary: In demanding professional environments and meeting review scenarios, lengthy text often imposes a high cognitive load. To facilitate efficient information communication, transforming verbose text into logically clear diagrams is essential. Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) provide an effective representation for this purpose due to their editability and resolution independence. However, current research on Text-to-SVG generation remains hindered by three major challenges: (1) the scarcity of datasets for complex, logic-rich diagrams; (2) the absence of explicit layout priors, which leads to chaotic spatial arrangements; and (3) the lack of fine-grained visual feedback to validate rendered outputs and correct aesthetic defects. To address these challenges, at the data level, we introduce DocMeetSVG-100K, a large-scale SVG dataset tailored for document authoring and meeting review scenarios. At the model level, we propose GVR-Coder, a novel framework designed to generate high-quality logical diagrams from lengthy professional texts. Specifically, we adopt a curriculum-driven rejection sampling fine-tuning to progressively enhance the model's capability in modeling complex structures, while explicitly incorporating layout constraint knowledge during training. In addition, we introduce reinforcement learning from dual rendering feedback, a mechanism that provides implicit feedback through reward signals to jointly optimize structural complexity and visual aesthetics. Furthermore, we design a generate-verify-repair agent loop, which improves generation quality through explicit, fine-grained feedback and targeted refinement. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GVR-Coder outperforms competitive baselines and reliably produces logically coherent and visually appealing diagrams. Code and data are available at https://github.com/CurryaNa/GVR-Coder.

AI.tldr: Proposes DocMeetSVG-100K dataset and GVR-Coder for high-quality Text-to-SVG generation, leveraging layout priors, curriculum-based fine-tuning, dual rendering feedback, and a generate-verify-repair loop.
AI.motivation: Address three bottlenecks in text-to-SVG: (1) limited datasets for complex, logic-rich diagrams; (2) lack of explicit layout priors leading to chaotic layouts; (3) absence of fine-grained visual feedback for validating and refining outputs.
AI.method: Data: DocMeetSVG-100K dataset for document authoring/meeting review SVGs. Model: GVR-Coder. Techniques: (a) curriculum-driven rejection sampling fine-tuning to handle complex structures; (b) explicit incorporation of layout constraint knowledge during training; (c) reinforcement learning from dual rendering feedback to optimize structure and aesthetics; (d) generate-verify-repair agent loop for explicit, fine-grained feedback and refinement.
AI.result: Empirical evaluation shows GVR-Coder surpasses competitive baselines, producing logically coherent and visually appealing diagrams. Code and data released at the provided repository.
AI.conclusion: The framework mitigates data scarcity, imposes layout priors, and leverages iterative feedback to improve Text-to-SVG generation, enabling more effective communication of lengthy professional texts.

title: Large scale cross-regional remote sensing flood monitoring framework for operative mapping and impact analysis
comment: 37 pages, 11 figures, 9 tables. Preprint submitted to Earth Systems and Environment. This version has not been peer reviewed
summary:
Effective flood monitoring is critical for minimizing the impacts of flood disasters on populations and infrastructure. Yet reliable remote sensing across extensive and environmentally diverse regions remains challenging, as most segmentation algorithms lack the generalisation capacity required for large-scale application, while annotated flood data are scarce and unevenly distributed.
  This study presents an end-to-end multimodal framework for Russian Federation territories sustainable flood monitoring and damage assessment based on synthetic aperture radar data, multispectral imagery, and digital elevation models with their derivatives, forming a 21-channel input. Using a self-collected multimodal dataset covering seven Russian regions, two strategies for water surface detection under limited data conditions were compared: a supervised U-Net++ model and the self-supervised AnySat architecture pre-trained and fine-tuned for the segmentation task. Under the data conditions of this study, supervised learning proved more effective, while the AnySat-based approach offered greater stability and retains advantages for settings where larger unlabelled data or missing modalities at inference are expected.
  The best flood area predictions were used to estimate flood impact in urban areas in terms of the area affected, material damage, casualties, and ecological and agricultural impact. The estimations were conducted following the official methodology of the Russian Ministry of Emergency Situations. Applied to the 2019 Tulun flood, the obtained results closely matched official assessments, except for material damage, due to the open-source databases usage. The results demonstrate the potential of deep learning and multimodal satellite data integration for scalable, reliable flood monitoring across diverse environmental and data-limited conditions.

AI.tldr: A 21-channel multimodal remote-sensing pipeline (SAR, multispectral imagery, DEM derivatives) for flood segmentation over Russian regions, comparing supervised U-Net++ and self-supervised AnySat; supervised learning performs best under limited data; validated on 2019 Tulun flood with results close to official assessments except material damage due to open data; demonstrates potential for scalable flood monitoring under data scarcity.
AI.motivation: Fill the gap in reliable, scalable flood segmentation across large, heterogeneous regions where annotated data are scarce and data modalities may be incomplete; leverage multimodal data and self-supervised pretraining to improve generalization and robustness.
AI.method: End-to-end framework integrating SAR, multispectral imagery, and DEM derivatives into a 21-channel input. Evaluate two strategies: (1) supervised U-Net++ for segmentation, (2) self-supervised AnySat pre-trained and fine-tuned for segmentation. Dataset: seven Russian regions, with a self-collected multimodal dataset. Flood extent predictions used to estimate urban impact (area, material damage, casualties, ecological/agricultural impact) following official Russian EMS methodology.
AI.result: Under study conditions, supervised learning outperformed AnySat; AnySat offered stability and potential when large unlabeled datasets or missing modalities are expected. For the 2019 Tulun flood, flood-area estimates closely matched official assessments except material damage, due to open-source database limitations.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates the potential of deep learning with multimodal satellite data for scalable, reliable flood monitoring in diverse environments and data-limited contexts; underscores need for comprehensive datasets for accurate material-damage estimation; points to future work on leveraging more unlabeled data and handling missing modalities.

title: Old Tricks, New Models: How Simple Image Transformations Break Modern AI-based Content Moderation
summary: While automated content-moderation systems have become essential for screening harmful content at scale, conventional task-specific classifiers often provide limited policy cov- erage and contextual understanding. Recently, commercial multimodal moderation APIs built on large foundation models have been introduced with the promise of providing broader and more capable safety filters. In this work, we analyze whether this shift also yields more robust image moderation. We conduct a large-scale black-box evaluation on three established commercial image-moderation services and compare their robustness. By evaluating seven simple, model-agnostic image transformations across multiple providers, datasets, harm categories, perceptual-similarity constraints, and transformation intensities, we find that: (1) all three commercial services can be bypassed using inexpensive image transformations that require no gradients, surrogate models, or knowledge of the target system; (2) even fixed transformations such as color inversion and grayscale conversion induce unsafe-to-safe decision changes while preserving content that remains recognizable to humans; (3) their robustness varies substantially across datasets and harm categories, with multimodal content and self-harm exhibiting pronounced vulnerabilities. This yields the conclusion that replacing conventional moderation classifiers with foundation-model-based APIs does not, by itself, provide a reliable security boundary. Such systems must be evaluated under realistic transformations and deployed as one component of a layered moderation pipeline rather than as standalone safety filters.

AI.tldr: Foundation-model-based multimodal moderation APIs are not inherently robust; they can be bypassed with simple, gradient-free image transformations; robustness varies by dataset and harm category; layered, multi-component moderation recommended.
AI.motivation: Evaluate whether shifting to foundation-model-based APIs improves safety boundaries; test robustness against common, simple image transformations in a black-box setting.
AI.method: Three commercial moderation services; seven simple, model-agnostic image transformations; multiple datasets, harm categories, perceptual constraints, transformation intensities; black-box evaluation.
AI.result: All three services susceptible to bypass via inexpensive transformations; fixed transforms (color inversion, grayscale) can flip safety decisions while preserving human recognizability; vulnerabilities are dataset- and category-dependent (notably multimodal content and self-harm).
AI.conclusion: Replacing traditional classifiers with foundation-model-based APIs is not sufficient for robust safety; deploy within layered moderation and evaluate with realistic transformations.

title: Chem World: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Physics-Informed Framework for Trustworthy Chemical Property Prediction
summary: Chemical property prediction plays a critical role in accelerating scientific discovery in chemistry, materials science, and drug development. However, existing benchmarks often suffer from limited task diversity, fragmented datasets, and inconsistent evaluation protocols, making it challenging to systematically assess the reliability and generalization of AI models. In this work, we introduce Chem World, a comprehensive benchmark for chemical property prediction that integrates 17 diverse chemical datasets with over 800,000 molecular samples, covering various properties including density, electrical conductivity, solubility, and other molecular characteristics. Chem World provides a unified platform for evaluating AI models across multiple property prediction tasks. Furthermore, we propose Mixture-PINN, a physics-informed neural network based prediction framework that incorporates chemical prior knowledge into data-driven learning, improving the accuracy, robustness, and reliability of chemical property prediction. Extensive experiments on Chem World demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared with existing methods. By combining large-scale standardized evaluation with physics-informed learning, Chem World establishes a foundation for developing trustworthy AI systems for computational chemistry and advancing AI-driven scientific discovery.

AI.tldr: Chem World is a large-scale, unified benchmark of 17 chemical datasets (~800k samples) for property prediction, paired with Mixture-PINN, a physics-informed neural network leveraging chemical priors to improve accuracy and reliability.
AI.motivation: Address fragmentation in benchmarks (limited task diversity, fragmented datasets, inconsistent evaluation) and enable trustworthy AI in computational chemistry.
AI.method: Assemble 17 diverse datasets into a single benchmark platform; introduce Mixture-PINN that integrates chemical priors into data-driven learning; conduct extensive experiments comparing against existing methods.
AI.result: Chem World demonstrates improved accuracy, robustness, and reliability of chemical property prediction; the approach outperforms baselines on the unified benchmark.
AI.conclusion: Provides standardized evaluation and physics-informed learning, establishing a foundation for trustworthy AI in computational chemistry and accelerating AI-driven discovery.

title: Negative controls reveal volume-driven confounding in radiomics and imaging foundation model features
comment: 22 pages (including supplementary), 6 figures, 2 supplementary tables, 5 supplementary figures
summary: Radiomics and imaging foundation models promise non-invasive biomarkers of tumour biology, yet predictive signatures may reflect tumour volume or acquisition artifacts rather than meaningful image structure. We introduce READII-2-ROQC, an open-source framework that uses volume-preserving negative controls to assess whether radiomic and deep imaging features capture independent spatial signals. READII-2-ROQC generates voxel-perturbed images across tumour, background and whole-image regions using configurable randomization strategies, then compares feature behaviour and model performance between original and control images. Applied to three public cancer imaging cohorts, the framework processed 3,552 tumour volumes and extracted PyRadiomics and foundation-model features from original images and nine matched controls. Reproducing published survival and HPV-status signatures, we show that multiple models retain performance after spatial structure is destroyed, revealing volume-driven or contextual confounding, whereas others show perturbation-sensitive signal. READII-2-ROQC provides a scalable quality-control strategy for developing interpretable, biologically grounded imaging biomarkers and reproducible radiomics workflows.

AI.tldr: READII-2-ROQC provides volume-preserving negative controls to test whether radiomic and deep features capture independent spatial signals, revealing volume-induced confounding in several models and offering a scalable QC framework for imaging biomarkers.
AI.motivation: Radiomic signatures risk reflecting tumor volume or acquisition artifacts rather than meaningful biology; there is a need for quality-control methods that disentangle true spatial biology from confounding effects to ensure interpretable, robust biomarkers.
AI.method: Create voxel-perturbed images across tumor, background, and whole-image regions using configurable randomization strategies to destroy spatial structure while preserving volume. Compare feature behavior and model performance between original and control images. Apply to three public cancer imaging cohorts (3,552 tumor volumes) and extract PyRadiomics and foundation-model features from original and nine matched controls.
AI.result: Reproduced published survival and HPV-status signatures; several models maintained predictive performance even after spatial structure destruction, indicating volume-driven or contextual confounding. Other models showed perturbation-sensitive signals, implying genuine spatial information captured by features/models.
AI.conclusion: READII-2-ROQC offers a scalable quality-control strategy to develop interpretable, biologically grounded imaging biomarkers and to enhance reproducibility in radiomics workflows by identifying and accounting for volume- or context-driven confounding.

title: Qwen-UI-Agent Technical Report: Toward Next-Generation Real-World Centric Foundation GUI Agents
summary:
GUI agents have the potential to become a general purpose executor over existing digital devices. To advance them toward real-world use, we envision agents that operate reliably on real devices, execute workflows across platforms, combine GUI interaction with CLI execution, complete long-horizon tasks, proactively initiate useful services, and autonomously improve their capabilities with minimal human effort. Guided by this vision, we present Qwen-UI-Agent, a real-world centric foundation GUI agent spanning mobile, computer-use, web, and DeepSearch environments. Qwen-UI-Agent combines diverse sandbox environments with a large-scale real-device mobile runtime. Its unified action space interleaves GUI operations with CLI execution and generates batched actions in a single model turn. An AutoResearch-style data flywheel uses agents to construct tasks and environments, diagnose failures, and plan subsequent iterations. Online RL supports training on trajectories exceeding 100 turns, with over 10,000 concurrent environments accelerating rollout. A lightweight harness layer supports proactive service initiation and stateful workflows across mobile and computer.
  Across a broad suite of evaluations, Qwen-UI-Agent sets state-of-the-art performance on mobile-use benchmarks while delivering competitive performance on computer- and browser-use tasks against frontier models, including Opus 4.8, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.6 Sol. On mobile use, it achieves 82.1% on MobileWorld, 92.2% on MobileWorld-Real, and 97.5% on AndroidDaily. On computer use, it achieves 79.5% on OSWorld-Verified and a 40.0% partial-progress score on OSWorld-v2. On browser use and GUI grounding, it achieves 73.6% on WebArena and 81.5% on ScreenSpot-Pro, respectively.

AI.tldr: A real-world centric GUI agent (Qwen-UI-Agent) unifies GUI and CLI actions across mobile, computer, and web, leveraging sandbox + real device runtime, an AutoResearch flywheel, and online RL to achieve state-of-the-art mobile performance and competitive results elsewhere.
AI.motivation: To advance GUI agents toward reliable, cross-device, long-horizon, self-improving autonomous agents suitable for real-world use.
AI.method: Unified action space blending GUI operations with CLI; multi-environment sandbox plus real-device runtime; AutoResearch-style data flywheel; online RL with long trajectories and massive parallelism; lightweight harness for proactive services and stateful workflows across mobile and computer.
AI.result: State-of-the-art mobile-use benchmarks; competitive on computer- and browser-use tasks relative to frontier models; specific scores include MobileWorld 82.1, MobileWorld-Real 92.2, AndroidDaily 97.5; OSWorld-Verified 79.5; OSWorld-v2 40.0 partial-progress; WebArena 73.6; ScreenSpot-Pro 81.5.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates strong real-world GUI automation across platforms with scalable training and proactive service capabilities, but further real-world deployment studies and broader generalization assessments are warranted.

title: From Expert Reduction to Behavioral Divergence: Tracing Numerical State through Sparse MoE Inference
summary: Mathematically equivalent expert-reduction orders can produce observably different sparse-MoE executions. We isolate this effect in native DeepSeek-V4-Flash by freezing local MoE state and varying only aggregation semantics. Four schemes separate operand representation from accumulator precision. At one layer-5 fork, 720 A-mode orders yield 10 continuation basins; 720 B-mode orders form 360 exact structural classes and 11 basins. Under one Chinese prompt, the B classes split into 202 layoffs, 113 hiring, and 45 other continuations. Maximum-L-infinity B-branch selection separates 12, 24, and 36 of 50 prompts by 8, 16, and 32 tokens. Across 192 persistent trajectories per scheme, P32, A, and B change every native-reference route trajectory, while C preserves routes, token sequences, and texts. A separate 192-trajectory C check matches native MoE, post-mHC, next-router, and LM states bitwise. For one controlled B branch, exact post-mHC endpoint reconstruction reproduces the measured downstream trajectory. At the next decode boundary, exact FP64 reconstruction of the branch's full persistent state yields agreement for 301 downstream post-mHC states, 301 persistent-state checkpoints, 301 routes, predictions, and text over seven steps, given the same naturally generated next input. These controls identify post-mHC as an intra-token boundary and full persistent state as a cross-token continuation boundary. Identical tokens need not imply identical autoregressive state: divergence can survive a token boundary and become visible later. These results make expert operand conversion, accumulator precision, and reduction order part of a numerical compatibility contract for sparse-MoE runtimes and hardware backends. They establish controlled causal possibility, not deployment incidence; C's order invariance is limited to evaluated six-term states and schedules.

AI.tldr: Equivalence in expert-reduction orders does not guarantee identical sparse-MoE behavior; aggregations semantics, operand representations, and precision influence observables. By freezing MoE state and varying aggregation, the study uncovers multiple trajectory families, state reconstructions, and boundary effects (intra-token vs cross-token), arguing for a numerical compatibility contract across backends.
AI.motivation: To investigate reproducibility and numerical stability of sparse-MoE computations across hardware/backends by isolating aggregation semantics and precision choices, revealing hidden dependencies not captured by nominal equivalence.
AI.method: Systematically freeze local MoE state and vary only aggregation semantics across four schemes (operands vs accumulators). Analyze two-mode representations (A/B) across many orders (A/B) at a layer-5 fork; assess 192 persistent trajectories per scheme; perform post-mHC and FP64 reconstructions; compare with native MoE states and routes; use a controlled Chinese prompt to reveal class splits; detect intra-token vs cross-token boundaries via exact reconstructions.
AI.result: Found large combinatorial divergence: 720 A-mode orders yield 10 continuation basins; 720 B-mode orders yield 360 exact classes and 11 basins; B-class splits under Chinese prompts into 202 layoffs, 113 hiring, 45 other; maximum-L-infinity B-branch selection separates multiple prompts by token counts; across 192 trajectories, A/B vary while C preserves; a 192-trajectory C confirms match with native states; exact post-mHC endpoint reconstructions reproduce downstream trajectories; FP64 reconstruction yields agreement across seven steps for 301 downstream states/checkpoints/routes/text; post-mHC is intra-token boundary; full persistent state is cross-token continuation boundary; identical tokens don't ensure identical autoregressive state; results imply operand conversion, accumulator precision, and reduction order form a numerical compatibility contract for sparse-MoE runtimes and hardware backends; C invariance limited to six-term states/schedules.
AI.conclusion: The study identifies critical boundary concepts (post-mHC vs persistent state) and demonstrates controlled causal possibilities rather than deployment incidence. It emphasizes that equivalence of reduction orders is not enough for perceptually identical outputs; a numerical compatibility contract is needed for robust cross-backend sparse-MoE execution. C’s order invariance is limited to the tested six-term states/schedules.

title: ViewMind3D: Modular View-Aware Inference for Training-Free 3D-QA
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and vision-language models (VLMs) have enabled new possibilities for 3D question answering (3D-QA), a key capability for embodied AI and robotic perception. However, most existing methods rely on 3D-specific training or fine-tuning with costly annotations, limiting their scalability and real-world applicability. We present \textbf{ViewMind3D}, a fully training-free and modular framework for 3D spatial reasoning over multi-view observations of a scene without requiring complete 3D reconstruction. The framework decomposes the 3D-QA task into four interpretable components: (1) question-driven multi-view selection, (2) guided visual grounding with language-conditioned object cues, (3) spatial context encoding via a bird's-eye-view (BEV) viewpoint indicator, and (4) structured answer generation through role-based reasoning. This design enables structured, robust, and interpretable reasoning without requiring model tuning. Experimental results on ScanQA and SQA3D show that ViewMind3D achieves competitive performance compared to prior training-free and fine-tuned 3D-LLMs. In particular, our method improves performance on spatially grounded question types, such as ``What'' questions in SQA3D, while maintaining strong overall accuracy (50.8\%) and achieving 73.4 CIDEr on ScanQA. These results demonstrate that effective 3D reasoning can be achieved through modular orchestration of general-purpose LLMs and VLMs for robotic perception in real-world environments.

AI.tldr: ViewMind3D is a training-free, modular framework for 3D-QA that orchestrates LLMs and VLMs over multi-view observations with BEV encoding and role-based reasoning, achieving competitive results on ScanQA and SQA3D without 3D reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Reduce dependency on 3D-specific training/fine-tuning and costly 3D annotations; enable scalable, robust 3D spatial reasoning using general-purpose models in real-world robotics.
AI.method: Decompose 3D-QA into four modules: (1) question-driven multi-view selection, (2) language-conditioned visual grounding cueing objects, (3) spatial context encoding via BEV viewpoint indicator, (4) structured answer generation through role-based reasoning; fully training-free and does not rely on complete 3D reconstruction.
AI.result: Competitive with prior training-free and fine-tuned 3D-LLMs on ScanQA and SQA3D; notable gains on spatially grounded questions (e.g., 'What' in SQA3D); reported accuracy 50.8% and CIDEr 73.4 on ScanQA.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates that modular orchestration of general-purpose LLMs and VLMs can achieve effective 3D reasoning for robotic perception without task-specific 3D training, preserving interpretability and scalability.

title: CDAE: Enhancing Perturbation Robustness in Pretrained Language Models with Contrastive Denoising
comment: Submitted to 16th International Conference on Computer and Knowledge Engineering (ICCKE 2026)
summary: Pre-trained language models have significantly improved sentence representation learning, yet their embedding remain sensitive to semantic preserving textual perturbations such as synonym substitution, masking and word dropout. This work proposes a lightweight Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE) that refines pre-trained BERT embedding by jointly optimizing contrastive and reconstruction objective to learn perturbation-invariant representation. We evaluate the proposed framework using multiple perturbation strategies with varying strengths and compare it against the original BERT embeddings and SimCSE. Experimental results show that CDAE consistently preserves higher embedding similarity under perturbations, with the improvements becoming more pronounced as framework effectively enhances representation stability while preserving semantic information, highlighting perturbation-invariant learning as a promising direction for improving sentence embeddings. The source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/ComputationIASBS/CDAE

AI.tldr: A lightweight CDAE refines BERT embeddings via joint contrastive and reconstruction objectives to achieve perturbation-invariant sentence representations, outperforming standard BERT and SimCSE under synonym substitution, masking, and dropout perturbations.
AI.motivation: Pre-trained embeddings are sensitive to semantic-preserving textual perturbations; robust, perturbation-invariant representations are needed for reliable sentence semantics.
AI.method: Contrastive Denoising Autoencoder (CDAE): fine-tunes a pre-trained encoder by combining a reconstruction loss (denoising perturbed embeddings) with a contrastive loss that brings augmented views of the same sentence closer while separating others; benchmarks include variants of perturbations and comparisons against BERT and SimCSE; open-source code provided.
AI.result: CDAE maintains higher embedding similarity under perturbations, with larger gains under stronger perturbations, indicating improved stability without sacrificing semantic information compared to BERT and SimCSE.
AI.conclusion: Perturbation-invariant learning is a promising direction for robust sentence embeddings; CDAE offers a lightweight, effective approach with open-source code for replication.

title: Information Bottleneck Learning for Faithful Time Series Forecasting Explanations
summary: As forecasts increasingly drive decisions in fields such as energy, transportation, and healthcare, understanding the historical data behind these predictions has become as crucial as the predictions themselves. Although existing interpretable-by-design forecasters reveal their internal structures, they offer no guarantee that these structures faithfully reflect the underlying evidence driving the predictions. In contrast, while faithfulness-oriented methods explicitly verify model behavior, they are almost exclusively designed for post-hoc classification tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose IB-Forecast, an inherently interpretable multivariate time-series forecasting framework. It decomposes forecasting into a learned periodic component and a residual component computed with explainable masks over input tokens. With a budget-constrained information bottleneck, end-to-end optimization enables users to directly control explanation sparsity. With a rigorous faithfulness evaluation protocol, extensive experiments demonstrate that IB-Forecast matches the forecasting error of leading black-box models while providing faithful explanations at no additional inference cost. Furthermore, under a matched sparsity budget, these native explanations consistently surpass gradient-based, occlusion-based, and optimization-based baselines across all evaluated datasets. Ultimately, whereas the native explanations of existing interpretable forecasters exhibit poor faithfulness, IB-Forecast guarantees high explanation fidelity, requiring only 14-20% of the observations to deliver low-error predictions.

AI.tldr: A faithful, inherently interpretable multivariate time-series forecaster (IB-Forecast) with explainable masks and a budgeted information bottleneck, achieving competitive accuracy with superior faithfulness and sparsity.
AI.motivation: Forecast-driven decisions demand explanations that faithfully reflect evidence; existing interpretable forecasters often lack faithfulness, while faithfulness-oriented methods are mainly designed for post-hoc classification tasks.
AI.method: IB-Forecast decomposes forecasting into a learned periodic component and a residual component guided by explainable masks over input tokens; uses a budget-constrained information bottleneck for end-to-end optimization to control explanation sparsity.
AI.result: Matches the forecasting error of leading black-box models; provides faithful explanations at no extra inference cost; under matched sparsity budgets, native explanations outperform common baselines (gradient-, occlusion-, optimization-based) across datasets; explanations rely on 14-20% of observations to deliver low-error predictions.
AI.conclusion: IB-Forecast delivers high-fidelity, native explanations for time-series forecasting with competitive accuracy, addressing the faithfulness-gap and enabling sparse, faithful insights without extra inference cost.

title: VisualRouter: Query-Grounded Visual Sampling for Long Video Understanding
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) have achieved significant progress in video understanding, yet understanding long videos remains challenging due to the large number of visual tokens and limited context windows. Visual sampling provides a practical solution by selecting an informative subset of frames. However, existing methods typically either rely on relevance-aware sampling, leading to redundant frame selection and insufficient temporal coverage, or adopt a fixed sampling strategy regardless of query type. In this paper, we propose VisualRouter, a training-free and plug-and-play framework for query-grounded visual sampling. VisualRouter first classifies each query as either global or local and then applies the corresponding sampling strategy. For global queries, it employs a relevance-coverage hybrid strategy that preserves temporal coverage while retaining query-relevant visual evidence. For local queries, it adopts an event-aware frame selection strategy that performs event partitioning, segment-level frame allocation, and intra-event frame selection, jointly balancing relevance, coverage, and diversity with a limited number of input frames. Experiments show that VisualRouter consistently improves multiple LVLMs over uniform sampling, achieving gains of 5.2%, 7.7%, and 11.6% on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU with Qwen2.5-VL-7B, and outperforming existing training-free visual sampling methods under the same setting.

AI.tldr: VisualRouter is a training-free, plug-and-play framework for query-grounded visual sampling in LVLMs. It classifies each query as global or local and applies corresponding sampling strategies to improve long-video understanding, outperforming uniform sampling and existing training-free baselines.
AI.motivation: Long videos contain many visual tokens and limited context, making uniform or relevance-only sampling ineffective. A query-aware sampling approach that balances relevance, temporal coverage, and diversity is needed to improve LVLM performance on long videos.
AI.method: VisualRouter uses a training-free query classifier to label queries as global or local. Global queries use a relevance-coverage hybrid sampling to keep temporal coverage while retaining query-relevant frames. Local queries use an event-aware sampling strategy with event partitioning, segment-level frame allocation, and intra-event frame selection to balance relevance, coverage, and diversity within a limited frame budget.
AI.result: Empirical gains are reported across datasets: 5.2%, 7.7%, and 11.6% on Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and MLVU when using Qwen2.5-VL-7B, outperforming existing training-free visual sampling methods under the same setting.
AI.conclusion: VisualRouter provides a scalable, training-free solution for query-grounded sampling in LVLMs, improving performance on long-video tasks and offering a practical plug-and-play component for LVLM pipelines.

title: AI and Authenticity in Islamic Research: A Critical Evaluation of Generative AI Reliability, Hallucination, and Source Fidelity in Quranic, Hadith, and Fiqh Knowledge
summary:
Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly used by Muslims for religious guidance, Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith explanation, jurisprudential rulings, and Islamic education. Despite its growing adoption, there is limited empirical evidence on whether current AI systems provide authentic, verifiable, and trustworthy Islamic knowledge suitable for high-trust religious contexts. This study evaluates six leading generative AI systems using fifty realistic open-ended Islamic questions covering Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith, Fiqh, ethics, pastoral advice, and Madhhab-sensitive topics. Responses were collected under real-world conditions from participants in Australia and the United Kingdom and analysed using a mixed-method framework examining domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, jurisprudential consistency, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation.
  The study addresses four research questions: (1) How accurate and authentic are AI-generated responses across major Islamic knowledge domains? (2) To what extent do AI systems produce hallucinations, incomplete citations, or unverifiable religious references? (3) How consistently do models handle jurisprudential disagreement, Madhhab diversity, and uncertainty? (4) Are current AI systems sufficiently reliable for religious guidance, Islamic education, and scholarly research?
  Overall, current generative AI systems are valuable as assistive tools for introductory Islamic learning but should not be treated as authoritative sources for religious rulings or Islamic research without verification against authenticated primary sources and qualified scholarly expertise. This study provides one of the first comprehensive empirical evaluations of AI reliability within Islamic knowledge, offering practical guidance for researchers, educators, AI developers, and the wider Muslim community.

AI.tldr: Comprehensive empirical evaluation shows current generative AI is useful for introductory Islamic learning but not reliable for authoritative religious rulings; verification with primary sources and qualified scholars is essential.
AI.motivation: Fill the empirical gap: there is limited evidence on whether AI systems provide authentic, verifiable, and trustworthy Islamic knowledge suitable for high-trust religious contexts.
AI.method: Six leading generative AI systems were evaluated using fifty realistic open-ended Islamic questions spanning Qur'anic interpretation, Hadith, Fiqh, ethics, pastoral guidance, and Madhhab-sensitive topics. Data were collected under real-world conditions from participants in Australia and the United Kingdom. A mixed-method framework assessed domain accuracy, citation verification, hallucinations, jurisprudential consistency, uncertainty handling, source provenance, and geographical variation.
AI.result: AI systems function as valuable assistive tools for introductory Islamic learning but are not reliable authoritative sources for religious rulings or Islamic research without verification against authenticated primary sources and qualified scholarly expertise.
AI.conclusion: The study provides one of the first comprehensive empirical evaluations of AI reliability in Islamic knowledge and offers practical guidance for researchers, educators, AI developers, and the wider Muslim community.

title: LM-GRASP: Instance-Specific Language Models for Combinatorial Construction via Online Imitation Learning
summary:
Machine learning for combinatorial optimization typically relies on neural constructors trained via reinforcement learning on large offline datasets for a fixed problem class-incurring high pretraining costs and generalizing poorly outside the training distribution. We propose an alternative: a metaheuristic framework that reformulates the randomized constructive phase of GRASP as an online imitation learning task, trained from scratch on each problem instance. A local search procedure acts as an expert oracle, while a decoder-only Transformer serves as the constructive policy. Unlike classical GRASP, which relies on static, myopic heuristic rules based on localized scalar costs, our approach is fully data-driven: the construction policy emerges from high-quality solutions discovered during the search itself, with no problem-specific feature engineering required.
  We instantiate this as LM-GRASP, a hybrid metaheuristic following an iterative learn-infer-improve cycle, training the policy online via behavioral cloning on a dynamic archive of elite trajectories-no external data or offline pretraining needed. The pipeline interfaces with the domain solely through the objective evaluator used by local search.
  Evaluated on the Taillard PFSP benchmark (ta51-ta60), the most discriminating block due to half its optima being unknown, LM-GRASP outperforms GPU-GRASP by 28.4 makespan units on average-comparable to the gain from GPU acceleration over sequential execution (27.2 units), though with overlapping standard deviations. This suggests instance-specific, online-trained language models are a promising, practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, especially for landscapes resistant to classical greedy construction.

AI.tldr: A data-driven online imitation-learning framework (LM-GRASP) rethinks the constructive phase of GRASP as a per-instance online learning task, using a local search expert and a transformer policy to construct solutions without offline pretraining.
AI.motivation: Address high pretraining costs and poor generalization of neural constructors trained offline by proposing an online, instance-specific learning loop that discovers quality constructions during search.
AI.method: An iterative learn-infer-improve cycle where a decoder-only Transformer acts as the constructive policy, trained by behavioral cloning from an online archive of elite trajectories generated by a local-search expert oracle (no external data). The method interfaces with the domain solely via the objective evaluator, and uses a dynamic elite-trajectory archive to guide policy learning.
AI.result: On the Taillard PFSP benchmark (ta51–ta60), LM-GRASP outperforms GPU-GRASP by 28.4 makespan units on average, a gain comparable to the 27.2-unit improvement from GPU acceleration over sequential execution, though with overlapping standard deviations.
AI.conclusion: Instance-specific, online-trained language models can be a practical alternative to hand-engineered constructors, particularly for problem landscapes that are poorly served by classical greedy construction.

title: Can Vision-Language Models Reason about AI Edits in Images?
summary: Detection and localization of AI-tampered images are critical for trustworthy AI, yet modern generative models have made such manipulations increasingly difficult to identify. While traditional binary classifiers can detect image tampering, they lack interpretability and generalization. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) offer a promising alternative due to their strong visual understanding and reasoning capabilities; however, existing approaches typically rely on supervised finetuning with curated explanations rather than exploiting their inherent reasoning capabilities. In this work, we investigate whether VLMs can be trained to reason about AI-generated image edits using reinforcement learning (RL) rather than explicit reasoning supervision. Motivated by the success in Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), an RL technique that incentivizes the model to reason by generating thinking traces prior to giving the final answer, we propose a GRPO-based training framework that utilizes simple accuracy and format rewards. Given an input image, the model produces a structured reasoning trace and predicts whether the image has been tampered with. A lightweight segmentation model is then guided by the reasoning output to generate pixel-level localization masks. Experiments across multiple image manipulation datasets demonstrate that our approach achieves competitive detection and localization performance compared to state-of-the-art image forgery detectors, despite requiring substantially weaker supervision. We introduce effective intersection over union (eff-IoU), a unified metric to jointly evaluate detection and localization. These results suggest that reinforcement learning provides an effective and scalable mechanism for teaching VLMs to reason about AI-generated content.

AI.tldr: A GRPO-based RL framework trains vision-language models to generate reasoning traces about AI-generated image edits, jointly predicting tampering and guiding a segmentation head for pixel-level localization; achieves competitive detection/localization with weak supervision and introduces eff-IoU for joint evaluation.
AI.motivation: Binary tampering detectors often lack interpretability and generalization. Vision-language models (VLMs) offer reasoning capabilities, but existing methods rely on supervised explanations. This work explores whether RL-driven reasoning traces can train VLMs to detect and localize AI edits with weaker supervision.
AI.method: A GRPO-based training framework where the model generates a structured reasoning trace and predicts tampering. A lightweight segmentation model is guided by the reasoning output to produce pixel-level masks. Rewards are simple accuracy and formatting signals to encourage reasoning before answering. Evaluation uses multiple manipulation datasets and a new eff-IoU metric to jointly measure detection and localization.
AI.result: The approach achieves competitive detection and localization performance compared to state-of-the-art image forgery detectors while requiring substantially weaker supervision. The authors propose eff-IoU as a unified metric to jointly evaluate detection and localization.
AI.conclusion: Reinforcement learning can effectively teach VLMs to reason about AI-generated content. The GRPO-based framework demonstrates scalable, interpretable reasoning for tampering detection and localization, with potential for further improvements and broader applicability.

title: Operationally Guided Placement-Aware Learning for Industrial Online 3D Bin Packing
summary: The online three-dimensional bin packing problem (3D-BPP) is a longstanding challenge in logistics and industrial palletizing. Recent learning-based methods use a learned policy to select among feasible candidate placements. Performance depends on the candidate generator and representation, especially in industrial settings where packings must be space-efficient, stable, compact, and balanced. However, prior work has mainly optimized the policy, while candidate generation and representation remain largely geometry-driven. We address this gap with OPAL, an operationally guided placement-aware learning framework for industrial online 3D-BPP which combines an Operationally Guided Empty-Maximal-Space generator (OG-EMS), an operational representation for each candidate placement, and a masked ranking policy trained with proximal policy optimization. OG-EMS evaluates multiple anchors within each free-space region and prioritizes low, well-supported, compact, and spatially diverse placements. An xLSTM-based Placement Encoder models dependencies among geometric and operational candidate attributes, while a lightweight recurrent core combines the resulting embeddings with the current item and pallet state to rank feasible actions. On the BED-BPP benchmark, OPAL achieves a mean space utilization of 0.49, with improvements of 15.1% from operationally guided candidate generation and 6.3% from learned ranking, while maintaining robust inference-time performance.

AI.tldr: OPAL is an online 3D-BPP framework combining an operationally guided candidate generator (OG-EMS), an operational placement representation, and a masked ranking policy (PPO) using an xLSTM placement encoder; it achieves improved space utilization on BED-BPP with robust inference-time performance.
AI.motivation: Existing learning-based 3D-BPP approaches mainly optimize the policy, while candidate generation and representation remain largely geometry-driven. There is a need for space-efficient, stable, and balanced industrial packings through operationally guided candidate generation and representation.
AI.method: OG-EMS evaluates multiple anchors within each free-space region to produce candidate placements prioritizing low, well-supported, compact, and spatially diverse options. Each candidate has an operational representation. An xLSTM-based Placement Encoder models dependencies among geometric and operational attributes. A lightweight recurrent core combines embeddings with the current item and pallet state to rank feasible actions, trained with proximal policy optimization.
AI.result: On the BED-BPP benchmark, OPAL achieves a mean space utilization of 0.49, with improvements of 15.1% from operationally guided candidate generation and 6.3% from learned ranking, while maintaining robust inference-time performance.
AI.conclusion: OPAL demonstrates that integrating operationally guided candidate generation and representation with a learned ranking policy yields notable gains in space utilization for online 3D-BPP and is suitable for industrial settings due to efficient inference and modular design.

authors: Jacobus G. M. van der Linden
title: Search Strategies for Optimal Classification and Regression Trees
summary: Optimal decision trees (ODTs) are compact, interpretable machine learning models that globally optimize a given objective, but their scalability remains challenging. While recent work has proposed a variety of search strategies to improve scalability, the precise contribution of each strategy remains unclear. To address this gap, we introduce a general algorithmic framework for ODTs that instantiates previously used search strategies and enables the definition of new ones. This provides a common lens through which to understand and compare different strategies, which we use to empirically investigate the effect of 18 search strategies. Compared to the state of the art, the best strategy in our evaluation achieves significantly better anytime performance for classification, and improves runtime by more than an order of magnitude for regression.

AI.tldr: A general, unifying framework for Optimal Decision Trees (ODTs) is proposed to instantiate and compare prior search strategies; an empirical study of 18 strategies shows the best one improves classification anytime performance and speeds up regression by over an order of magnitude relative to the state of the art.
AI.motivation: ODTs globally optimize objectives and are powerful and interpretable, but scalability is hindered by a lack of understanding of how individual search strategies contribute. A unified framework is needed to clarify, compare, and extend strategies.
AI.method: Introduce a general algorithmic framework for ODTs that can instantiate previously used search strategies and support new ones; conduct an empirical study by implementing 18 distinct search strategies within this framework to evaluate their impact on performance.
AI.result: Compared to state-of-the-art, the best strategy achieves significantly better anytime performance for classification and reduces regression runtime by more than an order of magnitude.
AI.conclusion: A unified, extensible framework clarifies the role of search strategies in ODTs, enabling fair comparisons and enabling substantial performance gains, particularly for classification and regression tasks.

title: Towards Real-Time PixOOD: Efficient Anomaly Segmentation for Autonomous Vehicles
comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 3 tables. Accepted at the Efficient Deep Learning: Methods and Applications workshop, 35th International Conference on Artificial Neural Networks (ICANN 2026)
summary: Real-time anomaly segmentation is essential for the safety of autonomous systems. Although recent approaches offer high accuracy, their computational cost limits their deployment on embedded hardware. This work presents an efficient and accelerated pipeline designed for both embedded and desktop platforms, targeting the autonomous driving and railway domains. The proposed approach reformulates the Neyman-Pearson scoring stage of PixOOD, a state-of-the-art out-of-distribution detection method, and deploys the full pipeline through hardware-optimized TensorRT compilation, reaching up to 182 FPS on a desktop NVIDIA RTX 4060 GPU and 75 FPS on the NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin embedded platform, respectively 20x and 18x faster than the original baseline. The achieved results demonstrate that advanced anomaly segmentation can be efficiently deployed for onboard processing in autonomous driving and railway applications.

AI.tldr: Efficient, hardware-accelerated real-time anomaly segmentation for autonomous driving and railway, using a TensorRT-optimized pipeline that reformulates the Neyman-Pearson scoring in PixOOD, achieving up to 182 FPS on desktop and 75 FPS on embedded hardware (Jetson AGX Orin), ~18–20x faster than the baseline.
AI.motivation: High accuracy anomaly segmentation methods exist but are computationally heavy, hindering deployment on embedded platforms. There is a need for an efficient, real-time, hardware-accelerated pipeline suitable for safety-critical autonomous systems in both driving and railway domains.
AI.method: Reformulation of the Neyman-Pearson scoring stage of the PixOOD out-of-distribution detection method, followed by deploying the full pipeline via hardware-optimized TensorRT compilation to target desktop and embedded hardware (RTX 4060 and Jetson AGX Orin).
AI.result: Achieves 182 FPS on desktop NVIDIA RTX 4060 and 75 FPS on NVIDIA Jetson AGX Orin; performance improvements of ~20x and ~18x over the original baseline, enabling real-time onboard anomaly segmentation.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates that advanced anomaly segmentation can be efficiently deployed for onboard processing in autonomous driving and railway applications, bridging the gap between high-accuracy methods and real-time, resource-constrained environments.

title: LLM-Guided Evolutionary Search for Constraint Model Reformulation to Improve Solver Efficiency
summary: Combinatorial problems appear in numerous industrial applications. A common approach is to formulate these problems as declarative constraint models that can subsequently be compiled to and solved by a range of back-end solvers. Recent work shows that Large Language Models (LLMs) can produce correct models from natural language, but even a correct model can be expensive to solve because performance remains sensitive to modelling choices. In this work, we investigate whether LLMs can automate performance-oriented model reformulation. Inspired by Automatic Heuristic Design (AHD), we use an evolutionary framework in which an LLM proposes candidate reformulations that are verified and benchmarked against the user-defined baseline model. We compare AHD-adapted search strategies that control which prior attempts, instructions, and measured feedback enter each prompt. Existing retention strategies prioritize recency or performance, but do not explicitly diversify the context. To cover this gap, we introduce Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR), which applies Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) to instance-level runtime vectors to retain behaviourally diverse attempts. We systematically evaluate the strategies on eight CSPLib problems using validation-based final model selection. The results show that: (i) iterative reformulation can produce substantial held-out speedups; (ii) strategies that keep the retained context diverse outperform those that retain only recent or the fastest attempts; and (iii) validation-based selection improves the held-out speedup of every strategy.

AI.tldr: LLMs can automate performance-oriented reformulation of declarative constraint models via an evolutionary, verification-based loop; proposes Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) with MMR to diversify retained attempts; validated on CSPLib problems, achieving speedups and improved held-out performance.
AI.motivation: Performance of constraint models is highly sensitive to modelling choices; automating reformulation aims to improve solver efficiency without manual tuning.
AI.method: An evolutionary framework where an LLM proposes reformulations; proposals are verified and benchmarked against a user baseline; retention strategies govern which past attempts, instructions, and feedback enter prompts; Profile-Diverse Retention (PDR) applies Maximal Marginal Relevance to instance-level runtime vectors to retain behaviorally diverse attempts.
AI.result: Iterative reformulation yields substantial held-out speedups; diversity-oriented retention strategies outperform purely recency- or performance-based approaches; validation-based final model selection improves held-out speedups across all strategies.
AI.conclusion: LLMs can effectively automate performance-oriented reformulation for declarative constraint models; incorporating context diversity through PDR and validating final models enhances performance gains, as demonstrated on CSPLib benchmarks.

title: Multi-channel Uplift Policy Learning
summary: E-commerce platforms must allocate fixed marketing budgets across multiple channels to maximize business utility. However, standard predict-then-optimize (PTO) paradigms fail in this compositional space due to observational confounding and severe extrapolation. We formulate this challenge as a simplex-constrained uplift decision problem and propose ReAlloc, a fast-slow causal framework. Specifically, an agile Orthogonal Teacher extracts unbiased local gradients from short-term logs, while an Explanation-Guided Student distills them into a structured marginal field over long-term horizons. This design enables support-aware, conservative decisions that capture cross-channel substitutions. Extensive simulations and large-scale online A/B tests on Taobao platform demonstrate that ReAlloc achieves simultaneous lifts in both pay order and income.

AI.tldr: ReAlloc is a fast-slow causal framework for simplex-constrained uplift in multi-channel marketing budgets, yielding simultaneous gains in pay order and income in simulations and Taobao A/B tests.
AI.motivation: PTO fails in compositional, confounded channels due to observational bias and severe extrapolation; there is a need for cross-channel substitution-aware, conservative optimization under budget constraints.
AI.method: Formulate as a simplex-constrained uplift decision. Use an Orthogonal Teacher to extract unbiased local gradients from short-term logs and an Explanation-Guided Student to distill them into a structured marginal field over long-term horizons, enabling support-aware, conservative decisions that capture cross-channel substitutions.
AI.result: Extensive simulations and large-scale online A/B tests on Taobao demonstrate simultaneous lifts in both pay order and income.
AI.conclusion: Integrating fast local causal signals with long-horizon marginal reasoning enables robust, scalable multi-channel budget allocation under confounding, with practical gains observed in production

title: AuricularWorld: Hierarchical Action-Guided World Modeling for Fine-Grained Auricular Structure Segmentation from CT Scans
summary: Fine-grained segmentation of auricular structures in CT is challenging because the ear occupies a small image region, cartilage boundaries are highly irregular, and interfaces between cartilage and surrounding soft tissues are often ambiguous. Clinical annotations may also include both composite structures containing cartilage and adjacent skin and their corresponding cartilage-only regions, producing nested and overlapping labels. We propose a world-model-based segmentation framework that enables iterative anatomical reasoning beyond conventional feed-forward prediction. Built on an encoder-decoder architecture, the framework introduces a deterministic recurrent state-space model into the intermediate latent space. Multi-scale encoder features and partially decoded representations are fused to form a structural observation that initializes the latent dynamics. During inference, the model performs a three-step latent rollout without ground-truth guidance. Hierarchical anatomical actions update the recurrent state and progressively refine the latent representation. The resulting latent trajectory is projected back into the decoder and combined with high-resolution features to produce the final segmentation. To learn reliable latent transitions, we introduce a balanced hierarchical action objective that addresses foreground sparsity, missing anatomical groups, and imbalance between add and remove operations. Extensive experiments show that the proposed framework consistently improves segmentation accuracy and reduces HD95 by more than 43% for small, irregular, and overlapping auricular structures in CT. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of latent world-model reasoning for challenging medical image segmentation.

AI.tldr: World-model-based segmentation with a deterministic recurrent state-space model in latent space, enabling iterative anatomical reasoning for fine-grained auricular CT segmentation; three-step latent rollout with hierarchical actions; improves HD95 by >43% on small/irregular overlapping structures.
AI.motivation: Challenges: small ear region, irregular cartilage boundaries, ambiguous tissue interfaces; nested/overlapping annotations complicate training; conventional feed-forward methods insufficient.
AI.method: Encoder-decoder backbone; deterministic recurrent state-space model in latent space; structural observation from multi-scale features and partial decodings to initialize dynamics; three-step latent rollout during inference; hierarchical anatomical actions update state and refine latent; latent trajectory decoded and fused with high-res features to output segmentation; balanced hierarchical action objective addressing sparsity, missing groups, and add/remove imbalance.
AI.result: Experiments show consistent accuracy gains and >43% reduction in HD95 for small, irregular, overlapping auricular structures in CT.
AI.conclusion: Latent world-model reasoning enhances segmentation performance for challenging anatomical structures; method demonstrates effectiveness of integrating world-model dynamics into segmentation.

title: MemHarness: Memory Is Reconstructed, Not Replayed
summary: Retrieving past experiences has become a common strategy to enhance large language model agents. However, most existing memory-augmented agents treat retrieved experiences as static records to be replayed verbatim, injecting them into the context regardless of whether they align with the agent's current situation. This ``replay'' paradigm ignores the gap between the abstract, general nature of stored experience and the concrete, ever-changing states encountered at decision time, frequently causing negative transfer. In contrast, humans rarely recall past experiences verbatim; instead, they reorganize and adapt retrieved memories to fit the present context. Inspired by this, we propose MemHarness, a framework that equips LLM agents to actively harness and reconstruct past experiences based on the present context. At each decision step, a unified policy model critiques and reconstructs the retrieved experience conditioned on the current state, producing context-grounded guidance before acting. This reconstructive ability emerges naturally through end-to-end training with GRPO. Experiments on ALFWorld and WebShop show that MemHarness substantially outperforms pure RL and static memory-augmented baselines, demonstrating strong robustness in out-of-distribution (OOD) scenarios. Furthermore, our analyses reveal that this reconstruction objective not only prevents negative transfer but also serves as latent guidance during training, fundamentally improving the agent's intrinsic reasoning capabilities.

AI.tldr: MemHarness reframes memory retrieval as a constructive, context-grounded reconstruction step rather than verbatim replay, improving decision quality and robustness for LLM agents.
AI.motivation: To address negative transfer from static, verbatim recall of past experiences by enabling agents to adapt memories to the present state, inspired by human memory.
AI.method: At each decision step, a unified policy model critiques and reconstructs retrieved experiences conditioned on the current state, generating context-grounded guidance before acting. End-to-end training with GRPO to induce the reconstructive ability.
AI.result: MemHarness outperforms pure RL and static memory baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop, with robustness in out-of-distribution settings; the reconstruction objective reduces negative transfer and enhances latent guidance and intrinsic reasoning.
AI.conclusion: The reconstructive objective enables context-aware memory use and improves intrinsic reasoning, offering a general, effective approach to memory-augmented LLM agents.

title: Persistent Gaussian Perturbations Prevent Oversmoothing in Recurrent Graph Neural Networks
summary: Oversmoothing is a fundamental limitation of deep graph neural networks (GNNs), where repeated message passing causes node representations to become increasingly similar, eventually collapsing toward a low-dimensional subspace. This phenomenon limits the effective depth of message-passing architectures and motivates the search for mechanisms that preserve representation diversity. In this paper, we study a recurrent graph neural network in which independent Gaussian noise is injected after every propagation step and analyze the resulting architecture as a stochastic dynamical system. Under a standard global contraction assumption on the deterministic update, we prove that the hidden representations form a geometrically ergodic Markov chain admitting a unique invariant probability measure. Our main theoretical result establishes an explicit positive lower bound on the expected stationary Dirichlet energy, proportional to both the noise variance and the spectral gap of the underlying graph. Consequently, the stationary representations cannot collapse onto the constant manifold, providing a rigorous guarantee that asymptotic oversmoothing is prevented in the sense of non-vanishing Dirichlet energy. Our analysis reveals persistent stochastic perturbations as a fundamentally different mechanism for combating oversmoothing, complementing existing deterministic approaches based on residual connections, normalization, and graph rewiring. Finally, numerical experiments on both linear and nonlinear recurrent graph neural networks closely match the theoretical predictions, illustrating the emergence of a stationary distribution and the predicted dependence of the limiting Dirichlet energy on the noise intensity.

AI.tldr: Injecting Gaussian noise after every propagation step in recurrent GNNs yields a geometrically ergodic Markov chain with a unique invariant distribution; a positive lower bound on stationary Dirichlet energy is established, proportional to noise variance and graph spectral gap, ensuring non-vanishing diversity and preventing oversmoothing.
AI.motivation: Provide rigorous theoretical guarantees and a principled mechanism to counteract oversmoothing in deep GNNs by stochastic perturbations, complementing existing deterministic remedies.
AI.method: Model the R-GNN as a stochastic dynamical system with additive Gaussian noise after each propagation; assume global contraction of the deterministic update; prove geometric ergodicity and unique invariant measure; derive a lower bound on expected stationary Dirichlet energy depending on noise variance and spectral gap; validate with linear and nonlinear experiments.
AI.result: Proves existence of a unique invariant measure and a positive lower bound on stationary Dirichlet energy, which scales with noise variance and graph spectral gap; empirical results align with theory, showing stationary distribution and energy dependence on noise.
AI.conclusion: Persistent stochastic perturbations provide a fundamental and complementary mechanism to mitigate oversmoothing in GNNs, alongside residual connections, normalization, and graph rewiring; theory and experiments corroborate the non-vanishing representation diversity in the stationary regime.

title: RefCaptioner: Multi-Reference Image-Grounded Video Captioning
summary: Existing video captioning models generate natural descriptions of video content but cannot explicitly ground local visual elements to multiple reference images. We introduce multi-reference image-grounded video captioning, a new task requiring factual video descriptions with phrase-level reference grounding, and propose RefCaptioner, a two-stage post-training framework for this task. RefCaptioner combines mixed-data SFT with Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO to jointly improve reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency while preserving general video-captioning ability. To support training, we construct a corpus containing $20,000$ videos and 171,354 reference images. We further introduce MRVBench, a benchmark for evaluating caption factuality and multi-reference grounding on both real-world and AI-generated videos. Experiments show that RefCaptioner achieves the best overall performance among the open-source models while remaining competitive on standard video captioning benchmarks. Human evaluation further confirms that its captions are preferred by annotators and enable more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary video generators.

AI.tldr: Proposes RefCaptioner for multi-reference image-grounded video captioning; introduces a two-stage post-training framework with mixed-data SFT and Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO to improve grounding and factuality while preserving captioning ability; builds a large corpus and MRVBench benchmark; shows superior open-source performance and favorable human evaluation for source-faithful reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Address the gap in video captioning where models generate descriptive captions but lack explicit, phrase-level grounding to multiple reference images. The goal is factual, grounded captions that can be traced to multiple references for reliability and cross-reference consistency.
AI.method: RefCaptioner uses a two-stage post-training pipeline combining mixed-data supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and Hierarchical Coverage-Discounted GRPO to optimize reference selection, phrase-level binding, distractor rejection, and cross-reference consistency. It leverages a large corpus (20k videos, 171,354 reference images) and a new training regime.
AI.result: RefCaptioner achieves the best overall performance among open-source models on the new task and remains competitive on standard video captioning benchmarks. Human evaluation shows captions are preferred by annotators and enable more source-faithful video reconstruction with both open-source and proprietary generators.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework advances grounded video captioning by enabling multi-reference grounding and phrase-level binding without sacrificing general captioning ability, validated by quantitative results and human judgments on MRVBench and related benchmarks.

title: Tycho: Active Abstraction with Programmatic World Models for ARC-AGI-3
comment: 52 pages, 18 figures, 17 tables. Open-source implementation: https://github.com/NIMI-research/Tycho
summary:
ARC-AGI-3 turns abstraction into an interactive problem of skill acquisition. A player must infer an unfamiliar game's rules, hidden state, and goal while maintaining action efficiency because every move counts. We formalize these environments as parameterized rendered deterministic Moore machines and introduce Tycho, a coding-agent system that constructs and uses game-specific models during interaction. Tycho separates actionable observations from intermediate animation, level-completion, and game-over frames. From this structured history, an agent can model, test, plan with, repair, or bypass a free-form executable hypothesis.
  In one matched public-set run per policy, we compare four orchestration policies on all 25 public games using Claude Opus 4.8 under matched inference budgets. Actor-requested delegation to a model builder obtains the highest observed mean Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE), 88.49. With this selected policy, GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5 both reach 100.00 RHAE and complete all 183 levels. Their game-balanced first-run human-replay midranks are 98.5 and 100.0. Opus 5 uses 61% fewer scored actions than the aggregate official human baselines.
  Automatic repair after verification failures produces models that reproduce observed transitions much more accurately, yet reaches only 83.07 RHAE. Transition match indicates whether a simulator reproduces observed dynamics, not whether it has identified the objective or improves the next action. Strong play also requires deciding when to construct, repair, use, or bypass a model. We call this joint problem active abstraction: generating a testable model from costly interaction and deciding when acquiring or using it is worth its cost.

AI.tldr: Tycho enables active abstraction in ARC-AGI-3 by learning game rules via interactive model-building over parameterized Moore machines; achieves high RHAE and complete gameplay with efficient action usage, highlighting cost-aware model construction and repair decisions.
AI.motivation: To tackle skill acquisition in abstract, interactive environments by separating actionable observations from non-actionable frames and by formulating model-based planning under restricted interaction budgets; to study when to build, repair, or bypass models (active abstraction).
AI.method: Construct and utilize game-specific models (via Tycho) from interaction histories that separate actionable observations from ancillary frames; compare four orchestration policies with a model-builder delegation under matched inference budgets across 25 public games; evaluate using Relative Human Action Efficiency (RHAE) as primary metric; examine automatic repair and transition matching.
AI.result: Best policy (actor-delegated to a model-builder) yields 88.49 RHAE; with GPT-5.6 Sol and Opus 5, both reach 100.00 RHAE and solve all 183 levels; human-replay midranks around 98.5–100.0; Opus 5 uses 61% fewer scored actions than official human baselines; automatic repair reaches 83.07 RHAE; transition match measures fidelity of reproduced dynamics rather than objective discovery; strong play requires strategic decisions on constructing, repairing, using, or bypassing models.
AI.conclusion: Active abstraction is a core capability for high-performance interactive agents: generating and testing executable hypotheses from costly interaction, and judiciously deciding when model construction and maintenance are worth the cost, yields near-perfect game mastery and substantial action efficiency gains.

title: TopoFormer: Topology Meets Attention for Graph Learning
summary: We introduce Topoformer, a lightweight and scalable framework for graph representation learning that encodes topological structure into attention-friendly sequences. At the core of our method is Topo-Scan, a novel module that decomposes a graph into a short, ordered sequence of topological tokens by slicing over node or edge filtrations. These sequences capture multi-scale structural patterns, from local motifs to global organization, and are processed by a Transformer to produce expressive graph-level embeddings. Unlike traditional persistent homology pipelines, Topo-Scan is parallelizable, avoids costly diagram computations, and integrates seamlessly with standard deep learning architectures. We provide theoretical guarantees on the stability of our topological encodings and demonstrate state-of-the-art performance across graph classification and molecular property prediction benchmarks. Our results show that Topoformer matches or exceeds strong GNN and topology-based baselines while offering predictable and efficient compute. This work opens a new path for parallelizable and unifying approaches to graph representation learning that integrate topological inductive biases into attention frameworks.

AI.tldr: Topoformer converts graphs into short, ordered topological token sequences via Topo-Scan and leverages a Transformer to produce graph embeddings, achieving scalable, stable, state-of-the-art results on graph classification and molecular property tasks.
AI.motivation: Address inefficiencies of persistent homology pipelines and enable topological inductive biases within attention-based architectures, yielding scalable, parallelizable graph representations.
AI.method: Topo-Scan decomposes a graph into a short, ordered sequence of topological tokens by slicing node or edge filtrations; these multi-scale tokens are processed by a Transformer to produce graph-level embeddings; the approach provides stability guarantees and avoids costly diagram computations while integrating with standard DL models.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art or competitive performance on graph classification and molecular property prediction benchmarks; matches or exceeds strong GNN and topology-based baselines with predictable, efficient compute.
AI.conclusion: Topology-informed attention frameworks like Topoformer offer a new, parallelizable paradigm for graph representation learning, combining topological inductive biases with Transformer-based architectures.

title: Beyond Frame Selection: Generative Latent Evidence Aggregation for Long-Video Understanding
summary: Long-video understanding commonly compresses videos into a small set of frames or visual tokens for answer generation. Existing compact pipelines focus on retaining relevant visual content as explicit evidence. Yet making evidence available does not ensure that complementary cues across moments are integrated for answering. Our key idea is to organize selected frames into query-relevant cross-frame evidence before generation.
