It achieves substantial memory reduction (≈71% less peak memory than FP16) and 1.4–1.6× block-level speedups with minimal accuracy loss (0.2–0.7 percentage points in simulation) across multiple platforms and real-robot experiments.
AI.motivation: PTQ methods for WAMs struggle because they optimize open-loop objectives, assume homogeneous model properties, and rely on calibration distributions that do not reflect deployment. A deployment-aware PTQ approach is needed to maintain performance while reducing resource usage.
AI.method: Three strategies: (1) shared-basis outlier calibration—pool activation evidence only across coordinate-compatible modules; (2) co-training-objective saliency—compute empirical-Fisher scores from joint video–action gradients and assign precision weights at a layer granularity that remains calibration-stable; (3) fixed-intervention rollout auditing—revise denoising-step protection schedules using reachable closed-loop states without changing the overall precision budget. Evaluation on Fast-WAM and LingBot-VA, across RoboTwin 2.0, LIBERO, and AgiBot G2 real-robot manipulation; W4A4-dominant setting.
AI.result: Simulation results show FP16 difference within 0.2–0.7 percentage points; real-robot trials demonstrate deployment feasibility on three manipulation tasks. Peak memory reduced to ~29% of FP16; block-level speedups of 1.4–1.6×.
AI.conclusion: QuantWAMs delivers deployment-aware PTQ for World Action Models, yielding substantial memory and speed benefits with minimal accuracy loss, validated across simulators and real-world robotic tasks.

title: On-Policy and Off-Policy Learning for Large Action Spaces
summary: This thesis studies policy learning in interactive systems where an agent observes a context, selects an action from a very large set, and receives partial feedback. The main framework is contextual bandits, with two paradigms: on-policy learning, where the agent interacts sequentially with the environment and minimizes regret, and off-policy learning, where it learns from logged data collected by a logging policy. In large action spaces, both settings face major challenges: inefficient exploration, sparse data coverage, high-variance importance weights, extrapolation bias, and difficult optimization landscapes. The first part develops structured Bayesian methods for on-policy learning. We introduce meTS, a mixed-effect extension of Thompson sampling, and dTS, which leverages diffusion-inspired priors to model dependencies between actions. These methods share information across actions and yield regret guarantees depending on an effective number of actions. The second part addresses off-policy learning. We propose sDM, a structured direct method based on latent variables, show that optimization error can dominate estimation error in large action spaces, and introduce concave, efficiently optimizable policy-weighted log-likelihood objectives. Finally, we develop differentiable pessimistic methods based on exponential smoothing and PAC-Bayesian bounds to control the bias-variance trade-off of regularized importance-sampling estimators.

AI.tldr: A thesis on policy learning in contextual bandits with large action spaces, proposing structured Bayesian on-policy methods (meTS, dTS) and structured off-policy methods (sDM), plus differentiable pessimistic estimators with PAC-Bayesian guarantees.
AI.motivation: Tackle exploration inefficiency, sparse data coverage, high-variance weights, and extrapolation bias in contextual bandits with vast action spaces; provide scalable methods with theoretical guarantees.
AI.method: On-policy: meTS (mixed-effect Thompson sampling) and dTS (diffusion-inspired priors modeling action dependencies). Off-policy: sDM (structured direct method) with latent variables; concave, efficiently optimizable policy-weighted log-likelihood objectives. Additionally, differentiable pessimistic estimators via exponential smoothing and PAC-Bayesian bounds to balance bias-variance in importance sampling.
AI.result: Regret guarantees that depend on an effective number of actions for on-policy methods; off-policy analysis showing optimization error can dominate estimation error in large action spaces; new concave objectives that are efficiently optimizable; a framework for controlling bias-variance via PAC-Bayesian bounds and differentiable pessimism.
AI.conclusion: A cohesive framework for large-action contextual bandits, delivering scalable, theoretically grounded methods for both on-policy and off-policy learning and practical estimators with adjustable bias-variance through structured priors and PAC-Bayesian techniques.

title: Beacon: Knowing When and How to Perform Agentic Visual Reasoning
summary: The fundamental goal of agentic visual reasoning is to improve the success rate of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on complex tasks, rather than merely equipping them with a sophisticated yet inefficient reasoning paradigm. In this work, we rethink agentic visual reasoning through two key dimensions of tool use: Mode Adaptiveness (MA) and Tool Effect (TE). Mode Adaptiveness characterizes whether an MLLM can recognize when tools are truly necessary and invoke them accordingly, thereby avoiding unnecessary computational overhead while improving performance on challenging problems that require tool assistance. Tool Effect characterizes the actual impact of tool use: tools should extend the model's capabilities on problems unsolvable through text-only reasoning, while avoiding additional errors on problems that the model can already solve without tools. We conduct a comprehensive analysis to quantify these two properties and empirically reveal that existing agentic visual reasoning models exhibit limited Mode Adaptiveness, while the gains produced by tool use on hard examples are largely offset by the harm introduced on easy examples that the models can already solve. Motivated by these observations, we propose Beacon, a novel agentic visual reasoning model that achieves stronger overall performance, improved Mode Adaptiveness, and genuine tool-induced performance gains. At the core of Beacon are the Necessity-Aware Adaptive Reward and the Hint-Guided Capability Expansion mechanism in the reinforcement learning stage, which respectively encourage adaptive tool invocation based on task necessity and strengthen the model's tool-use capability on the most challenging problems. Extensive experiments across diverse benchmarks demonstrate the strong overall performance of Beacon and its substantial improvements in both Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect.

AI.tldr: Beacon is a novel agentic visual reasoning model that emphasizes Mode Adaptiveness (MA) and Tool Effect (TE). It addresses the limited adaptive tool-use in existing models by introducing Necessity-Aware Adaptive Reward and Hint-Guided Capability Expansion to promote adaptive, beneficial tool usage. Empirically, Beacon achieves stronger performance, better MA, and genuine tool-induced gains across diverse benchmarks.
AI.motivation: To understand and improve when and how multimodal LLMs should use tools in visual reasoning tasks, by formalizing two properties (MA and TE) and addressing the trade-offs where tool use can help on hard problems but harm on easy ones.
AI.method: Quantify Mode Adaptiveness and Tool Effect; analyze existing agentic visual reasoning models; design Beacon with reinforcement learning components (Necessity-Aware Adaptive Reward and Hint-Guided Capability Expansion) to promote adaptive tool invocation and strengthen tool-use on hard problems; extensive benchmarks.
AI.result: Existing models show limited Mode Adaptiveness and their tool-enabled gains are largely offset by harms on easy problems. Beacon delivers stronger overall performance, improved MA, and genuine tool-induced improvements on challenging cases.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive tool-use is essential for robust multimodal reasoning. The proposed RL-based mechanisms in Beacon encourage necessary tool invocation and enhance capabilities on hard tasks, yielding better MA/TE and overall performance.

title: WIDE: Boosting Adaptive LLM Inference via Token-level Dynamic Width Pruning
summary: Pruning is a promising approach for improving the efficiency of LLMs. Existing static structured pruning methods are hardware-friendly and can deliver practical throughput gains, but their input-agnostic computation allocation often causes substantial accuracy degradation under aggressive sparsity. Recent dynamic sparsity methods improve quality retention by adapting computation to individual inputs, yet they remain largely limited to coarse-grained structural decisions and their practical acceleration under real-world inference scenarios remains challenging. To address these challenges, we present WIDE, the first end-to-end differentiable token-level dynamic width pruning framework designed for both prefill and decode scenarios. WIDE enables fine-grained computation allocation by allowing each token to dynamically select attention-head groups and FFN-channel groups, extending dynamic pruning beyond layer-level decisions to neuron-block-level granularity. Through a two-stage training pipeline, WIDE learns effective token-wise sparse execution patterns and achieves substantially better quality retention than existing approaches. To make such fine-grained dynamic pruning practical, we further propose a pruning--kernel co-design framework that decomposes dynamic sparsity acceleration into mask reordering, hardware-agnostic block-level skipping, and hardware-dependent intra-block skipping, enabling efficient execution across different granularities. At 50% sparsity, WIDE provides 55.1% performance boost when compared to the state-of-the-art dynamic depth pruning under calibration-only settings. Under prefill and decoding inference workloads, WIDE achieves close-to-theoretical kernel-level speedups of up to 1.98x for prefill and 4.95x for decoding, as well as 1.68x and 1.55x end-to-end acceleration. Our code is available at https://github.com/EIT-NLP/LLM-Pruning/tree/main/WIDE.

AI.tldr: WIDE introduces token-level dynamic width pruning for LLMs, enabling per-token allocation of compute to attention-head groups and FFN channels, with a two-stage training and a pruning–kernel co-design, achieving significant speedups and strong quality retention at 50% sparsity.
AI.motivation: Static structured pruning is hardware-friendly but input-agnostic, causing accuracy loss at aggressive sparsity. Dynamic sparsity helps quality but is limited to coarse granularity and practical acceleration is challenging in real-world inference.
AI.method: An end-to-end differentiable token-level dynamic width pruning framework that allows per-token selection of attention-head groups and FFN-channel groups. Two-stage training to learn token-wise sparse patterns, combined with a pruning–kernel co-design that decomposes acceleration into mask reordering, hardware-agnostic block-level skipping, and hardware-dependent intra-block skipping for cross-granularity efficiency.
AI.result: At 50% sparsity, achieves 55.1% performance boost over state-of-the-art dynamic depth pruning under calibration-only settings. Kernel-level speedups of up to 1.98× for prefill and 4.95× for decoding; end-to-end acceleration of 1.68× (prefill) and 1.55× (decoding). Code available at the provided repository.
AI.conclusion: WIDE enables fine-grained, end-to-end differentiable token-level dynamic pruning with practical acceleration for both prefill and decode workloads, offering substantial quality retention and throughput gains over existing approaches.

title: Chimera: Designing and Chinchilla-Scaling Hybrid Visual Diffusion Transformers
summary: Visual generation increasingly requires high-resolution images, long videos, and multimodal context, making the quadratic cost of full attention prohibitive. We introduce Chimera, a hybrid visual diffusion backbone with a principled scaling recipe. Chimera processes text, image, and video tokens in one raster-ordered stream without positional embeddings. It combines Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for long-context state tracking with O(N) complexity, interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) for direct global interaction, and modality-aware short convolutions for local spatiotemporal context. Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) layers expand capacity while controlling activated compute. To scale this heterogeneous architecture, we introduce HeteroP, a module-wise scheme that transfers hyperparameters across width and depth according to each tensor's functional fan-in and model depth. HeteroP yields a consistently tuned family used to fit Chinchilla-style compute-optimal laws for activated model size, training-token count, and image-video data ratio. Guided by these laws, we train an 11B-parameter Chimera with 2B activated parameters. Experiments show three results. First, measured by pretraining diffusion loss, the dense backbone is 1.7x as compute-efficient as a matched full-attention Wan-2.1 2B baseline, while the complete system reaches 7.3x. Second, without length-specific fine-tuning, Chimera extrapolates zero-shot from 5-second training clips to 30-second videos, with only 6.5% FID degradation in the last five seconds. Third, the fitted laws show that compute-optimal image pretraining divides compute nearly evenly between activated model size and training-token count, whereas video pretraining modestly favors model size at higher budgets. These results establish a foundation for designing and scaling efficient long-context diffusion architectures.

AI.tldr: Chimera is a scalable hybrid diffusion backbone for long-context, multi-modal generation that combines Kimi Delta Attention (KDA), interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA), modality-aware short convolutions, and sparse MoE, scaled by a novel HeteroP scheme. Trained at 11B parameters (2B activated), it achieves major compute efficiency gains and strong zero-shot long-context extrapolation, establishing compute-optimal laws for image/video pretraining.
AI.motivation: Mitigate the quadratic cost of full attention in high-resolution images and long videos by developing a hybrid architecture that preserves long-context modeling, global interaction, and local spatiotemporal context with scalable, compute-driven hyperparameter tuning.
AI.method: A raster-ordered, positional-embedding-free backbone that processes text, image, and video tokens using (i) Kimi Delta Attention (KDA) for long-context state tracking with O(N) complexity, (ii) Interleaved Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) for direct global interaction, (iii) modality-aware short convolutions for local spatiotemporal context, and (iv) Sparse MoE layers to expand capacity with controlled activated compute. A module-wise scaling scheme (HeteroP) transfers hyperparameters across width/depth according to functional fan-in and depth, yielding a compute-optimal family (Chinchilla-style laws) for activated parameters, tokens, and data ratios.
AI.result: Empirical findings: (1) the dense backbone achieves 1.7x higher compute-efficiency than a matched Wan-2.1 2B baseline; the full Chimera system achieves 7.3x efficiency. (2) Chimera exhibits zero-shot extrapolation from 5s training clips to 30s videos without length-specific fine-tuning, with only 6.5% FID degradation in the last 5 seconds. (3) The computed scaling laws indicate image pretraining should split compute roughly evenly between activated model size and training-token count, while video pretraining benefits model size at higher budgets.
AI.conclusion: Chimera, guided by explicit compute-optimal laws, provides a scalable blueprint for efficient long-context diffusion architectures across image and video modalities and validates a principled approach to balancing model size, tokens, and data for compute efficiency.

title: When Derived Measurements Mislead: Quantifying and Mitigating LLM Over-Trust with Privileged-Modality Reliability Evidence
comment: 25 pages, including references and supplementary material; 3 figures and 19 tables. Code: https://github.com/Zongheng-Guo/When-Derived-Measurements-Mislead
summary: Derived measurements increasingly enter large language model (LLM) pipelines as direct facts despite their instance-dependent validity. We define derived-feature over-trust (DFOT) as the failure in which a downstream LLM assigns such a measurement the epistemic status of a direct fact or uses it outside its valid scope. Using physiological sensing as a case study, D1 tests acceptance of a PPG-derived rhythm contradicted by offline ECG, whereas D2 tests rejection of an offline-confirmed reliable PPG rhythm under misleading severe history. ECG supplies training supervision and offline reference construction but is never shown to the LLM. Five estimands quantify this chain: conflict over-trust rate (COTR) and context-induced error rate (CIR) characterize D1/D2; correct repair rate (CRR) measures frozen-error repair; evidence-specific repair margin (ESRM) contrasts matched and patient-disjoint shuffled evidence; and utility harm rate (UHR) measures unnecessary verification among HIGH-reliability cases used without verification at baseline. The framework does not depend on a particular reliability generator. We demonstrate it on 50,000 paired PPG-ECG records using ECG-to-PPG privileged distillation as an illustrative baseline and PPG-only inference. On a protocol-locked 187-patient test, the baseline improves four repair and specificity endpoints by 1.82-6.69 percentage points, with all paired confidence intervals excluding zero; UHR increases by 0.67 percentage points (95% CI: -0.4 to +1.7). DFOT provides a common evaluation target for stronger mitigation methods. The code is available at https://github.com/Zongheng-Guo/When-Derived-Measurements-Mislead.

AI.tldr: DFOT (derived-feature over-trust) is the misclassification of derived measurements as direct facts in LLM pipelines. The paper introduces a framework with five estimands to quantify this fault, demonstrates it on large PPG–ECG data with a privileged-distillation baseline versus PPG-only inference, and provides code for replication.
AI.motivation: Derived measurements increasingly feed LLMs, but their validity is often instance-dependent. There is a risk that LLMs adopt these measurements as facts or apply them outside their valid scope. A principled evaluation framework is needed to quantify and mitigate this mis-trust.
AI.method: Define DFOT and two tests (D1: accept a PPG-derived rhythm contradicted by offline ECG; D2: reject an offline-confirmed reliable PPG rhythm under misleading history). ECG provides training supervision and offline references but is not exposed to the LLM. Introduce five estimands (COTR, CIR, CRR, ESRM, UHR) to characterize the error dynamics. Evaluate on 50k paired PPG–ECG records with privileged-distillation as a baseline and PPG-only inference, then verify on a protocol-locked 187-patient test.
AI.result: The baseline improved four repair and specificity endpoints by 1.82–6.69 percentage points with all paired CIs excluding zero; UHR rose by 0.67 percentage points (95% CI: -0.4 to +1.7), i.e., not statistically conclusive. DFOT serves as a unifying evaluation target for mitigation methods.
AI.conclusion: DFOT provides a common, task-agnostic benchmark for studying and mitigating derived-measurement mis-trust in LLM pipelines; code for replication is released at the cited repository.

title: QAdapt: A Noise-Adaptive Neural Pre-Decoding Framework for Quantum Error Correction
summary: Fault-tolerant quantum computing (FTQC) relies on quantum error correction to suppress physical errors and preserve logical information at scale. In practice, however, performance is constrained not only by physical noise but also by the latency of classical decoders processing rapidly generated syndrome data. This challenge is exacerbated by hardware noise that is strong, heterogeneous, and nonstationary, as well as by the simulation-to-hardware distribution shift that can substantially degrade fixed neural decoders. We present QAdapt, a noise-adaptive neural pre-decoding framework for surface-code quantum error correction. QAdapt captures local spatiotemporal correlations in syndrome data, sequentially adapts to evolving noise conditions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and forwards the residual syndrome to a conventional global decoder. Across 110 synthetic out-of-distribution noise configurations for rotated surface-code memory circuits, QAdapt consistently reduces the logical error rate relative to the neural pre-decoding baseline. On Google's Willow benchmark data, without target-domain fine-tuning, it achieves reductions of up to 5.79 percent in logical error rate and 9.32 percent in backend decoding latency on the residual syndrome. These results demonstrate that QAdapt provides a practical and decoder-compatible approach to improving the robustness and backend decoding efficiency of quantum error correction under evolving hardware noise.

AI.tldr: QAdapt is a noise-adaptive neural pre-decoding framework for surface-code quantum error correction that dynamically adapts to evolving, hardware-noise conditions and passes residual syndrome data to a conventional decoder, yielding lower logical error rates and faster backend decoding across diverse synthetic and real-world noise scenarios.
AI.motivation: FTQC performance is limited by not only physical noise but also the latency and robustness of classical decoders. Hardware noise can be strong, heterogeneous, and nonstationary, and distribution shifts between simulation and hardware can degrade fixed neural decoders. A robust, decoder-compatible pre-decoder that adapts online is needed.
AI.method: QAdapt uses a neural pre-decoder that leverages local spatiotemporal correlations in syndrome data, adapts sequentially to changing noise conditions while mitigating catastrophic forgetting, and forwards the residual syndrome to a conventional global decoder.
AI.result: Across 110 synthetic out-of-distribution noise configurations for rotated surface-code memory circuits, QAdapt consistently reduces the logical error rate relative to a neural pre-decoding baseline. On Google's Willow benchmark data, without target-domain fine-tuning, it achieves up to 5.79% reduction in logical error rate and 9.32% reduction in backend decoding latency on the residual syndrome.
AI.conclusion: QAdapt offers a practical, decoder-compatible approach to enhancing robustness and backend decoding efficiency of quantum error correction under evolving hardware noise, demonstrated across diverse synthetic scenarios and real benchmark data.

title: PhiZero: A World Model Built Around Physical Language
summary: We introduce PhiZero, a physical world model built around physical language, a compact discrete representation of world-state transitions. Existing physical world models typically predict future videos directly in pixel space, leaving the underlying world dynamics implicit within high-dimensional visual predictors. Motivated by humans' ability to abstract predictive structure from visual experience and organize it in natural language for explicit reasoning, we learn physical language from in-the-wild videos through self-supervision and use it to explicitly reason about how the physical world evolves. Accordingly, PhiZero adopts a reason-then-render paradigm: it first infers future world evolution as a physical-language sequence and then renders the inferred transitions into videos. Extensive experiments across generation and understanding benchmarks validate the ability of PhiZero to model physically coherent world evolution. We further show its potential for realistic and interactive world modeling, fine-grained action-conditioned simulation, and zero-shot motion transfer.

AI.tldr: PhiZero introduces a discrete physical-language world model that learns from in-the-wild videos via self-supervision. It uses a reason-then-render pipeline: infer a future evolution as a physical-language sequence and render it into video. The model demonstrates coherent dynamics and potential for interactive world modeling, action-conditioned simulation, and zero-shot motion transfer.
AI.motivation: Existing physical world models typically predict pixels directly, leaving dynamics implicit in high-dimensional visual predictors. Humans abstract predictive structure into language for explicit reasoning; a language-grounded representation may improve interpretability, controllability, and reasoning about world evolution.
AI.method: A self-supervised learning approach that extracts a physical-language representation of world-state transitions from unlabeled videos. The model first reasons about future evolution in this physical-language space and then renders the predicted transitions back into video using a separate renderer. The representation is compact and discrete, enabling explicit reasoning and manipulation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on generation and understanding benchmarks show PhiZero can produce physically coherent world evolution. The approach enables realistic and interactive world modeling, fine-grained action-conditioned simulation, and zero-shot motion transfer.
AI.conclusion: PhiZero demonstrates that language-grounded physical world models can capture dynamics explicitly, support reasoning and rendering, and pave the way for programmable, controllable world models that bridge perception and symbolic reasoning.

title: A foundation model of numerical intelligence with cross-disciplinary generalization
summary: Intelligence is commonly understood as the ability to acquire and apply knowledge, adapt to unfamiliar situations and solve new problems. Large language models exhibit this capacity by inferring task-relevant knowledge from textual context and applying it to new tasks. Yet intelligence need not be confined to language. For scientific and social systems, we need models that acquire and apply knowledge from numerical context-an ability we call numerical intelligence. Here we introduce UNified In-Context Operator Networks (UNICON), a foundation model that exhibits numerical intelligence across disciplines. Using graph-based examples from a system as context, UNICON infers the predictive relation shared across them and applies it to queries from the same system. Across scientific and social systems, including those from disciplines absent from training, the same model approaches specialist performance without retraining. Combining UNICON with language-model agents yields further gains, enabling it to surpass state-of-the-art specialists in a discipline unseen in training. We further show that training-corpus diversity improves generalization to unseen disciplines. Together, these results establish UNICON as a foundation model of numerical intelligence and position it as a building block for a broader ecosystem of artificial intelligence.

AI.tldr: UNICON is a numerical-intelligence foundation model that learns cross-disciplinary predictive relations from graph-based context and applies them to queries, achieving strong generalization—including to unseen disciplines—and benefits further from coupling with language-model agents and training-diversity.
AI.motivation: Move beyond language-only notions of intelligence to numerical intelligence; enable models to acquire and apply knowledge from numerical context across scientific and social systems; provide a foundation model that generalizes across disciplines.
AI.method: Use graph-based examples from a system as context to infer a predictive relation shared across them; apply the inferred relation to queries within the same system; evaluate across diverse disciplines, including those absent from training; enhance the approach by combining UNICON with language-model agents; study impact of training-corpus diversity on generalization.
AI.result: UNICON approaches specialist performance on unseen disciplines without retraining; when combined with language-model agents, it surpasses state-of-the-art specialists in an unseen discipline; training-corpus diversity improves generalization to unseen disciplines.
AI.conclusion: UNICON can be a foundation model of numerical intelligence and a building block for a broader AI ecosystem, enabling cross-disciplinary generalization and synergy with language models.

title: Kohn-Sham Spectral Embedding on Sparse Graphs at the Nishimori Temperature for Image Classification
comment: 42 pages, 10 figures, 5 tables, was presented at the 10th International Conference 'Deep Learning on Computational Physics (DLCP2026)', under review for the Moscow University Physics Bulletin, Physics series
summary: We introduce Kohn--Sham Spectral Embedding (KSSE), a physics-inspired energy-based model replacing dense CNN classifiers with a sparse-graph spectral embedding evaluated at the Nishimori temperature of an associated Random-Bond Ising Model. By mapping pre-trained features onto quasi-cyclic low-density parity-check graphs and constructing a regularized Laplacian acting as a Kohn--Sham Hamiltonian, we solve $D$ independent channel spectral problems in $\mathcal{O}(N\log N + k^2_{\text{mode}} N)$ time via FFT on circulant blocks (leveraging Pontryagin self-duality of $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$) and low-order Rayleigh refinement. Graph topology is optimized using \emph{star-domain surgery}: rather than destroying information-carrying codewords by removing frustrated cycles, we construct edge shifts creating local convexity around codewords while bounding residual frustration to $ρ(B_γ)\leq 1+δ$. Multi-scale fractal analysis ($D_2$ spectrum) and fractal learning-rate landscape certifies a landscape transition from rough regimes ($D_2>3$) to star-domain basins ($D_2<1$), enabling Rayleigh refinement with $k_{\text{mode}}=5$ modes. We prove six theoretical results: a generalized Ihara--Bass identity linking belief propagation to the Laplacian; trapping-set eigenvalue correspondence; additive channel separability with an explicit exchange-correlation bound; a surgery theorem bounding frustration with attractor width $Ω(1/\sqrt{d_{\min}})$; a quasi-stationarity perturbation bound; and a fixed-point convergence theorem. In a transductive protocol on ImageNet-1000 with frozen EfficientNet-B4 features ($D=1792$), KSSE achieves \textbf{88.93\%} Top-1 accuracy using $\approx 21.24$M parameters, outperforming Swin-L (197M, 86.4--87.3\%) and matching ViT-H/14 (632M, 88.0--89.5\%) under standard inductive setups, while reducing model footprint by $10\times$ and $30\times$, respectively.

AI.tldr: A physics-inspired KSSE framework for sparse-graph spectral embedding, using Nishimori temperature of a Random-Bond Ising Model, LDPC-like mappings, FFT-based spectral solves, and star-domain surgery. It provides six theoretical results and state-of-the-art efficiency, achieving 88.93% Top-1 on ImageNet-1000 with 21.24M parameters, outperforming Swin-L and matching ViT-H/14 while being ~10–30× smaller.
AI.motivation: To develop an efficient, scalable, physics-grounded spectral-embedding approach for vision tasks that leverages sparse graph representations and energy-based formulations to reduce model size without sacrificing accuracy, enabling competitive performance on large-scale benchmarks.
AI.method: Introduce Kohn–Sham Spectral Embedding (KSSE). Map pre-trained features to quasi-cyclic LDPC-like graphs and construct a regularized Laplacian acting as a Kohn–Sham Hamiltonian. Solve D independent spectral problems in O(N log N + k_mode^2 N) using FFT on circulant blocks, with Rayleigh refinement. Optimize graph topology via star-domain surgery to control frustration, ensuring residual frustration ρ(B_γ) ≤ 1+δ. Employ multi-scale fractal analysis (D2 spectrum) to certify a landscape transition from rough (D2>3) to basin-like (D2<1). Provide six theoretical results: generalized Ihara–Bass identity for belief propagation, trapping-set eigenvalue correspondence, additive channel separability with exchange-correlation bound, surgery theorem bounding frustration with attractor width Ω(1/√d_min), quasi-stationarity perturbation bound, and fixed-point convergence. Evaluate in transductive ImageNet-1000 with frozen EfficientNet-B4 features (D=1792), achieving 88.93% Top-1 with ~21.24M parameters, surpassing Swin-L (86.4–87.3%) and approaching ViT-H/14 (88.0–89.5%).
AI.result: Empirical performance on ImageNet-1000 with fixed features shows competitive accuracy at a fraction of parameter count compared to large transformers, supported by several theoretical guarantees and a novel graph-theoretic spectral approach.
AI.conclusion: KSSE provides a principled, physics-inspired pathway for efficient, high-accuracy spectral embedding in vision, with strong theoretical backing and practical performance gains over larger transformers in a transductive setting.

title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
summary: Embodied intelligence faces a fundamental data bottleneck. Models must capture how first-person perception, whole-body motion, dexterous manipulation, object state, sound, and touch evolve together as humans pursue goals over time. Existing datasets fragment this experience across viewpoints, modalities, or spatial scales, leaving the full perception-action loop only partially observed. We introduce the Ambient Capture Engine (ACE), a human-centric data engine that transforms real home environments into spatially calibrated, temporally synchronized recording studios. ACE operates at two complementary scales: a table-scale configuration resolves hand-object manipulation, while a room-scale configuration captures whole-body motion, locomotion, and interactions across a furnished home. ACE records egocentric and multi-view exocentric video, full-body and articulated hand motion, object geometry and 6-DoF trajectories, audio, and tactile signals as a unified multisensory stream. Using ACE, we build ACE-Data-0, comprising 150 hours and 17M video frames across 200 task categories, performed by 50 participants in 2 environments, for a total of 75,000 interaction episodes. The dataset spans atomic manipulation, long-horizon chains of household activities, and human-scene interaction, while preserving natural behavioral variation through goal-level rather than step-by-step instructions. We further introduce a hierarchical benchmark that progresses from signals to scene components and then to interactions. Evaluations of state-of-the-art methods expose substantial gaps under contact, occlusion, egomotion, and long temporal horizons. ACE-Data-0 provides synchronized human demonstrations with aligned perceptual, kinematic, and contact supervision, offering a scalable foundation for imitation learning, world models, vision-language-action systems, and embodied AI.

AI.tldr: Ambient Capture Engine (ACE) is a human-centric data engine that converts real homes into synchronized, multimodal recording studios at table- and room-scales, yielding ACE-Data-0 (150 hours, 17M frames, 50 participants, 200 tasks, 75k episodes) and a hierarchical benchmark to evaluate embodied AI under contact, occlusion, egomotion, and long-horizon challenges.
AI.motivation: To address the fundamental data bottleneck in embodied intelligence by capturing the full perception-action loop across modalities, scales, and naturalistic goals in real homes.
AI.method: Develop ACE hardware/software to create two scales (table-scale for manipulation, room-scale for full-body motion) and record synchronized egocentric/exocentric video, full-body/hand motion, 6-DoF object trajectories, audio, and tactile signals; assemble ACE-Data-0 and propose a hierarchical benchmark.
AI.result: ACE-Data-0: 150 hours, 17M frames, 50 participants, 2 environments, 200 tasks, 75k episodes; synchronized multisensory supervision enabling imitation learning, world models, and vision-language-action systems; baseline evaluations reveal gaps in state-of-the-art methods under contact, occlusion, egomotion, and long horizons.
AI.conclusion: ACE-Data-0 provides a scalable, richly supervised foundation for advancing embodied AI research across perception, control, and language-enabled tasks, and exposes current method limitations on long-horizon, contact-rich scenarios.

title: Metaphor Tracer: A Theory-Informed Analysis of Hidden States
summary:
What do a language model's hidden states say about the organization of a single text? From one forward pass, without training, we score every token position on two properties. The *aggregator* measures whether the position consolidates the whole text into a stable configuration. The *differentiator*, whether other tokens are transiently carried into its subspace as the model reads: metaphor in its root sense, transport. Constants were frozen on one discovery text; every other is confirmatory.
  The aggregator is not, in the classic sense, an information measure, nor a measure of salience. Across three unrelated models, as a signifier repeats, its surprisal and its attention drain while its aggregator score holds: the channel marks a token's place in the text. That this tracks a reading rests on independent ground truth: an engineered register the aggregator follows across its boundaries (6/6 cells), and a psychoanalyst's marking of clinical transcripts, fixed before the instrument existed, in 34/36 cells, with a graded increment above lexical controls and dissociations no type-level measure reproduces. A transfer test gives the result its shape: the model whose token structure travels with lexical type reads the singular discourse worst, and in a matched base/instruct pair tuning raises fidelity without moving type-transfer. Structural value is a property of a token's place in *this* text, not of its vector alone: a relational rather than essentialist reading of hidden states, operationalizing theory that predated the instrument.

AI.tldr: Zero-shot analysis of a language model's hidden states reveals two token-position properties, aggregator and differentiator, that encode a text's organizational structure in a text-specific, relational manner rather than as intrinsic vector features; validated against engineered ground truth and psychoanalytic transcripts, with cross-model transfer tests showing partial generalization.
AI.motivation: Understand how a language model encodes text organization in hidden states from a single forward pass without training, by defining relational properties that indicate where a token sits in the discourse.
AI.method: For each token position in a text, compute two properties in one forward pass: aggregator (stability of the whole text in a fixed subspace) and differentiator (whether other tokens transiently occupy its subspace). Constants are frozen on one discovery text; others serve as confirmatory. Evaluate across three models. Validate against independent ground truth: engineered register (6/6 cells) and psychoanalyst markings on clinical transcripts (34/36). Conduct transfer tests comparing lexical-type–driven and token-structure–driven readings; compare base vs instruct tuning.
AI.result: Aggregator tracks text structure across models; repeated signifiers show lower surprisal and attention drain while aggregator remains stable, implying a token's place in the text is encoded in its hidden-state relation. Ground-truth alignment is strong (6/6, 34/36) and dissociates from type-level measures. Transfer tests show token-structure behavior interacts with lexical-type readings; tuning improves fidelity without altering type-transfer. Structural value emerges as a property of the token’s position in this text, not the vector alone.
AI.conclusion: Token-level structure is relational and text-specific, supporting an interpretable, non-vector-based marker of discourse organization grounded in a theory predating the instrument. The approach generalizes across models to some extent and offers a novel, text-centric lens on hidden states, though broader validation across genres and longer texts is needed.

title: Oracle-Budgeted Molecular Optimization with Short-Term Graph Memory
summary: Molecular optimization is commonly performed under a limited oracle budget, which makes deciding what to evaluate as important as deciding what to generate. We introduce short-term graph memory, a plug-in module that preserves the generator architecture and native update rule while learning from previously evaluated molecules to prioritize subsequent oracle queries. The module maintains an online graph neural surrogate that pre-screens each round's candidate pool, so the fixed oracle budget is spent on molecules with higher predicted utility. Applied to a fragment-based generator on a standard molecular optimization benchmark, it improves the mean top-10 score at no extra oracle cost and never falls behind the base on any oracle; the gain extends to all four generators we tested at a tight budget of one thousand calls. We then analyze how surrogate-guided selection interacts with the exploration and exploitation behavior of different generators. Its benefit at larger budgets is consistent with two properties of the backbone: how broadly it searches, and how effectively its native search already exploits oracle feedback. We provide a simple way to spend a fixed oracle budget more selectively, and evidence on which generators benefit from it.

AI.tldr: Introduces short-term graph memory (STGM), a plug-in that learns from evaluated molecules using an online GNN surrogate to pre-screen candidate pools, guiding oracle queries under tight budgets. It preserves the generator’s architecture, improves mean top-10 scores without extra oracle cost, and benefits multiple generators, with analysis of exploration/exploitation interactions and a simple budget-spending strategy.
AI.motivation: Oracle-limited molecular optimization requires efficient allocation of evaluations. Existing generators may underutilize fixed budgets, leading to suboptimal exploration-exploitation trade-offs. A surrogate-guided pre-screening mechanism can prioritize high-utility candidates without altering the generator.
AI.method: Integrate an online graph neural surrogate as a plug-in that learns from past evaluations and pre-screens each round’s candidate pool, leaving the fixed oracle budget to high-utility molecules. Preserve the generator’s architecture and update rule. Evaluate on a fragment-based generator on a standard molecular optimization benchmark, with budgeted oracle calls (e.g., 1,000). Compare across four generators and analyze interaction with exploration/exploitation.
AI.result: STGM improves the mean top-10 score under the fixed budget without incurring extra oracle costs and never degrades the base method. The gain extends to all four generators at a tight budget (1,000 calls). Surrogate-guided selection’s benefits at larger budgets depend on the backbone’s exploration breadth and exploitation efficiency. The paper also provides a practical way to spend a fixed oracle budget more selectively and shows which generators benefit most.
AI.conclusion: A simple, effective budget-aware enhancement for molecular generation: surrogate-guided pre-screening can selectively allocate oracle queries to high-utility molecules, enhancing performance under budget constraints. The benefit is influenced by the generator’s search behavior, suggesting tailored deployment depending on backbone characteristics.

title: ReToken: One Token to Improve Vision-Language Models for Visual Retrieval
summary: Long visual context poses a challenge for vision-language models: performance degrades as the number of distractors grows, and processing all tokens at once is computationally infeasible under GPU memory constraints. We present ReToken, a single learnable embedding trained as an explicit retrieval target that selects a sparse set of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache. Trained on only a small image-QA dataset, ReToken yields consistent gains across image and video benchmarks: on Visual Haystacks it improves Qwen3VL-8B by 13.4 points and InternVL3.5 by 12.4 points (>20% relative), and on LVBench it transfers zero-shot to long video for an 8.0-point gain with Qwen3VL-8B. Thanks to its lightweight design, both training and long-video inference fit on a single H100. Code is available at: https://github.com/avaxiao/ReToken

AI.tldr: ReToken introduces a learnable retrieval target to sparsify token selection from a large visual KV cache, enabling efficient long-context vision-language reasoning with negligible training data.
AI.motivation: Long visual contexts degrade performance and are computationally expensive; need sparse, trainable retrieval to select relevant tokens from a large cache.
AI.method: Train a single learnable embedding as explicit retrieval target; selects a sparse subset of query-relevant visual tokens from a pre-filled visual KV cache. Trained on a small image-QA dataset; integrates with vision-language models to improve performance on long-context image and video tasks.
AI.result: On Visual Haystacks: Qwen3VL-8B +13.4 points; InternVL3.5 +12.4 points (>20% relative). On LVBench: zero-shot to long video with 8.0-point gain for Qwen3VL-8B. Lightweight design allows training and long-video inference on a single H100.
AI.conclusion: ReToken provides consistent gains across image and video benchmarks with an efficient, trainable retrieval mechanism that sparsifies visual token usage; it enables scalable long-context VLMs with modest training data and hardware requirements.

title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
summary: Scaling test-time computation can improve language-model reasoning, but uniform budgets waste computation on easy inputs, while verifier-guided refinement relies on external feedback. We introduce Self-Verifying Refinement (SVR), an oracle-free multi-turn reinforcement learning framework that learns to use self-verification as a compute-control policy. At each turn, the model produces a solution together with a discrete correctness verdict and a confidence score; it retains the current answer only when the verdict is Correct and confidence exceeds a threshold, and otherwise continues refinement using its own self-verification. Ground-truth correctness is used only to construct training rewards and is never exposed to the policy through refinement prompts or required at inference. SVR is trained with GRPO on fixed-horizon trajectories using rewards that promote solution correctness, calibration-aware self-verification, and stop-ready correct states; adaptive stopping is activated only at inference. On seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B, SVR achieves a macro-average accuracy of 0.563 with only 2.99 inference turns on average. In the evaluated complete-system comparison, it exceeds standard GRPO, strong multi-turn baselines, and a fixed-budget oracle-guided score-feedback reference while requiring substantially fewer turns than fixed ten-turn inference. These results demonstrate that learned self-verification can serve as an effective internal control signal for answer retention and adaptive test-time compute allocation.

AI.tldr: SVR introduces an oracle-free, multi-turn RL framework that uses self-verification as an internal compute-control signal to decide whether to retain an answer or refine further. It trains with GRPO on fixed horizons using rewards tied to correctness and calibration, enabling adaptive stopping at inference. It achieves state-of-the-art-like results on seven math benchmarks with fewer turns than fixed ten-turn baselines.
AI.motivation: To improve reasoning precision while avoiding wasted computation on easy inputs and avoiding reliance on external verifier feedback; aim to learn a self-verification-based control policy for test-time compute allocation.
AI.method: Multi-turn reinforcement learning (GRPO) where each turn outputs a solution, a discrete verdict, and a confidence score. The answer is kept only if verdict=Correct and confidence>threshold; otherwise refinement continues using self-verification. Training uses ground-truth correctness to shape rewards but not exposed during inference. Adaptive stopping is enabled at inference only. Evaluation on seven math benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B.
AI.result: SVR achieves macro-average accuracy 0.563 with 2.99 turns on average. It surpasses standard GRPO, strong multi-turn baselines, and a fixed-budget oracle-guided reference, while using far fewer turns than a fixed ten-turn setting.
AI.conclusion: Learned self-verification can serve as an effective internal control signal for answer retention and adaptive test-time compute allocation, enabling efficient and reliable multi-turn reasoning.

title: Cybersecurity Detection Classification with Reasoning-enabled Language Models
summary: A major issue in Security Operations Centers (SOCs) is alert fatigue, as the number of detections reported is more than staff can triage in a given day. Prior work prompts or fine-tunes large language models (LLMs) to emit a triage label directly, but does not train them to reason about whether a detection is a genuine threat. We train a chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning-enabled triage classifier on real, human-labeled Windows endpoint detections by combining automated prompt optimization, self-training, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. We find that CoT reasoning also degrades the label-token probabilities that automated triage relies on, so we separately train a calibrator that reads the full reasoning trace and estimates the probability that the verdict is correct. Our system reaches 82.6% test accuracy and, at the high-confidence operating point that governs automated triage, improves benign recall by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% over a direct-label LLM classifier. We further show that the trained calibrator is necessary - an untrained confidence judge collapses high-confidence recall to zero - and that a finetuned 30B model significantly outperforms frontier general-purpose models, motivating targeted training over scale.

AI.tldr: A CoT-based triage classifier with a calibrated confidence estimator improves automated threat triage in SOCs, achieving 82.6% test accuracy and notable recall gains over direct-label LLMs; targeted training outperforms scaling.
AI.motivation: Address alert fatigue in Security Operations Centers by enabling reasoning about whether detections are genuine threats, not just producing labels.
AI.method: Train a chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning-enabled triage classifier on real Windows endpoint detections using automated prompt optimization, self-training, and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Observe that CoT degrades label-token probabilities, so train a separate calibrator that reads the full reasoning trace to estimate the probability that the verdict is correct.
AI.result: The system achieves 82.6% test accuracy. At a high-confidence operating point for automated triage, benign recall improves by 43.0% and malicious recall by 18.3% over a direct-label LLM classifier. The calibrator is necessary (an untrained confidence judge collapses high-confidence recall to zero). A finetuned 30B model significantly outperforms frontier general-purpose models, underscoring the value of targeted training over scaling.
AI.conclusion: CoT reasoning with a calibrated verdict estimator and targeted model training yields robust automated triage improvements in SOCs, with gains in both benign and malicious recall and evidence that precision calibration is essential for reliable high-confidence automation.

title: LeanCSP: A Framework for Certifying Constraint Reformulation and Solving in Lean
summary: Constraint programming is a core technology for solving complex combinatorial problems in scheduling, planning, configuration, and verification. Trusting its results therefore demands guarantees at two levels: that reformulations applied beforehand are semantics-preserving, and that solvers produce correct answers. In this work, we introduce a framework that addresses both verification levels in the Lean theorem prover: it can be used to prove formulation-level properties, such as equivalence, equisatisfiability, and the correctness of symmetry-breaking constraints, parametrically for entire problem families; and to check solver-produced certificates for individual instances via translation backends to external formats such as MiniZinc, SMT-LIB, and OPB. Combining both levels yields an end-to-end workflow that establishes the satisfiability or unsatisfiability of a constraint problem without trusting the external solver. Experimental results show that our framework's verified symmetry breaking also pays off in practice: a single parametric proof per problem family, reused across all instance sizes, reduces solver search effort by a factor of up to 2x10^7, while the entire in-Lean certification stays affordable, taking at most a few minutes for our largest instances.

AI.tldr: A Lean-based framework for end-to-end, verified constraint solving that proves formulation-level properties and checks solver certificates, enabling massive, reusable symmetry-breaking gains.
AI.motivation: Trust in constraint programming requires both semantics-preserving reformulations and correct solver results; existing tools lack integrated verification across reformulations and solver certificates.
AI.method: A Lean theorem-prover framework with parametric proofs over problem families for properties like equivalence, equisatisfiability, and correctness of symmetry-breaking constraints; translation backends to external formats (MiniZinc, SMT-LIB, OPB) for certificate checking; an end-to-end workflow combining both levels.
AI.result: A single parametric proof per problem family can be reused across all instance sizes, reducing solver search effort up to 2×10^7; the Lean-based certification remains affordable, taking only minutes for the largest instances.
AI.conclusion: Demonstrates practical viability of fully verified CP workflows; verified symmetry breaking yields substantial performance gains and builds trust by avoiding reliance on external solvers.

title: Stage-Replay Divergence Follows the KV Cache: Fixed-Prefix Precision Controls and Bidirectional Cache Transplantation
comment: 15 pages, 1 figure, 6 tables. Reproducibility artifacts (frozen manifests, token IDs, per-item scores, analysis harnesses) described in Section 3.9
summary: Stage-replay diagnostics reconstruct intermediate token prefixes and treat fresh-prefill continuation as continuation from the decoder state that originally reached the prefix. We audit that assumption at a whole reasoning-stage boundary in a Qwen2.5-derived system. A matched 200-item experiment compares retained live cache with one-shot prefill of identical integer tokens and places an exact replica on both sides. In BF16, replicas remain exact while the constructions differ on 166 suffixes and 20 correctness labels; the accuracy difference is only one point (paired 95% CI [-3.5, +5.5]). A fixed-prefix 2x2 holds all 200 token states constant while crossing construction and precision. The BF16 disagreements recur, whereas FP32 produces no decoded disagreement (95% Wilson upper bound 1.88%). A prospective bridge makes token-by-token incremental and retained live caches bit-exact on 12/12 rows; an all-200 saved-ledger audit reproduces every retained trajectory and comparison fingerprint. Bidirectional transplantation of all 48 key/value layers makes every tested divergent continuation follow its cache donor, both on a selected set at the primary checkpoint (24/24) and an outcome-blind replication at a later checkpoint (43/43). Exact-token replay can therefore be repeatable without preserving live-state fidelity. On the tested states, boundary K/V cache is a causally sufficient carrier of the divergent trajectory, while numerical precision moderates its behavioral expression.

AI.tldr: Stage-replay diagnostics show that boundary key/value caches can carry divergent token continuations and permit exact-token replay even when live state fidelity is not preserved; precision affects, but does not fully determine, divergence, with FP32 showing tighter alignment than BF16.
AI.motivation: To validate the assumption that a fresh-prefill continuation can be treated as a continuation from the decoder state at the prefix, evaluated at a reasoning-stage boundary in a Qwen2.5-derived system and across precision/construct variations.
AI.method: 200-item experiment comparing retained live cache against one-shot prefill of identical integer tokens; BF16 and FP32 precisions; analyses include fixed-prefix 2x2 tests, prospective token-by-token bridge, saved-ledger audit, and bidirectional transplantation of 48 K/V layers. Metrics include exact-token replication, sentence-level and token-level divergences, and Wilson score bounds.
AI.result: In BF16, replicas remain exact for some features but 166 suffixes and 20 correctness labels diverge; accuracy difference ~1 point (95% CI [-3.5, +5.5]). FP32 yields no decoded disagreement (Wilson upper bound 1.88%). A token-by-token bridge achieves bit-exact caches on 12/12 rows; full 200-token ledger reproduces trajectories and fingerprints. Bidirectional transplantation of all 48 K/V layers causes every divergent continuation to follow its cache donor (24/24 at primary checkpoint; 43/43 at later checkpoint). Exact-token replay is repeatable without preserving live-state fidelity.
AI.conclusion: Boundary K/V caches are a causally sufficient carrier of divergent trajectories; numerical precision modulates behavior but does not undermine replayability. Exact-token replay is achievable under tested conditions, enabling auditability of stage-replay continuations without requiring full live-state fidelity.

title: A report-grounded vision-language foundation model for colonoscopy from 280000 routine reports
summary: Vision-language models remain underused in colonoscopy despite the rich expert descriptions recorded in routine reports. These reports document lesion appearance, size and location but summarise entire procedures rather than caption individual frames, leaving clinical findings only weakly linked to the corresponding images. Here we develop EndoCLIP, a colonoscopy vision-language foundation model trained on 125,756 lesion-level image-text pairs progressively recovered from 280,476 routine colonoscopy records. Across lesion-level image-text retrieval, structured report generation and six multi-centre clinical classification tasks, EndoCLIP outperforms general-purpose and biomedical vision-language encoders in both zero-shot and linear-probe settings. On benign-versus-malignant classification, its linear probe approaches the performance of expert readers in a blinded study involving 12 endoscopists. These results suggest that recovering finding-to-frame correspondence can transform routine documentation into scalable supervision, enabling clinical targets to be specified in language rather than separately annotated for each task.

AI.tldr: EndoCLIP, a colonoscopy vision-language model trained on large-scale lesion-level image-text pairs, delivers strong lesion-level retrieval, structured report generation, and multicenter clinical classification, with its linear probe approaching expert performance on benign-vs-malignant classification, highlighting the value of finding-to-frame correspondence to enable language-based supervision.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models are underutilized in colonoscopy; routine reports document lesions but do not align text with specific frames, limiting image-captioning utility. Recovering frame-level finding-to-text alignment could unlock scalable, language-based supervision for clinical tasks.
AI.method: Train EndoCLIP on 125,756 lesion-level image-text pairs derived progressively from 280,476 routine colonoscopy records. Evaluate on lesion-level image-text retrieval, structured report generation, and six multi-centre clinical classification tasks in zero-shot and linear-probe settings; validate with a blinded study of 12 endoscopists for benign-vs-malignant classification.
AI.result: EndoCLIP outperforms general-purpose and biomedical vision-language encoders across the tasks in both zero-shot and linear-probe settings. In benign-versus-malignant classification, its linear probe performance approaches that of expert readers in the blinded study (12 endoscopists). The model demonstrates meaningful recovery of finding-to-frame correspondence, enabling language-based specification of clinical targets.
AI.conclusion: Recovering finding-to-frame correspondence converts routine documentation into scalable supervision and supports clinical targets defined in language rather than requiring task-specific annotations.

title: The Role of Causality in Algorithmic Recourse
summary:
Algorithmic recourse aims to provide individuals with actionable changes to improve their predicted outcomes in high-stakes classification settings, such as loan and mortgage applications. However, most existing approaches focus only on flipping a model's prediction, without accounting for whether the recommended changes lead to genuine improvement in an individual's true qualifications or merely enable strategic gaming of the classifier. Consequently, deployed recourse policies can induce behavioral responses that degrade predictive accuracy and become ineffective after model retraining.
  In this work, we formalize this failure mode through a causal performative framework for recourse. We model how recourse actions propagate through a structural causal model, capturing interactions among features as well as their effect on the true label. These causal responses induce a non-convex optimization problem, even under standard convex losses. We characterize conditions under which performatively stable solutions exist and can be efficiently computed via simple iterative dynamics. Our analysis reveals that recourse policies that ignore causal structure can induce large, misaligned behavioral responses, whereas causal recourse leads to stable equilibria that reduce incentives for gaming. Experiments on both semi-synthetic and real credit datasets demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms standard empirical risk minimization while reducing the need for repeated model retraining to accommodate distribution shifts caused by strategic agent behavior.

AI.tldr: A causal performative framework for recourse is proposed to account for how recourse actions affect true qualifications, yielding stable equilibria, reducing gaming, and less retraining; it outperforms standard ERM on semi-synthetic and real credit data.
AI.motivation: Address misalignment between recourse that flips predictions and genuine improvement in true qualifications, and the resulting gaming and distribution shifts after model updates.
AI.method: Formalize recourse within a structural causal model to capture feature interactions and their impact on the true label; derive a non-convex optimization under standard losses; identify conditions for performatively stable solutions and compute them via simple iterative dynamics; validate with semi-synthetic and real credit datasets.
AI.result: Findings show performatively stable recourse reduces gaming incentives, improves robustness to model retraining, and improves predictive performance compared to standard empirical risk minimization.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating causal structure into recourse yields stable equilibria, mitigates strategic manipulation, and offers a practical, efficient approach for high-stakes decision systems that endure model updates.

title: Towards Autonomous Aircraft Surveillance from Nanosatellites through On-Board Inference and Generative Data Augmentation
summary: Airborne surveillance from low Earth orbit is hindered by two interconnected bottlenecks: nanosatellites have a limited downlink budget, yet the conventional approach still transmits terabytes of raw imagery to the ground for processing, and open satellite datasets for aircraft are scarce and severely class-imbalanced. These limitations either delay timely decision-making or prevent standard detectors from learning robust representations of rare aircraft classes. In this paper, a workflow that combines on-board inference with generative data augmentation is proposed to address both limitations jointly. Inference is executed on a 6U CubeSat equipped with a low-power edge tensor accelerator, while a diffusion model fine-tuned through low-rank adaptation generates synthetic minority-class imagery. This synthetic output is automatically annotated, pseudo-labelled, by an intermediate detector and merged with classically augmented samples. The results show that the balanced dataset increases global mean average precision from 77.9% to 82.2%, with the minority class rising from F1=0.683 to F1=0.811, and that the quantised detector fits the on-chip memory and projects 25-30 frames per second on orbit. This approach contrasts with the conventional bent-pipe architecture, in which the satellite acts as a passive data collector. Therefore, the computational tests support the proposed workflow as a decision-support tool for real-time, autonomous airborne surveillance from nanosatellites.

AI.tldr: On-board inference on a 6U CubeSat with diffusion-generated synthetic data to balance an imbalanced aircraft dataset, improving detection performance while fitting on-chip memory and enabling real-time autonomous surveillance.
AI.motivation: Address two bottlenecks in airborne nanosatellite surveillance: limited downlink bandwidth for raw imagery and scarcity/class-imbalance of open aircraft datasets, which hinder timely decision-making and robust detectors.
AI.method: On-board inference using a low-power edge tensor accelerator on a 6U CubeSat; diffusion model fine-tuned with low-rank adaptation to generate synthetic minority-class aircraft imagery; automatic pseudo-labeling via an intermediate detector; merge synthetic outputs with classically augmented samples; use a quantized detector that fits on-chip memory; evaluate performance (global mAP, minority F1) and on-orbit frame rate (25–30 fps).
AI.result: Global mean average precision improves from 77.9% to 82.2%; minority F1 improves from 0.683 to 0.811; a quantized detector fits on-chip memory and processes 25–30 frames per second on orbit.
AI.conclusion: The workflow demonstrates a feasible, real-time, autonomous airborne surveillance pipeline for nanosatellites, offering a practical alternative to the conventional bent-pipe architecture by performing inference and data augmentation on-board.

title: Same Graph Cross-Task Transfer in GNNs: Protocols and Predictors
summary: Many real-world graphs support multiple predictive tasks over the same underlying structure, creating an opportunity to reuse supervision across node classification (NC) and link prediction (LP). However, existing evaluations often rely on incompatible splits, observed-graph assumptions, and negative sampling rules, making conclusions about same-graph cross-task transfer unreliable. We formalize same-graph NC-LP transfer and propose a leakage-free protocol that fixes node and edge splits, uses a shared message-passing graph that excludes evaluated edges, and employs fixed negatives for LP. Across three backbones (GCN, GraphSAGE, GPS), we find that transfer is strongly directional and predictable: NC $\to$ LP is consistently beneficial on homophilic graphs, while LP $\to$ NC is fragile and can even degrade accuracy under naive representation reuse. LP $\to$ NC becomes reliably positive mainly in a structure-dominant regime where LP is easy but NC is unsaturated, suggesting that LP acts as structural pretraining. Finally, we introduce the CoTask Score (CTS) to summarize joint NC+LP utility when a shared encoder must serve both tasks, and show that simple dataset statistics, especially homophily, can guide mechanism choice and help avoid negative transfer.

AI.tldr: Leakage-free, same-graph NC-LP transfer is strongly directional and dataset-dependent; NC→LP benefits on homophilic graphs, LP→NC is fragile unless the structure dominates; a structural pretraining view explains LP's role; CTS summarizes joint NC+LP utility for shared encoders.
AI.motivation: To address unreliable conclusions from incompatible data splits and leakage in cross-task transfer between node classification (NC) and link prediction (LP) on the same graph, and to formalize a leakage-free evaluation protocol.
AI.method: Introduce a leakage-free protocol with fixed node/edge splits, a shared message-passing graph excluding evaluated edges, and fixed negatives for LP; evaluate across three backbones (GCN, GraphSAGE, GPS); develop CoTask Score (CTS) to summarize joint NC+LP utility; analyze transfer directionality and regimes using dataset statistics (notably homophily).
AI.result: Across NC/LP transfer, directionality is strong: NC→LP yields consistent gains on homophilic graphs, while LP→NC is fragile and can degrade with naive representation reuse; LP→NC becomes reliably positive in a structure-dominant regime where LP is easy but NC is unsaturated, suggesting LP acts as structural pretraining; CTS correlates with joint utility and dataset homophily informs mechanism choice.
AI.conclusion: Same-graph NC–LP transfer is predictable and governed by data structure; homogeneous graphs favor cross-task transfer from NC to LP, while LP can pretrain structures for NC under structure-dominant regimes. CTS provides a compact measure of joint encoder utility and helps select mechanisms using simple dataset statistics like homophily.

title: A Fuzzy Rule-based Neuro-Symbolic Approach for Pipe Severity Prediction in Sewer Networks
summary:
Standard automated sewer pipe severity assessment relies on direct image classification, creating a "black box" where the link between visual defects and final severity scores remains implicit. This study introduces a modular, fuzzy rule-based neuro-symbolic framework that bridges this gap by decoupling neural perception from symbolic reasoning. The perception module utilizes a Swin Transformer to predict 14 multilabel inspection CODE degrees directly from images. For reasoning, a DT, specifically Weka's J48, algorithm is trained on ground-truth CODEs and severity labels, and its paths are converted into 19 fixed IF--THEN rules. Inference operates via fuzzy logic: t-norm activations from CODE conditions are weighted by rule confidence and combined with corresponding s-norms to produce interpretable class evidence. We assessed Product, Łukasiewicz, and Hamacher operator pairs using a dataset of 3,244 images spanning five highly imbalanced severity classes. Ground-truth labels were robustly generated via consensus from five independent large language models analyzing original inspector notes. Our results show an improvement of accuracy, balanced accuracy, Macro F1 and MCC by 17.9%, 12.2%, 23.0%, and 17.3%, respectively, over image-only based classification.
  Overall, the framework combines competitive class-balanced performance with traceable reasoning from predicted CODE degrees to rule supports and severity evidence.

AI.tldr: A modular neuro-symbolic framework uses a Swin Transformer to predict 14 inspection codes from images and a decision tree-derived set of 19 IF-THEN rules fed via fuzzy logic to infer sewer pipe severity, improving several metrics over image-only classification on a 3,244-image, five-class dataset with LLM-consensus ground-truth.
AI.motivation: Address the opacity of end-to-end image-to-severity models by decoupling perception from symbolic reasoning to achieve interpretable, traceable evidence linking visual defects to severity scores.
AI.method: Perception: Swin Transformer outputs 14 multilabel CODE degrees from images. Reasoning: A J48 decision tree is trained on CODEs and severity labels; its paths are converted into 19 fixed IF-THEN rules. Inference uses fuzzy logic with t-norms (for CODE conditions) weighted by rule confidence and combined with s-norms to produce class evidence. Evaluated with Product, Łukasiewicz, and Hamacher t-norm/s-norm pairs on 3,244 images across five imbalanced classes. Ground-truths derived by consensus from five independent LLM analyses of inspector notes.
AI.result: Compared to image-only classification, the framework achieves improvements in accuracy (≈17.9%), balanced accuracy (≈12.2%), Macro F1 (≈23.0%), and MCC (≈17.3%). The approach yields competitive class-balanced performance with interpretable reasoning from CODE degrees to rule supports and severity evidence.
AI.conclusion: The neuro-symbolic pipeline successfully couples perceptual predictions with symbolic-rule-based reasoning to provide traceable evidence for sewer-pipe severity, reducing opacity while delivering better or comparable performance on imbalanced multi-class data.

title: APO: Unsupervised Atomic Policy Optimization for 3D Structure Prediction of Atomic Systems
summary: Predicting the 3D structures of atomic systems is fundamental to advancing material science and drug discovery. While flow-matching models (, FlowDPO) have recently shown promise in this domain, their performance relies heavily on alignment with ground-truth coordinates via supervised preference learning. However, obtaining experimental labels for novel crystal phases or de novo proteins is prohibitively expensive, creating a bottleneck for structural modeling in data-scarce regimes. In this work, we propose (Atomic Policy Optimization), a fully unsupervised alignment framework that eliminates the need for ground-truth reference structures. APO adapts group-relative policy optimization to 3D atomic environments, utilizing a novel dual-reward mechanism: (i) a that reinforces the policy's dominant latent structural modes through eigen-decomposition of sample similarities, and (ii) a that enforces thermodynamic stability. Our framework enables the model to ``self-correct'' by identifying physically plausible configurations within sampled groups. Extensive benchmarks on crystal and antibody structure prediction demonstrate that APO consistently outperforms fully supervised baselines, achieving a new state-of-the-art in match rates and structural fidelity. Furthermore, we show that APO effectively straightens probability paths, significantly improving inference efficiency. Our results suggest that intrinsic physical consistency can serve as a superior guide for alignment compared to noisy, supervised coordinate matching.

AI.tldr: Unsupervised alignment for 3D atomic structure prediction using Atomic Policy Optimization (APO) with dual rewards, achieving state-of-the-art match rates without ground-truth references.
AI.motivation: Ground-truth coordinates are expensive to obtain for novel crystal phases or de novo proteins; existing flow-matching approaches rely on supervised labels, creating a data-scarce bottleneck. An unsupervised alignment method guided by intrinsic physics could enable better generalization and efficiency.
AI.method: APO adapts group-relative policy optimization to 3D atomic environments. It employs a dual-reward mechanism: (i) an intrinsic reward from eigen-decomposition of sample similarities to reinforce dominant latent structural modes, and (ii) a thermodynamic-stability reward. The model self-corrects by identifying physically plausible configurations within sampled groups, leading to improved alignment without ground-truth coordinates.
AI.result: On crystal and antibody structure prediction benchmarks, APO consistently outperforms fully supervised baselines, achieving state-of-the-art match rates and higher structural fidelity. It also improves inference efficiency by straightening probability paths, suggesting intrinsic physical consistency as a strong guide for alignment versus noisy supervised matching.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic physical consistency can effectively guide alignment in 3D structure prediction, enabling high performance in data-scarce regimes without ground-truth references. APO's unsupervised framework potentially generalizes to other 3D structural tasks and could reshape how alignment is approached in structure prediction.

title: SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination
summary: Can supply-chain AI move beyond isolated decision modules toward unified operational planning? A complete replenishment plan specifies which products each location carries, which upstream facility supplies it, how often it is replenished, and how deliveries are routed. These decisions are operationally coupled: the selected assortment changes the demand and load passed to later stages; source assignment and replenishment frequency reshape the delivery requests; and route feasibility and cost, in turn, determine the system value of the earlier choices. Yet in modern supply chains, these decisions are often handled by separate departments and optimized through separate systems, which can lead to stockouts, inventory exposure, and avoidable transportation. We propose SCOPE: Supply-Chain Operations through Coupled Policies for End-to-End Coordination, a composite policy model that represents supply-chain entities as tokens, contextualizes them through a shared operational representation, and maps each token type to the corresponding decision interface. Each decision builds on the partial plan formed by earlier decisions while the completed plan is evaluated using a shared system-level utility. We instantiate this framework in urban fresh-retail replenishment, where service frequency, assortment, capacity pressure, and road-network routing interact strongly, and evaluate it on real operational data from Dingdong and JD.com, two large-scale supply chains operating at different replenishment echelons. Across both settings, SCOPE consistently outperforms methods that optimize each decision stage separately, as well as practice-oriented baselines commonly used in supply-chain operations. These results show that learning and coordinating cross-department operational couplings lead to more effective end-to-end supply-chain decisions.

AI.tldr: SCOPE introduces a unified, token-based, end-to-end policy framework for coordinated replenishment decisions in supply chains, yielding better performance than siloed optimization on real-world data.
AI.motivation: Operational couplings in replenishment (assortment, source, frequency, routing) create value only when optimized jointly; siloed decisions cause stockouts and inefficiencies.
AI.method: Proposes SCOPE: composite policy model with tokenized entities, a shared representation, and decision interfaces; sequentially builds a partial plan and evaluates with a shared utility; instantiated on urban fresh-retail replenishment; evaluated using real data from Dingdong and JD.com.
AI.result: SCOPE consistently outperforms stage-wise optimization and common baselines across two real-world settings, demonstrating the value of learning and coordinating cross-department couplings for end-to-end decisions.
AI.conclusion: End-to-end coupled policies can improve supply-chain performance; the approach provides a general framework applicable to other settings, pending further exploration of scalability and operational integration.

title: $β$-OPSD: Deriving with Policy Optimization, Training with Self-Distillation
